answers.explanation: Using an IAM user is generally not recommended for managing EC2 instances. IAM roles are preferred for this purpose. This approach also doesn't integrate well with the existing IAM role setup.

answers.text: Enable Default Host Configuration Management in Systems Manager to manage the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Enabling Default Host Configuration Management allows Systems Manager to automatically manage the EC2 instances with minimal configuration. It creates and applies a default IAM role, ensuring Systems Manager has the necessary permissions without disrupting the existing IAM role used for database access. This simplifies the process and is the best option to avoid disrupting applications.

answers.text: Remove the existing policies from the existing IAM role. Add the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy to the existing IAM role.
answers.explanation: Removing existing policies from the IAM role will disrupt the applications' access to the RDS databases. This directly contradicts the requirement to avoid disruption.

overall_explanation: Enabling Default Host Configuration Management in Systems Manager is the optimal solution. It allows Systems Manager to manage the instances without requiring manual IAM role creation or modification of the existing role, thus preventing any disruption to the applications' database access. The Default Host Management Configuration setting allows AWS Systems Manager to manage your Amazon EC2 instances automatically as managed instances.

question: A company runs container applications using Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) and the Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler. The workload fluctuates throughout the day. A solutions architect observes that the number of nodes doesn't automatically scale out when the existing nodes reach maximum capacity, leading to performance issues in the cluster. Which solution will resolve this issue with the LEAST administrative overhead?

answers.text: Scale out the nodes by tracking the memory usage.
answers.explanation: Scaling based solely on memory usage is insufficient. It doesn't address the core issue of automatic node scaling within the Kubernetes cluster.

answers.text: Use the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to manage the number of nodes in the cluster.
answers.explanation: The Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler automatically adjusts the number of nodes in the cluster based on resource demands. It integrates with Auto Scaling groups and requires minimal administrative overhead.

answers.text: Use an AWS Lambda function to resize the EKS cluster automatically.
answers.explanation: Using a Lambda function for resizing adds complexity and administrative overhead compared to the Cluster Autoscaler.

answers.text: Use an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to distribute the workload.
answers.explanation: While an Auto Scaling group is fundamental to the Cluster Autoscaler, it does not independently solve the issue of Kubernetes-aware node scaling.

overall_explanation: The Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler is the best solution. It monitors the Kubernetes scheduler for pending pods that can't be scheduled due to insufficient resources. The Autoscaler then automatically adjusts the size of the Auto Scaling group to accommodate the workload. This approach requires the least administrative overhead as it directly integrates with the Kubernetes cluster and automatically manages the scaling process. It handles the dynamic scaling needs of the EKS cluster without manual intervention. Alternatively consider Karpenter or EKS Managed Node Groups with autoscaling enabled. However, Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler is generally a better choice for least administrative overhead.

question: A company stores 300 TB of data in Amazon S3 Standard storage. The S3 objects, around 50 GB each, are frequently replaced using multipart uploads by a global application. Although the data volume and object size remain consistent, S3 storage costs are increasing. What strategy should a solutions architect employ to reduce these costs?

answers.text: Switch from multipart uploads to Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration.
answers.explanation: Switching to S3 Transfer Acceleration will not directly address increasing costs related to incomplete multipart uploads. It focuses on accelerating data transfers, not reducing storage overhead.

answers.text: Enable an S3 Lifecycle policy that deletes incomplete multipart uploads.
answers.explanation: This is the correct approach. Incomplete multipart uploads consume storage space without providing accessible objects. Configuring an S3 Lifecycle policy to automatically delete these incomplete uploads will reduce storage costs.

answers.text: Configure S3 inventory to prevent objects from being archived too quickly.
answers.explanation: S3 Inventory is used to manage and audit the replication and encryption status of your objects for business, compliance and regulatory needs. Configuring S3 inventory does not directly address costs associated with multipart uploads, archiving is not a concern in this scenario.

answers.text: Configure Amazon CloudFront to reduce the number of objects stored in Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a CDN and won't directly influence the number of objects stored in S3, so this will not help the cost increase caused by uncompleted multipart uploads.

overall_explanation: The increasing costs are most likely due to incomplete multipart uploads consuming storage without being finalized into complete objects. Enabling an S3 Lifecycle policy to automatically delete incomplete multipart uploads is the most effective solution to reduce these costs. S3 Transfer acceleration will improve upload speed but does not reduce storage cost. S3 Inventory and CloudFront will not help reduce cost associated with multipart uploads.

question: A company has deployed a multiplayer game for mobile devices that requires live location tracking of players based on latitude and longitude. The game uses an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance with read replicas to store the location data. During peak usage periods, the database struggles to maintain acceptable performance for reading and writing location updates, and the game's user base is growing rapidly. What should a solutions architect do to improve the performance of the data tier in this scenario?

answers.text: Take a snapshot of the existing DB instance. Restore the snapshot with Multi-AZ enabled.
answers.explanation: Enabling Multi-AZ improves availability but doesn't directly address performance bottlenecks related to rapid updates and retrieval.

answers.text: Migrate from Amazon RDS to Amazon OpenSearch Service with OpenSearch Dashboards.
answers.explanation: While OpenSearch is good for search and analytics, migrating the database might not be the best solution for rapid, transactional updates of location data.

answers.text: Deploy Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the existing DB instance. Modify the game to use DAX.
answers.explanation: DAX is specifically designed for DynamoDB. It does not work with Amazon RDS PostgreSQL instances. Thus, it is not a relevant solution in this case.

answers.text: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of the existing DB instance. Modify the game to use Redis.
answers.explanation: ElastiCache for Redis provides an in-memory data store with very low latency, suitable for caching frequently accessed data and handling high-volume read and write operations. Using Redis as a cache for location data can significantly improve the game's performance.

overall_explanation: ElastiCache for Redis offers a low-latency, in-memory caching solution that can improve read and write performance for location data updates. It is well-suited for high-volume, real-time applications like multiplayer games. While the existing database is PostgreSQL, ElastiCache can be added in front to serve as a fast cache for location data, which is more effective than other options like Multi-AZ or migrating the database entirely.

question: A company stores critical data in Amazon DynamoDB tables in the company's AWS account. An IT administrator accidentally deleted a DynamoDB table, causing a significant loss of data and disruption to the company's operations. The company wants to prevent this type of disruption in the future with the LEAST operational overhead. Which solution will meet this requirement?

answers.text: Configure a trail in AWS CloudTrail. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for delete actions. Create an AWS Lambda function to automatically restore deleted DynamoDB tables.
answers.explanation: This solution involves setting up several services (CloudTrail, EventBridge, Lambda), increasing operational overhead. It also assumes the automatic restoration is feasible and complete, which might not always be the case.

answers.text: Create a backup and restore plan for the DynamoDB tables. Recover the DynamoDB tables manually.
answers.explanation: While a good practice, this doesn't prevent accidental deletion. It only helps in recovery. Manual recovery also increases operational overhead during an incident.

answers.text: Configure deletion protection on the DynamoDB tables.
answers.explanation: Deletion protection directly prevents accidental deletion of DynamoDB tables. It's a simple, built-in feature that adds minimal operational overhead.

answers.text: Enable point-in-time recovery on the DynamoDB tables.
answers.explanation: Point-in-time recovery allows you to restore a table to a previous state but doesn't prevent accidental deletion. It's a recovery mechanism, not a preventative measure.

overall_explanation: Configuring deletion protection on the DynamoDB tables directly prevents accidental deletions with the least operational overhead. It is a built-in feature designed precisely for this purpose. Other options involve more complex setups or only focus on recovery after a deletion has already occurred. https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats- new/2023/03/amazon-dynamodb-table-deletion-protection/

question: A company has an on-premises data center that is running out of storage capacity. The company wants to migrate its storage infrastructure to AWS while minimizing bandwidth costs. The solution must allow for immediate retrieval of data at no additional cost. How can these requirements be met?

answers.text: Deploy Amazon S3 Glacier Vault and enable expedited retrieval. Enable provisioned retrieval capacity for the workload.
answers.explanation: S3 Glacier is designed for archival data and involves costs for expedited retrieval. It's not suitable for immediate retrieval at no additional cost.

answers.text: Deploy AWS Storage Gateway using cached volumes. Use Storage Gateway to store data in Amazon S3 while retaining copies of frequently accessed data subsets locally.
answers.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway in cached mode stores the primary data in S3, while frequently accessed data is cached on-premises for low-latency access. This minimizes the on-premises storage footprint and reduces bandwidth costs by only transferring frequently accessed data. It also allows for immediate retrieval of frequently accessed data.

answers.text: Deploy AWS Storage Gateway using stored volumes to store data locally. Use Storage Gateway to asynchronously back up point-in-time snapshots of the data to Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: While stored volumes offer low-latency access by storing all data locally, it doesn't address the on- premises storage capacity issue. Also, since they want to migrate to AWS, storing all data locally doesn't accomplish the migration goal.

answers.text: Deploy AWS Direct Connect to connect with the on-premises data center. Configure AWS Storage Gateway to store data locally. Use Storage Gateway to asynchronously back up point-in-time snapshots of the data to Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: AWS Direct Connect addresses network connectivity but doesn't directly address the storage capacity issue or minimize bandwidth costs related to immediate data retrieval. Storing all data locally defeats the purpose of migrating to AWS.

overall_explanation: AWS Storage Gateway using cached volumes is the most suitable solution. It minimizes on- premises storage, reduces bandwidth costs by caching only frequently accessed data locally, and enables immediate retrieval of frequently accessed data. Data is primarily stored in Amazon S3, aligning with the migration goal. Stored volumes do not address storage capacity issue and Glacier expedited retrieval comes with additional cost.

question: A company hosts a three-tier web application within a VPC across multiple Availability Zones. The application tier consists of Amazon EC2 instances managed by an Auto Scaling group. The company requires an automated scaling plan that analyzes the daily and weekly historical workload trends of each resource, ensuring appropriate scaling based on both forecasted demand and real-time utilization changes. Which scaling strategy should a solutions architect recommend to fulfill these requirements?

answers.text: Implement dynamic scaling with step scaling based on average CPU utilization from the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: This option only addresses dynamic scaling based on a single metric (CPU utilization) and does not incorporate historical trend analysis for forecasting.

answers.text: Enable predictive scaling to forecast and scale. Configure dynamic scaling with target tracking.
answers.explanation: This option combines predictive scaling, which analyzes historical trends, with dynamic scaling and target tracking, which responds to real-time utilization changes. This is the most appropriate choice.

answers.text: Create an automated scheduled scaling action based on the traffic patterns of the web application.
answers.explanation: Scheduled scaling is based on known, repeating patterns, but it does not dynamically adjust to unexpected changes in utilization or incorporate historical trend analysis.

answers.text: Set up a simple scaling policy. Increase the cooldown period based on the EC2 instance startup time.
answers.explanation: This option focuses on optimizing the cooldown period, not on implementing a scaling strategy based on both forecasting and real-time utilization.

overall_explanation: The most suitable solution is to enable predictive scaling, which forecasts future demand based on historical trends, and combine it with dynamic scaling using target tracking, which responds to real-time changes in resource utilization. This approach ensures that the application scales appropriately based on both predicted demand and current load.

question: A company recently launched Linux-based application instances on Amazon EC2 in a private subnet and launched a Linux-based bastion host on an Amazon EC2 instance in a public subnet of a VPC. A solutions architect needs to connect from the on-premises network, through the company's internet connection, to the bastion host, and to the application servers. The solutions architect must make sure that the security groups of all the EC2 instances will allow that access. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.text: Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the application instances.
answers.explanation: This option is incorrect because the bastion host needs to allow inbound connections from the on- premises network, not the application instances.

answers.text: Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the internal IP range for the company.
answers.explanation: This option is incorrect because the connection from on-premise to the Bastion host goes through the internet and will not be using the internal IP range.

answers.text: Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the external IP range for the company.
answers.explanation: This option is correct. This will restrict access to the bastion host from the specific IP range of the on-premises network, ensuring secure connectivity. It ensures that only authorized users from the on-premises network can access the bastion host.

answers.text: Replace the current security group of the application instances with one that allows inbound SSH access from only the private IP address of the bastion host.
answers.explanation: This option is correct. This step enables SSH connectivity from the bastion host to the application instances in the private subnet. By allowing inbound SSH access only from the private IP address of the bastion host, you ensure that SSH access is restricted to the bastion host only.

answers.text: Replace the current security group of the application instances with one that allows inbound SSH access from only the public IP address of the bastion host.
answers.explanation: This option is incorrect. Since the application instances are in a private subnet, allowing inbound SSH from the bastion host's public IP is not the ideal approach.

overall_explanation: The correct options are C and D. To connect from on-premises to the application instances via the bastion host, the bastion host's security group must allow inbound access from the company's external IP range (option C). The application instances' security group must allow inbound SSH access only from the bastion host's private IP address (option D), ensuring secure access within the VPC.

question: A package delivery company's application uses Amazon EC2 instances and an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. As the application gains popularity, EC2 instance usage increases slightly, but DB cluster usage increases at a much faster rate. The company added a read replica, which temporarily reduced DB cluster usage, but the load continues to grow. Repeated read statements related to delivery details are the primary cause of the increased DB cluster usage. The company needs to reduce the impact of these repeated reads on the DB cluster MOST cost-effectively. Which solution should the company implement?

answers.text: Implement an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster between the application and the DB cluster.
answers.explanation: ElastiCache for Redis can cache the results of repeated read queries, reducing the load on the Aurora DB cluster and improving performance. Caching is an efficient way to alleviate the pressure from repeated read operations, making it a cost-effective solution.

answers.text: Add an additional read replica to the DB cluster.
answers.explanation: While adding read replicas can distribute the read load, it does not address the underlying issue of repeated identical queries. It may temporarily reduce load but won't prevent the database from processing the same requests repeatedly, making it less cost-effective than caching.

answers.text: Configure Aurora Auto Scaling for the Aurora read replicas.
answers.explanation: Aurora Auto Scaling dynamically adjusts the number of read replicas based on load. While this can help with scaling, it doesn't prevent repeated identical read requests from reaching the database in the first place. Therefore, it is not as cost-effective as implementing a caching layer.

answers.text: Modify the DB cluster to have multiple writer instances.
answers.explanation: Aurora MySQL does not support multiple writer instances. Also, the problem described is read- heavy. Thus, adding writer instances would not solve the problem.

overall_explanation: The most cost-effective solution is to implement an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster. This approach caches the results of repeated read statements, reducing the load on the Aurora DB cluster. While read replicas can help, they don't prevent the database from processing the same repeated requests. Aurora Auto Scaling helps with scaling, but it doesn't address the repeated nature of the read requests like a caching solution does. Aurora MySQL does not support multiple writer instances.

question: A company's application uses an Amazon DynamoDB table. Many requests aren't returning the latest data, but other database performance metrics are normal. What design change should a solutions architect recommend?

answers.text: Add read replicas to the table.
answers.explanation: Adding read replicas won't solve data staleness issues. Read replicas typically improve read throughput but don't guarantee data consistency.

answers.text: Use a global secondary index (GSI).
answers.explanation: Using a GSI won't fix the inconsistency problem. GSIs are used to optimize query performance with different access patterns.

answers.text: Request strongly consistent reads for the table.
answers.explanation: DynamoDB defaults to eventual consistency, which means reads might not reflect the latest writes. Requesting strongly consistent reads ensures that the latest data is returned.

answers.text: Request eventually consistent reads for the table.
answers.explanation: The application is already using eventually consistent reads, which is the root cause of the problem.

overall_explanation: DynamoDB defaults to eventual consistency for read operations. To ensure that read operations return the latest data and address the issue of stale data being returned to users, the solutions architect should recommend switching the read consistency level from eventually consistent reads to strongly consistent reads.

question: A company has deployed its application on Amazon EC2 instances with an Amazon RDS database. The company used the principle of least privilege to configure the database access credentials. The company's security team wants to protect the application and the database from SQL injection and other web-based attacks with the LEAST operational overhead.

answers.text: Use security groups and network ACLs to secure the database and application servers.
answers.explanation: Security groups and network ACLs are helpful for network-level access control, but they don't directly protect against SQL injection and other web-based attacks.

answers.text: Use AWS WAF to protect the application. Use RDS parameter groups to configure the security settings.
answers.explanation: AWS WAF is a web application firewall that helps protect your web applications from common web exploits and bots. Parameter groups can help configure security settings for the database such as auditing.

answers.text: Use AWS Network Firewall to protect the application and the database.
answers.explanation: AWS Network Firewall is a network-level firewall service. While it offers protection, it is less specialized for web application attacks like SQL injection compared to WAF and might involve higher operational overhead for application-level protection.

answers.text: Use different database accounts in the application code for different functions. Avoid granting excessive privileges to the database users.
answers.explanation: While using different database accounts with least privilege is a good security practice, it doesn't prevent SQL injection attacks. It limits the impact if an attack is successful, but doesn't stop the attack itself.

overall_explanation: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) is specifically designed to protect web applications from attacks like SQL injection. Using AWS WAF provides the best protection against the specified attacks with the least operational overhead. RDS parameter groups can be used to configure database security settings. Network ACLs and security groups provide network-level security, while database user separation with least privilege is a general security best practice but neither directly address SQL injection attacks as effectively as WAF. Therefore, the correct answer is B.

question: An ecommerce company runs applications in AWS accounts that are part of an organization in AWS Organizations. The applications run on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL databases across all the accounts. The company needs to prevent malicious activity and must identify abnormal failed and incomplete login attempts to the databases. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

answers.text: Attach service control policies (SCPs) to the root of the organization to identity the failed login attempts.
answers.explanation: Attaching SCPs won't directly identify failed login attempts. SCPs control permissions and don't analyze login activity.

answers.text: Enable the Amazon RDS Protection feature in Amazon GuardDuty for the member accounts of the organization.
answers.explanation: GuardDuty's RDS Protection feature directly monitors RDS login activity, detects suspicious behavior, and is designed for this specific use case. It is operationally efficient because it's a managed service.

answers.text: Publish the Aurora general logs to a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Export the log data to a central Amazon S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: While this provides the logs, it requires significant manual effort to analyze the data and set up alerts, making it less operationally efficient.

answers.text: Publish all the Aurora PostgreSQL database events in AWS CloudTrail to a central Amazon S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: CloudTrail doesn't capture all the details of database login attempts. Additionally, analyzing the large volume of CloudTrail data for specific login attempts would be operationally complex.

overall_explanation: Amazon GuardDuty's RDS Protection feature continuously monitors RDS login activity and profiles it for suspicious activities like unauthorized access or unusual login patterns. It’s the most operationally efficient solution because it's a managed service specifically designed for threat detection in RDS environments. Options involving CloudWatch Logs or CloudTrail require extensive manual configuration and analysis, making them less efficient. SCPs are for permission control, not threat detection.

question: A company has an AWS Direct Connect connection from its corporate data center to its VPC in the us-east-1 Region. The company acquired another corporation with several VPCs and a Direct Connect connection between its on-premises data center and the eu-west-2 Region. The CIDR blocks for the VPCs of the company and the corporation do not overlap. The company requires connectivity between the two Regions and the data centers with a solution that is scalable and reduces operational overhead. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.text: Set up inter-Region VPC peering between the VPC in us-east-1 and the VPCs in eu- west-2.
answers.explanation: Inter-Region VPC peering does not natively extend to on-premises data centers through Direct Connect. This solution would not provide connectivity for on-premises resources.

answers.text: Create private virtual interfaces from the Direct Connect connection in us-east-1 to the VPCs in eu-west-2.
answers.explanation: Direct Connect virtual interfaces are region-specific. You cannot directly connect a virtual interface from one region's Direct Connect to VPCs in another region.

answers.text: Establish VPN appliances in a fully meshed VPN network hosted by Amazon EC2. Use AWS VPN CloudHub to send and receive data between the data centers and each VPC.
answers.explanation: While this option could work, it introduces operational overhead by requiring the management of EC2 instances and VPN appliances. It may also not be as scalable or cost-effective as other solutions.

answers.text: Connect the existing Direct Connect connections to a Direct Connect gateway. Route traffic from the virtual private gateways of the VPCs in each Region to the Direct Connect gateway.
answers.explanation: A Direct Connect gateway provides a global point for Direct Connect traffic. It allows connecting Direct Connect connections from different regions to VPCs in different regions through virtual private gateways (VGWs). This solution is scalable and reduces operational overhead.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to connect the existing Direct Connect connections to a Direct Connect gateway. By routing traffic from the virtual private gateways of the VPCs in each Region to the Direct Connect gateway, the company can achieve scalable inter-region connectivity with reduced operational overhead. A Direct Connect gateway acts as a central hub for routing traffic between VPCs in different regions through the Direct Connect connections, and it's designed for scenarios involving multiple regions and Direct Connect connections.

question: A mobile gaming company requires a solution to handle high traffic spikes and process score updates in order of receipt for a leaderboard. The processed updates must be stored in a highly available database with minimal operational overhead. Which architecture best meets these requirements?

answers.text: Push score updates to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Process the updates in Kinesis Data Streams with AWS Lambda. Store the processed updates in Amazon DynamoDB.
answers.explanation: This option satisfies all requirements: Kinesis Data Streams handles traffic spikes and ordered processing, Lambda provides serverless processing, and DynamoDB is a highly available, managed NoSQL database with minimal overhead.

answers.text: Push score updates to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Process the updates with a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances set up for Auto Scaling. Store the processed updates in Amazon Redshift.
answers.explanation: While Kinesis Data Streams handles traffic spikes and ordered processing, managing EC2 instances introduces operational overhead. Amazon Redshift is not designed for single record updates, which are required in this use case.

answers.text: Push score updates to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe an AWS Lambda function to the SNS topic to process the updates. Store the processed updates in a SQL database running on Amazon EC2.
answers.explanation: SNS does not guarantee message ordering. Using a SQL database on EC2 increases operational overhead compared to DynamoDB.

answers.text: Push score updates to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances with Auto Scaling to process the updates in the SQS queue. Store the processed updates in an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance.
answers.explanation: While SQS can handle traffic spikes, it does not inherently guarantee strict ordering. Using EC2 instances and RDS Multi-AZ for processing and storage introduces more operational overhead compared to using Lambda and DynamoDB.

overall_explanation: The optimal solution uses Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest and maintain the order of score updates, AWS Lambda for serverless processing, and Amazon DynamoDB for highly available data storage with minimal operational overhead. Other options either lack ordering guarantees, introduce unnecessary operational overhead with EC2 instances and managed relational databases, or are not suited for single record updates.

question: A company has multiple AWS accounts with applications deployed in the us-west-2 Region. Application logs are stored within Amazon S3 buckets in each account. The company wants to build a centralized log analysis solution that uses a single S3 bucket. Logs must not leave us- west-2, and the company wants to incur minimal operational overhead. Which solution meets these requirements and is MOST cost-effective?

answers.text: Create an S3 Lifecycle policy that copies the objects from one of the application S3 buckets to the centralized S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: S3 Lifecycle policies are primarily used for transitioning objects between storage classes, not for copying objects between buckets. This is not the most suitable approach for log aggregation.

answers.text: Use S3 Same-Region Replication to replicate logs from the S3 buckets to another S3 bucket in us-west-2. Use this S3 bucket for log analysis.
answers.explanation: S3 Same-Region Replication (SRR) is a cost-effective solution that automatically and asynchronously replicates objects between S3 buckets in the same AWS Region. It minimizes operational overhead and keeps the data within the us-west-2 Region.

answers.text: Write a script that uses the PutObject API operation every day to copy the entire contents of the buckets to another S3 bucket in us-west-2. Use this S3 bucket for log analysis.
answers.explanation: Writing a script to copy logs daily using the PutObject API introduces significant operational overhead for maintenance, error handling, and scheduling. It's less cost-effective than replication due to compute costs and manual effort.

answers.text: Write AWS Lambda functions in these accounts that are triggered every time logs are delivered to the S3 buckets (s3:ObjectCreated:* event). Copy the logs to another S3 bucket in us-west-2. Use this S3 bucket for log analysis.
answers.explanation: Using Lambda functions triggered by S3 events introduces operational overhead and potential complexity in managing the functions across multiple accounts. While this would work, SRR is a simpler and more cost-effective choice.

overall_explanation: S3 Same-Region Replication (SRR) provides an automated, cost-effective, and operationally efficient way to centralize logs from multiple S3 buckets into a single bucket within the same region (us-west-2). SRR minimizes operational overhead compared to scripting or Lambda functions. Lifecycle policies are not designed for cross-bucket data transfer.

question: A company delivers on-demand training videos to students globally, allowing authorized developers to upload content. Data is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket in us-east-2. The company has created S3 buckets in eu-west-2 and ap-southeast-1 and aims to replicate data to minimize latency for uploads near eu-west-2 and streaming near ap-southeast-1. Which combination of steps meets these requirements with the FEWEST application changes?

answers.text: Configure one-way replication from the us-east-2 S3 bucket to the eu-west-2 S3 bucket. Configure one-way replication from the us-east-2 S3 bucket to the ap- southeast-1 S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: This setup replicates data from the primary region (us-east-2) to the new regions, but doesn't necessarily optimize for uploads from the new regions or keep the buckets synchronized if uploads occur in multiple regions.

answers.text: Configure one-way replication from the us-east-2 S3 bucket to the eu-west-2 S3 bucket. Configure one-way replication from the eu-west-2 S3 bucket to the ap- southeast-1 S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: This creates a chain replication which may introduce latency issues as replication has to go through eu-west-2 before reaching ap-southeast-1. It doesn't efficiently handle uploads from ap-southeast- 1.

answers.text: Configure two-way (bidirectional) replication among the S3 buckets that are in all three Regions.
answers.explanation: Two-way replication ensures that any changes made in any of the three S3 buckets are reflected in the other two. This addresses the scenario where developers might be uploading videos from locations closer to the eu-west-2 or ap-southeast-1 regions.

answers.text: Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point. Modify the application to use the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Multi-Region Access Point for video streaming. Do not modify the application for video uploads.
answers.explanation: This option improves streaming latency by directing video requests to the nearest S3 bucket via the Multi-Region Access Point, but does not address optimizing upload latency.

answers.text: Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point. Modify the application to use the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Multi-Region Access Point for video streaming and uploads.
answers.explanation: Using a Multi-Region Access Point for both streaming and uploads allows the application to direct requests to the closest S3 bucket, minimizing latency for both operations.

overall_explanation: The best solution involves using an S3 Multi-Region Access Point for both streaming and uploads (Option E) and configuring two-way replication across all three S3 buckets (Option C). The Multi-Region Access Point ensures that users are directed to the nearest S3 bucket for both uploads and downloads, reducing latency. Two-way replication keeps all three S3 buckets synchronized, irrespective of where the initial upload occurs. This minimizes latency for both uploads and streaming with the fewest code changes to the application.

question: A company has developed a new mobile application that allows users worldwide to view local news based on their selected topics and upload photos and videos directly through the app. Content is frequently accessed in the initial minutes after posting, with newer content quickly superseding older content, leading to the eventual disappearance of the older content. Given the local nature of the news, 90% of the content consumption occurs within the AWS Region where it was uploaded. Which solution will optimize the user experience by providing the LOWEST latency for content uploads?

answers.text: Upload and store content in Amazon S3. Use Amazon CloudFront for the uploads.
answers.explanation: CloudFront is primarily designed for content delivery (reading) and caching, not for optimizing upload latency.

answers.text: Upload and store content in Amazon S3. Use S3 Transfer Acceleration for the uploads.
answers.explanation: Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration leverages CloudFront's globally distributed edge locations to accelerate content uploads to Amazon S3, providing the lowest latency.

answers.text: Upload content to Amazon EC2 instances in the Region that is closest to the user. Copy the data to Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: While this approach reduces latency for the initial upload, managing EC2 instances and then copying to S3 adds complexity and potential points of failure compared to S3 Transfer Acceleration.

answers.text: Upload and store content in Amazon S3 in the Region that is closest to the user. Use multiple distributions of Amazon CloudFront.
answers.explanation: While storing in the nearest S3 region is good, multiple CloudFront distributions are best for content delivery and do not directly optimize upload speed as effectively as S3 Transfer Acceleration.

overall_explanation: Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration offers the lowest latency for content uploads by utilizing Amazon CloudFront's edge locations. Users upload to the nearest CloudFront edge, and the data is then transferred to the S3 bucket in the designated region using optimized network paths. This is more efficient than standard S3 uploads or using CloudFront distributions alone for upload optimization. Therefore, using S3 Transfer Acceleration will result in the best user experience in terms of upload speed.

question: A company is developing a serverless application using an Amazon API Gateway REST API and AWS Lambda functions. The application needs to distribute messages received from the API Gateway to multiple target Lambda functions based on message content. The solution must filter messages to ensure each Lambda function receives only relevant data and minimize operational overhead. Which solution best meets these requirements?

answers.text: Send the requests from the API Gateway REST API to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues to the SNS topic. Configure the target Lambda functions to poll the different SQS queues.
answers.explanation: This option involves multiple services (SNS, SQS, and Lambda), increasing operational overhead. Lambda functions need to poll SQS queues, adding complexity.

answers.text: Send the requests from the API Gateway REST API to Amazon EventBridge. Configure EventBridge to invoke the target Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: EventBridge can directly invoke Lambda functions based on filtering rules, offering a simpler and more efficient solution with less operational overhead. EventBridge rules can filter messages based on content, attributes, or patterns.

answers.text: Send the requests from the API Gateway REST API to Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK). Configure Amazon MSK to publish the messages to the target Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: Amazon MSK is a complex streaming service that is not ideal for this use case. It introduces significant operational overhead compared to simpler solutions.

answers.text: Send the requests from the API Gateway REST API to multiple Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues. Configure the target Lambda functions to poll the different SQS queues.
answers.explanation: While this provides message distribution, it lacks built-in filtering capabilities. Each Lambda would still need to filter, increasing function complexity, and adds overhead in managing multiple SQS queues.

overall_explanation: EventBridge provides a direct and efficient way to route messages to Lambda functions based on filtering rules, minimizing operational overhead compared to using SNS with SQS or directly using SQS queues. MSK introduces unnecessary complexity. While EventBridge has a default limit of 5 targets per rule, multiple rules can be created to bypass this limit.

question: A solutions architect is designing a two-tier web application. The application consists of a public-facing web tier hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets. The database tier consists of Microsoft SQL Server running on Amazon EC2 in a private subnet. Security is a high priority for the company. How should security groups be configured to ensure secure communication while adhering to the principle of least privilege? (Choose two.)

answers.text: Configure the security group for the web tier to allow inbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0.
answers.explanation: This allows HTTPS traffic from any IPv4 address, enabling users to access the web application. While generally recommended to restrict the source IP range to a more specific range rather than allowing access from 0.0.0.0/0 (anywhere), it fulfills the requirement of public accessibility.

answers.text: Configure the security group for the web tier to allow outbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0.
answers.explanation: While outbound traffic is allowed by default for security groups, explicitly opening outbound traffic to all destinations is not the most secure approach. Security groups are stateful, so return traffic for established connections is automatically allowed.

answers.text: Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound traffic on port 1433 from the security group for the web tier.
answers.explanation: This allows the web tier EC2 instances to connect to the database tier on port 1433 (the default SQL Server port). By specifying the web tier's security group as the source, you restrict database access only to the web tier instances, enhancing security.

answers.text: Configure the security group for the database tier to allow outbound traffic on ports 443 and 1433 to the security group for the web tier.
answers.explanation: Opening outbound ports on the database tier to the web tier on ports 443 and 1433 is unnecessary and a security risk. The database only needs to respond to the web tier's connection requests. Since Security Groups are stateful, the response traffic is already permitted.

answers.text: Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound traffic on ports 443 and 1433 from the security group for the web tier.
answers.explanation: Allowing inbound traffic on port 443 to the database server isn't required, SQL Server communicates on port 1433, opening other ports increases the attack surface and are unnecessary.

overall_explanation: To ensure secure communication between the web tier and the database tier, the security group for the web tier should allow inbound HTTPS traffic (port 443) from the internet (0.0.0.0/0). This enables public access to the web application. The security group for the database tier should only allow inbound traffic on port 1433 (default SQL Server port) from the security group associated with the web tier. This restricts database access to only the web tier instances, significantly improving security. Outbound rules from the web tier aren't required as security groups are stateful, allowing return traffic from established connections.

question: A company migrated millions of archival files to Amazon S3. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that will encrypt all the archival data using a customer-provided key. The solution must encrypt existing unencrypted objects and future objects. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.text: Create a list of unencrypted objects by filtering an Amazon S3 Inventory report. Configure an S3 Batch Operations job to encrypt the objects from the list with server- side encryption with a customer-provided key (SSE-C). Configure the S3 default encryption feature to use server-side encryption with a customer-provided key (SSE-C).
answers.explanation: This option uses S3 Inventory to identify unencrypted objects and S3 Batch Operations to encrypt the existing unencrypted objects. S3 default encryption ensures future objects are encrypted using SSE-C.

answers.text: Use S3 Storage Lens metrics to identify unencrypted S3 buckets. Configure the S3 default encryption feature to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
answers.explanation: S3 Storage Lens metrics identify unencrypted buckets, not individual objects. This approach also doesn't address encrypting the existing unencrypted objects and uses SSE-KMS instead of SSE-C.

answers.text: Create a list of unencrypted objects by filtering the AWS usage report for Amazon S3. Configure an AWS Batch job to encrypt the objects from the list with server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Configure the S3 default encryption feature to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
answers.explanation: AWS usage reports do not provide details on the encryption status of individual objects. Also, the question specifies using a customer-provided key, so SSE-KMS is incorrect.

answers.text: Create a list of unencrypted objects by filtering the AWS usage report for Amazon S3. Configure the S3 default encryption feature to use a server-side encryption with a customer-provided key (SSE-C).
answers.explanation: AWS usage reports do not provide details on the encryption status of individual objects. Also, this option doesn't address encrypting the existing unencrypted objects.

overall_explanation: The correct solution is to use S3 Inventory to identify unencrypted objects because it has an 'Encryption status' field and then use S3 Batch Operations to encrypt those existing objects with a customer-provided key (SSE-C). Finally, enable default encryption for the bucket with SSE-C to ensure all new objects are encrypted with the customer-provided key. This ensures both existing and future objects are encrypted as per the requirements.

question: A company's website, hosted on AWS, is experiencing service disruptions due to outages at their current DNS provider. The company needs to quickly migrate to a more resilient managed DNS service on AWS. As a solutions architect, what is the MOST efficient way to migrate the DNS hosting service?

answers.text: Create an Amazon Route 53 public hosted zone for the domain name. Import the zone file containing the domain records hosted by the previous provider.
answers.explanation: This is the correct approach. A public hosted zone in Route 53 is designed for publicly accessible domains and importing the zone file allows for a rapid migration of existing DNS records.

answers.text: Create an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone for the domain name. Import the zone file containing the domain records hosted by the previous provider.
answers.explanation: A private hosted zone is used for internal DNS resolution within VPCs and would not make the website publicly accessible.

answers.text: Create a Simple AD directory in AWS. Enable zone transfer between the DNS provider and AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for the domain records.
answers.explanation: Simple AD is not designed for public DNS hosting and zone transfers from the current provider are unlikely to be supported.

answers.text: Create an Amazon Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint in the VPC. Specify the IP addresses that the provider's DNS will forward DNS queries to. Configure the provider's DNS to forward DNS queries for the domain to the IP addresses that are specified in the inbound endpoint.
answers.explanation: Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoints are used to resolve DNS queries originating from on-premises networks or other VPCs to resources within a VPC. This approach is unnecessarily complex for simply migrating public DNS records.

overall_explanation: The quickest and most appropriate solution is to create a public hosted zone in Amazon Route 53 and import the existing DNS records from the previous provider. This provides a resilient and managed DNS service on AWS for the company's public website. Private hosted zones are for internal DNS resolution and inbound resolvers are for on-premise DNS queries to AWS resources.

question: A company is developing an application on AWS that needs to connect to an Amazon RDS database. The company requires a solution to effectively manage the application configuration and securely store and retrieve database credentials, while minimizing administrative overhead.

answers.text: Use AWS AppConfig to store and manage the application configuration. Use AWS Secrets Manager to store and retrieve the credentials.
answers.explanation: AWS AppConfig is designed for managing application configurations, and AWS Secrets Manager is purpose-built for securely storing and retrieving secrets like database credentials. This combination provides a managed solution with minimal administrative overhead.

answers.text: Use AWS Lambda to store and manage the application configuration. Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to store and retrieve the credentials.
answers.explanation: Using Lambda to store application configuration is not its intended use and would require custom code and management overhead. While Parameter Store can store credentials, Secrets Manager is better suited and more secure for sensitive information.

answers.text: Use an encrypted application configuration file. Store the file in Amazon S3 for the application configuration. Create another S3 file to store and retrieve the credentials.
answers.explanation: While this solution is possible, managing encryption keys and access control for the S3 files adds significant administrative overhead compared to using managed services like AppConfig and Secrets Manager.

answers.text: Use AWS AppConfig to store and manage the application configuration. Use Amazon RDS to store and retrieve the credentials.
answers.explanation: Storing credentials directly in the RDS database is a security risk and is not a recommended practice. Secrets Manager is designed for secure credential storage and retrieval.

overall_explanation: The most efficient and secure solution is to use AWS AppConfig for application configuration management and AWS Secrets Manager for storing and retrieving database credentials. AppConfig provides a centralized and managed way to handle configurations, while Secrets Manager is specifically designed for secure credential management with features like rotation and access control. Options B, C, and D introduce unnecessary complexity and security risks compared to using these dedicated services.

question: A company needs to encrypt all of its application data in transit while communicating with an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance to meet security requirements. A recent security audit revealed that encryption at rest is enabled using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS), but data in transit is not enabled. What should a solutions architect do to satisfy the security requirements?

answers.text: Enable IAM database authentication on the database.
answers.explanation: While IAM database authentication provides benefits, including encrypted network traffic, it doesn't fully address the need for ensuring SSL/TLS encryption. Further configuration with root certificates is still needed.

answers.text: Provide self-signed certificates. Use the certificates in all connections to the RDS instance.
answers.explanation: Using self-signed certificates is not recommended for production environments, as they can lead to trust issues and are more difficult to manage. AWS provides root certificates that should be used instead.

answers.text: Take a snapshot of the RDS instance. Restore the snapshot to a new instance with encryption enabled.
answers.explanation: This action is not related to enabling in-transit encryption. It addresses encryption at rest, which is already configured.

answers.text: Download AWS-provided root certificates. Provide the certificates in all connections to the RDS instance.
answers.explanation: To encrypt data in transit to an RDS MySQL instance, you need to configure the database connection to use TLS/SSL, which requires using AWS-provided root certificates to establish a secure connection.

overall_explanation: To encrypt data in transit for an RDS MySQL instance, you need to configure TLS/SSL encryption on the database connections. This involves downloading the AWS-provided root certificates and configuring the clients to use them when connecting to the database. The RDS instance uses an AWS-provided certificate, so the application needs to be configured to trust that certificate.

question: A company is designing a new web service that will run on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) load balancer. Many of the web service clients can only reach IP addresses authorized on their firewalls. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet the clients’ needs?

answers.text: A Network Load Balancer with an associated Elastic IP address.
answers.explanation: A Network Load Balancer (NLB) supports assigning Elastic IP addresses. These static IP addresses can then be whitelisted by the clients on their firewalls, ensuring they can reach the web service.

answers.text: An Application Load Balancer with an associated Elastic IP address.
answers.explanation: Application Load Balancers (ALB) do not support direct assignment of Elastic IP addresses. This option would not allow clients to whitelist specific IPs.

answers.text: An A record in an Amazon Route 53 hosted zone pointing to an Elastic IP address.
answers.explanation: While Route 53 can use A records, this option doesn't directly address associating a static IP with the load balancer itself, which is what the clients need to whitelist. An A record pointing to an Elastic IP would require an EC2 instance to hold that Elastic IP.

answers.text: An EC2 instance with a public IP address running as a proxy in front of the load balancer.
answers.explanation: While this could work, it introduces unnecessary complexity and management overhead. It's better to leverage the NLB's native Elastic IP support. This also creates a single point of failure and scaling bottleneck.

overall_explanation: Using a Network Load Balancer with an associated Elastic IP address is the most suitable solution. NLBs are designed for high throughput and low latency, and their support for static IP addresses allows clients to easily whitelist the web service in their firewalls. Alternatives involve unnecessary complexity or don't directly solve the core problem.

question: A company has created a new AWS account. The account has the default settings and no changes have been made yet. The company is concerned about the security of the AWS account root user and wants to follow AWS best practices. What steps should the company take to enhance the security of the root user?

answers.text: Create IAM users for daily administrative tasks. Disable the root user.
answers.explanation: While creating IAM users for daily tasks is correct, disabling the root user is generally not recommended or fully possible. The root user is required for certain account-level tasks.

answers.text: Create IAM users for daily administrative tasks. Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) on the root user.
answers.explanation: This is the best option. Creating IAM users for day-to-day tasks limits the use of the root user. Enabling MFA on the root user provides an additional layer of security when the root user *must* be used.

answers.text: Generate an access key for the root user. Use the access key for daily administration tasks instead of the AWS Management Console.
answers.explanation: Generating an access key for the root user and using it for daily tasks is a security risk and defeats the purpose of using IAM roles and users for granular permissions.

answers.text: Provide the root user credentials to the most senior solutions architect. Have the solutions architect use the root user for daily administration tasks.
answers.explanation: Sharing root user credentials and using them for daily administration tasks is a major security risk and violates the principle of least privilege.

overall_explanation: The best practice is to create IAM users for daily tasks to avoid using the root user. Enabling Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) on the root user's account is crucial as an additional layer of security when the root user *must* be used for specific tasks. The root user should not be used for regular administration. Segregation of duties dictates that root access must never be used for routine activities.

question: A company is deploying an application that processes streaming data in near-real time using Amazon EC2 instances. The network architecture must be configured to minimize latency between nodes. Which combination of network solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.text: Enable and configure enhanced networking on each EC2 instance.
answers.explanation: Enhanced networking provides higher bandwidth, higher packet per second (PPS) performance, and consistently lower inter-instance latencies.

answers.text: Group the EC2 instances in separate accounts.
answers.explanation: Grouping instances in separate accounts does not directly impact latency between nodes.

answers.text: Run the EC2 instances in a cluster placement group.
answers.explanation: A cluster placement group is a logical grouping of instances within a single Availability Zone. This configuration is recommended for applications that need low network latency, high network throughput, or both. Cluster placement groups place instances close together physically, which reduces latency.

answers.text: Attach multiple elastic network interfaces to each EC2 instance.
answers.explanation: Attaching multiple ENIs primarily increases network bandwidth, not necessarily reduces latency.

answers.text: Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) optimized instance types.
answers.explanation: EBS-optimized instances improve throughput to EBS but do not directly reduce latency between instances.

overall_explanation: To achieve the lowest possible latency between EC2 instances, you should enable enhanced networking and run the instances in a cluster placement group. Enhanced networking provides better performance and lower latency, while a cluster placement group ensures the instances are physically located close together, minimizing network hops and latency.

question: A financial services company needs to migrate over 100 TB of data from two on-premises data centers to AWS as part of a datacenter shutdown project. The existing data is unstructured, stored in an intricate directory structure with millions of small files, and uses SMB-based storage from various vendors. The company wants to minimize operational overhead and avoid application changes after the migration. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.text: Use AWS Direct Connect to migrate the data to Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: While AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated network connection, migrating directly to S3 might require application changes to access the data and could be complex given the existing SMB structure.

answers.text: Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon FSx for Lustre.
answers.explanation: Amazon FSx for Lustre is designed for high-performance computing and isn't the best fit for SMB- based storage and unstructured data. It does not natively support SMB file shares.

answers.text: Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.
answers.explanation: AWS DataSync simplifies and accelerates data transfer between on-premises storage and AWS. FSx for Windows File Server supports SMB and preserves file system metadata, requiring minimal application changes. This option offers the least operational overhead.

answers.text: Use AWS Direct Connect to migrate the data on-premises file storage to an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway.
answers.explanation: While AWS Storage Gateway supports SMB and allows on-premises applications to access AWS storage, it introduces additional complexity and doesn't directly address the data migration and operational overhead concerns as effectively as DataSync.

overall_explanation: AWS DataSync is a data transfer service that simplifies, automates, and accelerates moving and replicating data between on-premises storage systems and AWS storage services. Given the company's desire to maintain SMB compatibility and minimize application changes, migrating the data using AWS DataSync to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server would be the most efficient and least operationally intensive solution. FSx for Windows File Server supports SMB and allows preserving file system metadata during the migration.

question: A company uses an organization in AWS Organizations to manage AWS accounts that contain applications. The company sets up a dedicated monitoring member account in the organization. The company wants to query and visualize observability data across the accounts by using Amazon CloudWatch. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.text: Enable CloudWatch cross-account observability for the monitoring account. Deploy an AWS CloudFormation template provided by the monitoring account in each AWS account to share the data with the monitoring account.
answers.explanation: CloudWatch cross-account observability allows you to query and visualize data from multiple AWS accounts in a single monitoring account. Deploying the CloudFormation template establishes the necessary trust and permissions for data sharing.

answers.text: Set up service control policies (SCPs) to provide access to CloudWatch in the monitoring account under the Organizations root organizational unit (OU).
answers.explanation: SCPs control the maximum permissions available in member accounts. While they can restrict access, they do not inherently enable cross-account data querying and visualization.

answers.text: Configure a new IAM user in the monitoring account. In each AWS account, configure an IAM policy to have access to query and visualize the CloudWatch data in the account. Attach the new IAM policy to the new IAM user.
answers.explanation: This approach requires manual configuration of IAM policies in each account and is less scalable and manageable than using CloudWatch cross-account observability.

answers.text: Create a new IAM user in the monitoring account. Create cross-account IAM policies in each AWS account. Attach the IAM policies to the new IAM user.
answers.explanation: This approach is similar to Option C and also involves manual configuration of IAM policies in each account, making it less efficient than CloudWatch cross-account observability.

overall_explanation: CloudWatch cross-account observability is the most efficient and scalable solution for querying and visualizing data across multiple AWS accounts. It simplifies the process of data sharing and reduces the manual configuration required. Option A provides the correct configuration to setup CloudWatch cross-account observability.

question: A company website sells products and runs on EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). An Amazon CloudFront distribution is used for caching, and AWS WAF protects against SQL injection. The ALB is the CloudFront origin. Security logs reveal a malicious external IP that needs to be blocked. What should a solutions architect do to protect the application?

answers.text: Modify the network ACL on the CloudFront distribution to add a deny rule for the malicious IP address.
answers.explanation: Network ACLs operate at the subnet level and are not the appropriate tool for blocking specific IPs at the application layer in front of CloudFront.

answers.text: Modify the configuration of AWS WAF to add an IP match condition to block the malicious IP address.
answers.explanation: AWS WAF is designed to protect web applications from common exploits and can be configured to block specific IP addresses using IP match conditions.

answers.text: Modify the network ACL for the EC2 instances in the target groups behind the ALB to deny the malicious IP address.
answers.explanation: Network ACLs operate at the subnet level. While they can block traffic, it is better to block the malicious traffic closer to the edge using WAF, preventing the traffic from reaching the ALB and EC2 instances.

answers.text: Modify the security groups for the EC2 instances in the target groups behind the ALB to deny the malicious IP address.
answers.explanation: Security Groups are stateful and only support allow rules, not deny rules. Therefore, you cannot block traffic using security groups.

overall_explanation: The best approach is to use AWS WAF to block the malicious IP address. WAF is designed for this purpose and allows you to quickly and effectively block unwanted traffic at the application layer before it reaches your backend infrastructure. Modifying network ACLs is not as effective because it operates at a lower level (subnet) and doesn't provide the same level of application-specific filtering. Security groups can only allow traffic, not block it.

question: A company is migrating a multi-tiered application from its on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud with the goal of enhancing application performance and modernizing its architecture. The application tiers communicate using RESTful services. Currently, the application experiences transaction drops when a tier becomes overloaded. As a solutions architect, you must design a solution that addresses these issues while ensuring operational efficiency. Which solution is the MOST suitable?

answers.text: Use Amazon API Gateway to route transactions to AWS Lambda functions for the application layer. Implement Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) as the communication layer between application services.
answers.explanation: This solution leverages serverless architecture with Lambda for auto-scaling and SQS for decoupling, addressing both performance and modernization requirements. API Gateway handles RESTful service requests efficiently. This option is operationally efficient as it reduces the need for managing servers.

answers.text: Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to analyze application performance history to identify peak utilization of servers during performance failures. Increase the size of the application server's Amazon EC2 instances to accommodate peak requirements.
answers.explanation: While this may address performance issues, it doesn't modernize the application or improve operational efficiency. Scaling up EC2 instances might be costly and doesn't inherently address dropped transactions due to overloading.

answers.text: Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to manage messaging between application servers running on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the SNS queue length and scale up and down as required.
answers.explanation: SNS is primarily for pub/sub messaging, not for queuing and guaranteed delivery needed to prevent transaction drops. While Auto Scaling helps, it doesn't modernize the application and is less operationally efficient than serverless options.

answers.text: Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to handle the messaging between application servers running on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the SQS queue length and scale up when communication failures are detected.
answers.explanation: This solution uses EC2 instances, which is not modernizing the application, and also scales based on communication failures which is a reactive approach. This is less operationally efficient than Option A with API Gateway and Lambda.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to use Amazon API Gateway to route transactions to AWS Lambda functions, with Amazon SQS managing communication between application services. This approach modernizes the application using serverless technology (Lambda), improves performance with auto-scaling, and prevents transaction drops by decoupling the tiers with SQS. It is also the most operationally efficient, as it minimizes server management overhead.

question: A company has an AWS Organizations setup with 10 accounts. They need to grant access to these accounts for thousands of employees, using their existing on-premises identity provider (IdP) for authentication. What is the MOST suitable AWS service that allows the company to federate access from their existing IdP to these AWS accounts?

answers.text: Create IAM users for all employees in each AWS account, connect these IAM users to the existing IdP, and configure federated authentication.
answers.explanation: Creating IAM users in each account is not scalable for thousands of users and increases management overhead. Connecting IAM users to the IdP directly is complex to configure and manage.

answers.text: Set up AWS account root users with user email addresses and passwords synchronized from the existing IdP.
answers.explanation: Using the root user is a security risk and not recommended for day-to-day access. Synchronizing credentials is also a complex task and does not align with best practices.

answers.text: Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On). Connect IAM Identity Center to the existing IdP. Provision users and groups from the IdP.
answers.explanation: IAM Identity Center simplifies user management and provides centralized access control across multiple AWS accounts. It allows easy integration with existing IdPs and supports user and group provisioning, making it the most suitable choice for this scenario.

answers.text: Use AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) to share access to the AWS accounts with users from the existing IdP.
answers.explanation: AWS RAM is primarily used for sharing resources within your AWS organization or with other AWS accounts, not for federating identities from an external IdP.

overall_explanation: IAM Identity Center is the MOST suitable solution because it allows centralized management of users and permissions across multiple AWS accounts, seamlessly integrates with existing identity providers (IdPs), and simplifies the process of provisioning users and groups. IAM Identity Center redirects authentication to the existing IdP and grants access based on policies created in IAM Identity Center. Option A is not scalable. Option B is a security risk and not recommended. Option D is incorrect as AWS RAM is used to share resources and not for federating identities.

question: A solutions architect is designing an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) authorization model for a company's AWS account. The company has designated five specific employees to have full access to AWS services and resources in the AWS account. The solutions architect has created an IAM user for each of the five designated employees and has created an IAM user group. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.text: Attach the AdministratorAccess resource-based policy to the IAM user group. Place each of the five designated employee IAM users in the IAM user group.
answers.explanation: Resource-based policies are attached to resources, not IAM user groups. Therefore, this option is incorrect.

answers.text: Attach the SystemAdministrator identity-based policy to the IAM user group. Place each of the five designated employee IAM users in the IAM user group.
answers.explanation: The SystemAdministrator policy provides limited access compared to AdministratorAccess. The requirement is to provide full access.

answers.text: Attach the AdministratorAccess identity-based policy to the IAM user group. Place each of the five designated employee IAM users in the IAM user group.
answers.explanation: The AdministratorAccess policy grants full access to AWS services and resources. This policy attached to an IAM group containing the users will fulfill the requirement.

answers.text: Attach the SystemAdministrator resource-based policy to the IAM user group. Place each of the five designated employee IAM users in the IAM user group.
answers.explanation: Resource-based policies are attached to resources, not IAM user groups. Additionally, SystemAdministrator policy does not grant full access.

overall_explanation: To provide full access to the five designated employees, the solutions architect should attach the AdministratorAccess identity-based policy to the IAM user group and place each of the five employee IAM users in the IAM user group. Identity-based policies are attached to IAM identities (users, groups, roles), while resource-based policies are attached to AWS resources. AdministratorAccess provides full access, whereas SystemAdministrator offers limited privileges.

question: A company's multi-tier payment processing application currently uses virtual machines (VMs). Communication between tiers is asynchronous via a third-party middleware guaranteeing exactly-once delivery. The company wants to migrate to a solution requiring the least infrastructure management while maintaining exactly-once delivery for application messaging. Which combination of actions achieves these goals? (Choose two.)

answers.text: Use AWS Lambda for the compute layers in the architecture.
answers.explanation: AWS Lambda offers a serverless compute environment, minimizing infrastructure management. It automatically scales and manages the underlying resources, reducing operational overhead.

answers.text: Use Amazon EC2 instances for the compute layers in the architecture.
answers.explanation: EC2 instances require manual management of the operating system, patching, scaling, and other infrastructure-related tasks, which does not meet the requirement for least infrastructure management.

answers.text: Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) as the messaging component between the compute layers.
answers.explanation: Amazon SNS provides a pub/sub messaging service but does not guarantee exactly-once delivery. It's possible for messages to be lost or delivered multiple times.

answers.text: Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues as the messaging component between the compute layers.
answers.explanation: Amazon SQS FIFO (First-In-First-Out) queues provide exactly-once processing and message ordering. This ensures each message is delivered exactly once and in the order it was sent, fulfilling the application's requirement.

answers.text: Use containers that are based on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) for the compute layers in the architecture.
answers.explanation: Amazon EKS, while offering container orchestration, requires more infrastructure management compared to Lambda. Managing the Kubernetes cluster, nodes, and networking adds complexity and operational overhead.

overall_explanation: Using AWS Lambda for compute provides serverless operation, reducing management overhead. Amazon SQS FIFO queues ensure exactly-once message delivery, fulfilling the requirement. SNS doesn't provide exactly-once delivery, and EC2/EKS require more infrastructure management than Lambda.

question: A company has a nightly batch processing routine that analyzes report files that an on- premises file system receives daily through SFTP. The company wants to move the solution to the AWS Cloud. The solution must be highly available and resilient. The solution also must minimize operational effort. Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.text: Deploy AWS Transfer for SFTP and an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system for storage. Use an Amazon EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group with a scheduled scaling policy to run the batch operation.
answers.explanation: This option uses AWS Transfer for SFTP for a managed and highly available SFTP service and EFS for a shared, scalable file system. Using an EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group with a scheduled scaling policy addresses high availability and resilience while also automating the batch processing.

answers.text: Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance that runs Linux and an SFTP service. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for storage. Use an Auto Scaling group with the minimum number of instances and desired number of instances set to 1.
answers.explanation: This option requires more operational effort because the company must manage the SFTP server on the EC2 instance. Also, EBS is not ideal for sharing data across multiple instances for high availability. Setting the desired number of instances to 1 negates the Auto Scaling benefits.

answers.text: Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance that runs Linux and an SFTP service. Use an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system for storage. Use an Auto Scaling group with the minimum number of instances and desired number of instances set to 1.
answers.explanation: This option requires more operational effort because the company must manage the SFTP server on the EC2 instance. Setting the desired number of instances to 1 negates the Auto Scaling benefits.

answers.text: Deploy AWS Transfer for SFTP and an Amazon S3 bucket for storage. Modify the application to pull the batch files from Amazon S3 to an Amazon EC2 instance for processing. Use an EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group with a scheduled scaling policy to run the batch operation.
answers.explanation: While this option leverages managed services and Auto Scaling, it requires modifying the application to pull files from S3, which increases the operational effort. EFS support directly by Transfer Family reduces the complexity.

overall_explanation: Option A is the most suitable solution. It utilizes AWS Transfer for SFTP to provide a highly available and resilient SFTP service, and Amazon EFS for a shared, scalable file system. The use of an EC2 instance within an Auto Scaling group, configured with a scheduled scaling policy, ensures both high availability and resilience for the batch processing. This setup also minimizes operational overhead by leveraging managed services and automation, aligning with the requirement to minimize operational effort.

question: A company has users all around the world accessing its HTTP-based application deployed on Amazon EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions. The company wants to improve the availability and performance of the application.
