answers.explanation: If the development instance is replaced, its public IP address might change, requiring manual DNS updates in Route 53. This solution does not provide automatic routing after instance replacement.

answers.text: Create an A Record for the development website with the value set to the ALB. Create a listener rule on the ALB to redirect requests for the development website to the public IP address of the development instance.
answers.explanation: ALB listener rules are not intended to directly redirect traffic to the public IP addresses of EC2 instances. Redirecting to a public IP bypasses the benefits of using a target group for health checks and automated replacement.

answers.text: Place all instances in the same target group. Create an A Record for the development website. Set the value to the ALB. Create a listener rule on the ALB that forwards requests for the development website to the target group.
answers.explanation: Placing all instances in the same target group does not isolate the development instance. Requests intended for the development website might be incorrectly routed to production instances, and it will be difficult to isolate the Dev Environment.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to create an A Record pointing to the ALB and create a listener rule on the ALB to forward requests for the development website to the target group containing the development instance. This setup ensures that traffic is correctly routed to the development instance and that routing is automatically updated when the instance is replaced.

question: A company runs a container application on a Kubernetes cluster in the company's data center. The application uses Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP) to communicate with a message queue. The data center cannot scale fast enough to meet the company’s expanding business needs. The company wants to migrate the workloads to AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.text: Migrate the container application to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to retrieve the messages.
answers.explanation: While ECS is a good container orchestration service and SQS is a managed queueing service, SQS does not support the AMQP protocol. Therefore, this option requires application code changes.

answers.text: Migrate the container application to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Use Amazon MQ to retrieve the messages.
answers.explanation: This option allows the company to use a familiar container orchestration platform (Kubernetes) via EKS. Amazon MQ provides compatibility with AMQP, minimizing code changes and operational overhead.

answers.text: Use highly available Amazon EC2 instances to run the application. Use Amazon MQ to retrieve the messages.
answers.explanation: While this solution works, it requires more manual configuration and management of EC2 instances, increasing operational overhead compared to a managed container service.

answers.text: Use AWS Lambda functions to run the application. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to retrieve the messages.
answers.explanation: This option would likely require a significant rewrite of the container application to fit the Lambda execution model. Additionally, SQS doesn't support AMQP, adding further complexity.

overall_explanation: The best option is to migrate the application to Amazon EKS and use Amazon MQ. EKS allows the company to continue using Kubernetes, and Amazon MQ provides compatibility with the AMQP protocol, which is required by the application. This approach minimizes code changes and operational overhead. While ECS + SQS offers less overhead in general, the lack of AMQP support in SQS makes it unsuitable. Using EC2 directly increases operational overhead compared to managed services. Lambda introduces significant application rewrite requirements and doesn't address AMQP.

question: An online gaming company hosts its platform on Amazon EC2 instances behind Network Load Balancers (NLBs) across multiple AWS Regions. The NLBs can route requests to targets over the internet. The company wants to improve the customer playing experience by reducing end-to- end load time for its global customer base. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.text: Create Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in each Region to replace the existing NLBs. Register the existing EC2 instances as targets for the ALBs in each Region.
answers.explanation: ALBs are typically used for HTTP/HTTPS traffic and don't provide the same level of performance improvement for gaming traffic as Global Accelerator. Also, this option involves significant changes to the existing infrastructure.

answers.text: Configure Amazon Route 53 to route equally weighted traffic to the NLBs in each Region.
answers.explanation: Equally weighted traffic distribution does not optimize for latency and proximity to the user. It will not significantly reduce end-to-end load time for the global customer base.

answers.text: Create additional NLBs and EC2 instances in other Regions where the company has large customer bases.
answers.explanation: While this can help, it doesn't guarantee optimal routing and requires more infrastructure management. It also doesn't address the inherent latency of internet routing.

answers.text: Create a standard accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Configure the existing NLBs as target endpoints.
answers.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator uses the AWS global network to direct traffic to the closest healthy endpoint, minimizing latency and improving the user experience for a global customer base. Because the infrastructure currently uses NLBs, Global Accelerator is an optimal solution.

overall_explanation: AWS Global Accelerator is designed to improve the performance of applications by directing traffic to the optimal endpoint based on user location and network conditions. By creating a standard accelerator and configuring the existing NLBs as target endpoints, the gaming company can leverage the AWS global network to reduce latency and improve the playing experience for its global customer base. Option A would be better if it implemented Cloudfront as well, but it doesn't. Route 53 routing doesn't optimize for latency. Creating additional NLBs does not guarantee optimal routing. Therefore, option D is the best answer.

question: A company is migrating to the AWS Cloud. Currently, an on-premises application uses SFTP to collect financial data from multiple vendors. The company has created a new cloud application that utilizes Amazon S3 APIs for file uploads from vendors. However, some vendors use legacy applications that do not support S3 APIs and want to continue using SFTP. The company wants to use managed services to accommodate these vendors with minimal operational overhead. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.text: Create an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) instance to replicate data from the storage of the vendors that use legacy applications to Amazon S3. Provide the vendors with the credentials to access the AWS DMS instance.
answers.explanation: AWS DMS is designed for database migrations, not file-based SFTP uploads.

answers.text: Create an AWS Transfer Family endpoint for vendors that use legacy applications.
answers.explanation: AWS Transfer Family is a fully managed service that directly supports SFTP, FTPS, and FTP protocols, providing a managed SFTP endpoint for vendors to upload data directly to Amazon S3, minimizing operational overhead.

answers.text: Configure an Amazon EC2 instance to run an SFTP server. Instruct the vendors that use legacy applications to use the SFTP server to upload data.
answers.explanation: This solution requires managing and maintaining an EC2 instance, increasing operational overhead.

answers.text: Configure an Amazon S3 File Gateway for vendors that use legacy applications to upload files to an SMB file share.
answers.explanation: S3 File Gateway supports SMB and NFS, not SFTP.

overall_explanation: AWS Transfer Family is a fully managed service that allows you to set up SFTP endpoints for accessing Amazon S3 storage. By creating an AWS Transfer Family endpoint, the company can provide vendors with a familiar SFTP interface to upload data directly to Amazon S3 without requiring changes to their legacy applications. This eliminates the need for the company to manage additional infrastructure such as EC2 instances or file gateways, reducing operational overhead.

question: A marketing team is preparing a campaign for an upcoming multi-sport event. They possess a collection of news reports in PDF format spanning the past five years. The team needs a solution to extract key insights and analyze the sentiment expressed within these news reports. The solution must leverage Amazon Textract to process the PDF documents. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.text: Provide the extracted insights to Amazon Athena for analysis. Store the extracted insights and analysis in an Amazon S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Using Athena would require creating and managing tables and queries, increasing operational overhead. It's also not ideally suited for sentiment analysis.

answers.text: Store the extracted insights in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use Amazon SageMaker to build a sentiment model.
answers.explanation: Building and managing a SageMaker sentiment model introduces significant operational complexity and overhead. DynamoDB is also not optimized for this type of analytical workload.

answers.text: Provide the extracted insights to Amazon Comprehend for analysis. Save the analysis to an Amazon S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Amazon Comprehend provides built-in sentiment analysis capabilities with minimal operational overhead. It integrates well with Textract and S3, providing a streamlined solution.

answers.text: Store the extracted insights in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize and analyze the data.
answers.explanation: QuickSight is primarily for visualization and requires additional steps to perform sentiment analysis, increasing operational overhead. It also does not provide built in sentiment analysis.

overall_explanation: The most efficient solution involves using Amazon Textract to extract text from the news reports and then leveraging Amazon Comprehend's built-in sentiment analysis capabilities. The results can then be stored in an S3 bucket. This approach minimizes operational overhead by utilizing managed services specifically designed for these tasks.

question: A company's application runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are in multiple Availability Zones. The application needs to ingest real-time data from third-party applications. The company needs a data ingestion solution that places the ingested raw data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.text: Create Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for data ingestion. Create Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams to consume the Kinesis Data Streams. Specify the S3 bucket as the destination of the delivery streams.
answers.explanation: This solution utilizes Kinesis Data Streams for real-time data ingestion, and Kinesis Data Firehose for delivering the data to an S3 bucket. This fulfills the requirements of real-time ingestion and S3 storage.

answers.text: Create database migration tasks in AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Specify replication instances of the EC2 instances as the source endpoints. Specify the S3 bucket as the target endpoint. Set the migration type to migrate existing data and replicate ongoing changes.
answers.explanation: AWS DMS is primarily for database migrations, not real-time data ingestion from applications. It's not suitable for handling the real-time data ingestion requirement.

answers.text: Create and configure AWS DataSync agents on the EC2 instances. Configure DataSync tasks to transfer data from the EC2 instances to the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: AWS DataSync is designed for periodic data transfers, not real-time ingestion. It's not suitable for handling the real-time data ingestion requirement.

answers.text: Create an AWS Direct Connect connection to the application for data ingestion. Create Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams to consume direct PUT operations from the application. Specify the S3 bucket as the destination of the delivery streams.
answers.explanation: AWS Direct Connect is about creating dedicated network connections; it doesn't inherently solve the data ingestion problem itself. Also, Kinesis Firehose is generally used for ingestion from Kinesis Streams, not directly from applications via PUT operations.

overall_explanation: Kinesis Data Streams and Kinesis Data Firehose is the most suitable solution for ingesting real-time data from third-party applications and storing it in an S3 bucket. Kinesis Data Streams handles the real-time ingestion, while Kinesis Data Firehose efficiently delivers the data to the specified S3 destination.

question: A company’s application receives data from multiple sources, with data sizes varying up to 700 KB and expected to increase. The company has chosen Amazon DynamoDB as its primary database. A solutions architect needs a solution that handles these potentially large data sizes operationally efficiently. Which of the following approaches is the MOST operationally efficient for storing data exceeding DynamoDB's item size limits?

answers.text: Create an AWS Lambda function to filter data exceeding DynamoDB item size limits and store the larger data in an Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) database.
answers.explanation: Using DocumentDB introduces another database technology into the stack, increasing operational complexity and management overhead. Filtering data might lead to data loss.

answers.text: Store the large data as objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. In a DynamoDB table, create an item with an attribute pointing to the S3 URL of the data.
answers.explanation: This approach decouples large data storage from DynamoDB, leveraging S3's scalability and cost- effectiveness for large objects. DynamoDB stores metadata and pointers to the actual data.

answers.text: Split all incoming large data into a collection of items that share the same partition key. Write the data to a DynamoDB table in a single operation using the BatchWriteItem API operation.
answers.explanation: Splitting data into multiple items adds complexity to both writing and reading the data, and BatchWriteItem has its own limitations.

answers.text: Create an AWS Lambda function that uses gzip compression to compress large objects as they are written to a DynamoDB table.
answers.explanation: Compression reduces size, but doesn't guarantee the data will fit within the DynamoDB's 400 KB limit, especially with increasing data sizes. Also, compression and decompression add computational overhead.

overall_explanation: Storing large data in Amazon S3 and referencing it with a URL in DynamoDB offers the most operationally efficient solution. It leverages S3's ability to store large objects cost- effectively, while DynamoDB manages metadata and pointers to the S3 objects. This approach avoids the complexities of using another database or splitting data into multiple DynamoDB items and is in line with AWS recommended practices. Compression may help, but it's not guaranteed to keep the data under the DynamoDB size limit as data sizes grow.

question: A company hosts its web applications in the AWS Cloud. The company configures Elastic Load Balancers to use certificates that are imported into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). The company's security team must be notified 30 days before the expiration of each certificate. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

answers.text: Add a rule in ACM to publish a custom message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic every day, beginning 30 days before any certificate will expire.
answers.explanation: ACM does not directly support custom rules for sending notifications directly to SNS based on specific conditions like certificate expiration. EventBridge is the mechanism for ACM notifications.

answers.text: Create an AWS Config rule that checks for certificates that will expire within 30 days. Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to invoke a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) when AWS Config reports a noncompliant resource.
answers.explanation: AWS Config can check for expiring certificates using the `acm-certificate-expiration-check` managed rule. When a certificate is found to be non-compliant (expiring within the specified timeframe), EventBridge can trigger an SNS notification.

answers.text: Use AWS Trusted Advisor to check for certificates that will expire within 30 days. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is based on Trusted Advisor metrics for check status changes. Configure the alarm to send a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
answers.explanation: Trusted Advisor does not monitor certificate expiration and is not the appropriate tool for this task.

answers.text: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to detect any certificates that will expire within 30 days. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to send a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
answers.explanation: While EventBridge can detect certificate expiration events, it is more complex to create custom logic within EventBridge or Lambda to look ahead 30 days. AWS Config provides a managed rule specifically for this purpose, making Option B more efficient.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to use AWS Config with the `acm-certificate-expiration-check` managed rule. AWS Config continuously monitors the compliance of AWS resources. EventBridge will then trigger an SNS topic, which allows you to notify the security team when the certificates expire within 30 days. This approach simplifies the notification process, making it more reliable and easier to manage.

question: A company is migrating a legacy application from an on-premises data center to AWS. The application relies on hundreds of cron jobs that run between 1 and 20 minutes on different recurring schedules throughout the day. The company wants a solution to schedule and run the cron jobs on AWS with minimal refactoring. The solution must support running the cron jobs in response to an event in the future. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.text: Create a container image for the cron jobs. Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to create a recurring schedule. Run the cron job tasks as AWS Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: This solution is incorrect because AWS Lambda functions have a maximum execution time limit of 15 minutes. The cron jobs run for up to 20 minutes, which exceeds the Lambda limit.

answers.text: Create a container image for the cron jobs. Use AWS Batch on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with a scheduling policy to run the cron jobs.
answers.explanation: This solution is a possible solution, but not optimal because you would have to run highly-available virtual machines or containers waiting for the event to happen. This solution has higher operational overhead compared to Fargate.

answers.text: Create a container image for the cron jobs. Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to create a recurring schedule. Run the cron job tasks on AWS Fargate.
answers.explanation: This solution is correct because Amazon EventBridge Scheduler can create recurring schedules to trigger tasks. AWS Fargate allows running containerized applications without managing the underlying infrastructure and can execute tasks longer than 15 minutes. Fargate allows you to pay only for the resources consumed during the execution of the cron jobs.

answers.text: Create a container image for the cron jobs. Create a workflow in AWS Step Functions that uses a Wait state to run the cron jobs at a specified time. Use the RunTask action to run the cron job tasks on AWS Fargate.
answers.explanation: This solution is incorrect because it introduces unnecessary complexity by using Step Functions. While Step Functions can schedule and execute tasks, EventBridge Scheduler is specifically designed for scheduling tasks and integrates directly with Fargate.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to create the recurring schedules and run the cron job tasks on AWS Fargate. EventBridge Scheduler is designed for scheduling and supports running tasks in response to events. AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers that allows you to run the cron jobs without managing the underlying infrastructure. Since Lambda has a 15-minute limit and the jobs can run for 20 minutes, Lambda cannot be used.

question: A company uses Salesforce and needs to load existing data and ongoing data changes from Salesforce to Amazon Redshift for analysis. The company has a strict requirement to avoid data transfer over the public internet. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

answers.text: Establish a VPN connection from the VPC to Salesforce. Use AWS Glue DataBrew to transfer data.
answers.explanation: A VPN connection still utilizes the public internet, which violates the requirement. Additionally, AWS Glue DataBrew is not the most suitable choice for ongoing data changes.

answers.text: Establish an AWS Direct Connect connection from the VPC to Salesforce. Use AWS Glue DataBrew to transfer data.
answers.explanation: While AWS Direct Connect avoids the public internet, it involves significant setup effort and cost. Also, DataBrew is not optimal for loading ongoing data changes.

answers.text: Create an AWS PrivateLink connection in the VPC to Salesforce. Use Amazon AppFlow to transfer data.
answers.explanation: AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity, avoiding the public internet. Amazon AppFlow is a fully managed service specifically designed for integration between SaaS applications like Salesforce and AWS services like Amazon Redshift, minimizing development effort.

answers.text: Create a VPC peering connection to Salesforce. Use Amazon AppFlow to transfer data.
answers.explanation: VPC peering is for connecting two AWS VPCs. Salesforce is external to AWS and does not have a VPC, therefore VPC peering cannot be used to connect to Salesforce.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to create an AWS PrivateLink connection in the VPC to Salesforce and use Amazon AppFlow to transfer data. PrivateLink ensures data doesn't traverse the public internet, and AppFlow is a managed service optimized for Salesforce integration, minimizing development effort. AWS PrivateLink enables private connectivity between VPCs and supported AWS services. Amazon AppFlow simplifies data transfer between SaaS applications (like Salesforce) and AWS services (like Amazon Redshift).

question: A company recently migrated its application to AWS. The application runs on Amazon EC2 Linux instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The application stores data in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system that uses EFS Standard- Infrequent Access storage. The application indexes the company's files. The index is stored in an Amazon RDS database. The company needs to optimize storage costs with some application and services changes. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.text: Create an Amazon S3 bucket that uses an Intelligent-Tiering lifecycle policy. Copy all files to the S3 bucket. Update the application to use Amazon S3 API to store and retrieve files.
answers.explanation: This is the most cost-effective solution. S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves data between frequent and infrequent access tiers based on usage patterns, optimizing storage costs. It also allows for application changes and uses the S3 API which provides scalability and durability.

answers.text: Deploy Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file shares. Update the application to use CIFS protocol to store and retrieve files.
answers.explanation: FSx for Windows File Server is not cost-effective and is designed for Windows-based applications. Switching to CIFS protocol is not beneficial in this scenario.

answers.text: Deploy Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system shares. Update the application to use the new mount point to store and retrieve files.
answers.explanation: FSx for OpenZFS can be expensive and optimized for High-Performance Data analysis. It is not suitable for cost optimization in this scenario.

answers.text: Create an Amazon S3 bucket that uses S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Copy all files to the S3 bucket. Update the application to use Amazon S3 API to store and retrieve files as standard retrievals.
answers.explanation: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval has longer retrieval times (up to a few hours), which makes it unsuitable for an application that requires faster access to the files. EFS Infrequent access provides millisecond retrieval time, and Glacier is not a like-for-like replacement.

overall_explanation: The most cost-effective solution is to use Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering. This allows for automatic data tiering based on access patterns, reducing storage costs. Other options are either more expensive or have unacceptable retrieval times. Switching to S3 also requires application changes, which the company is open to, making this a feasible solution. Options B and C are more expensive. Option D has unacceptable retrieval times, rendering the application unusable.

question: A robotics company is developing a surgical robot using advanced sensors, cameras, and AI. They need a public load balancer in AWS to ensure seamless and encrypted communication with backend services, capable of routing traffic based on query strings. Which solution best meets these requirements?

answers.text: Use a Network Load Balancer with a certificate attached from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Use query parameter-based routing.
answers.explanation: Network Load Balancers do not support query parameter-based routing.

answers.text: Use a Gateway Load Balancer. Import a generated certificate in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Attach the certificate to the load balancer. Use HTTP path-based routing.
answers.explanation: Gateway Load Balancers do not support query parameter-based routing and importing certificates into IAM for use with load balancers is not the standard practice; ACM is preferred.

answers.text: Use an Application Load Balancer with a certificate attached from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Use query parameter-based routing.
answers.explanation: Application Load Balancers support query parameter-based routing and using ACM for certificate management. This also provides encryption.

answers.text: Use a Network Load Balancer. Import a generated certificate in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Attach the certificate to the load balancer. Use query parameter- based routing.
answers.explanation: Network Load Balancers do not support query parameter-based routing. Certificates are typically managed via ACM, not IAM.

overall_explanation: The Application Load Balancer (ALB) is the correct choice because it supports query parameter-based routing, which is required by the company. It also allows the attachment of a certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) for encrypting traffic. Network Load Balancers and Gateway Load Balancers do not support query parameter-based routing.

question: A company's application currently runs on a single Amazon EC2 instance, with a MySQL database hosted on the same instance. To handle increased traffic and ensure high availability and automatic scalability, what solution should the company implement?

answers.text: Deploy the application to EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Create an Amazon Redshift cluster that has multiple MySQL- compatible nodes.
answers.explanation: This option uses Auto Scaling and Application Load Balancer for application scaling but uses Amazon Redshift, which is a data warehousing service, and is not suitable for replacing a MySQL database.

answers.text: Deploy the application to EC2 instances that are configured as a target group behind an Application Load Balancer. Create an Amazon RDS for MySQL cluster that has multiple instances.
answers.explanation: This option uses an Application Load Balancer and target groups, which do not inherently provide automatic scaling. RDS for MySQL provides a scalable database solution but the lack of Auto Scaling for the application instances is a drawback.

answers.text: Deploy the application to EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Create an Amazon Aurora Serverless MySQL cluster for the database layer.
answers.explanation: This option provides a highly available and automatically scalable solution. Auto Scaling ensures the application scales based on traffic, the Application Load Balancer distributes the traffic, and Aurora Serverless provides a scalable and managed MySQL-compatible database.

answers.text: Deploy the application to EC2 instances that are configured as a target group behind an Application Load Balancer. Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster that uses the MySQL connector.
answers.explanation: This option uses ElastiCache for Redis, which is an in-memory data store, and is not suitable for replacing a MySQL database. Target groups also don't provide automatic scaling.

overall_explanation: The best solution for high availability and automatic scalability is to deploy the application to an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer and use Amazon Aurora Serverless MySQL for the database layer. This ensures the application scales based on demand and the database is also automatically scalable. Redshift and ElastiCache are not direct replacements for MySQL in this scenario. Target Groups don't provide autoscaling. Therefore, option C is the correct answer.

question: A company is planning to migrate data to an Amazon S3 bucket. The data must be encrypted at rest within the S3 bucket. The encryption key must be automatically rotated every year. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.text: Migrate the data to the S3 bucket. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3). Use the built-in key rotation behavior of SSE-S3 encryption keys.
answers.explanation: SSE-S3 encryption keys are rotated regularly, but AWS does not guarantee a specific rotation period like every year. Also, encryption should be enabled *before* migrating the data. Thus, this option does not strictly meet the requirements.

answers.text: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Enable automatic key rotation. Set the S3 bucket's default encryption behavior to use the customer managed KMS key. Migrate the data to the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: This solution correctly utilizes a KMS customer managed key with automatic key rotation enabled, ensuring encryption at rest and automatic yearly key rotation. This involves the least operational overhead as the rotation is handled automatically by KMS.

answers.text: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Set the S3 bucket's default encryption behavior to use the customer managed KMS key. Migrate the data to the S3 bucket. Manually rotate the KMS key every year.
answers.explanation: While using a KMS customer managed key will allow encryption at rest, manually rotating the key every year incurs operational overhead. The question specifies the solution with the LEAST operational overhead, so this is incorrect.

answers.text: Use customer key material to encrypt the data. Migrate the data to the S3 bucket. Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key without key material. Import the customer key material into the KMS key. Enable automatic key rotation.
answers.explanation: Importing customer key material introduces more complexity and operational overhead than necessary. Directly using KMS customer managed keys for S3 encryption is more straightforward and meets the requirements with less effort. Also, data encrypted with customer keys needs to be decrypted first before uploading, adding further complexity and possible security risk. The first step in this answer is also incorrect - the data should be encrypted within S3.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to create a KMS customer managed key, enable automatic key rotation, and then set the S3 bucket's default encryption to use this KMS key. This provides encryption at rest and automatic yearly key rotation with the least operational overhead. SSE-S3 does not guarantee yearly rotation and manual rotation increases overhead. Importing customer key material is unnecessarily complex.

question: A company is migrating applications from an on-premises Microsoft Active Directory, managed by the company, to AWS. The applications are deployed across multiple AWS accounts managed centrally using AWS Organizations. The security team requires a single sign-on (SSO) solution for all AWS accounts while continuing to manage users and groups in the on-premises Active Directory. Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.text: Create an Enterprise Edition Active Directory in AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory. Configure the Active Directory to be the identity source for AWS IAM Identity Center.
answers.explanation: Creating a new Active Directory requires migrating users and groups, failing to meet the requirement of continuing to use the on-premises AD.

answers.text: Enable AWS IAM Identity Center. Configure a two-way forest trust relationship to connect the company's self-managed Active Directory with IAM Identity Center by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory.
answers.explanation: This solution allows IAM Identity Center to integrate with the existing on-premises AD for authentication and authorization, providing SSO across AWS accounts while retaining the on- premises AD as the primary identity source.

answers.text: Use AWS Directory Service and create a two-way trust relationship with the company's self-managed Active Directory.
answers.explanation: While this establishes trust, it does not provide the SSO functionality needed for the AWS accounts. IAM Identity Center is needed for SSO.

answers.text: Deploy an identity provider (IdP) on Amazon EC2. Link the IdP as an identity source within AWS IAM Identity Center.
answers.explanation: While feasible, deploying an IdP on EC2 introduces unnecessary overhead and complexity compared to using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory with IAM Identity Center.

overall_explanation: The correct answer is to enable AWS IAM Identity Center and configure a two-way forest trust relationship using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory. This allows seamless integration with the existing on-premises Active Directory, providing SSO across multiple AWS accounts without migrating users or groups.

question: A company is planning to deploy its application on an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 cluster. The application will receive large amounts of traffic. The company wants to optimize the storage performance of the cluster as the load on the application increases and minimize I/O costs.

answers.text: Configure the cluster to use the Aurora Standard storage configuration.
answers.explanation: Aurora Standard storage may be cheaper for low I/O workloads, but for high traffic applications, the I/O costs can quickly become prohibitive. It charges for I/O operations.

answers.text: Configure the cluster storage type as Provisioned IOPS.
answers.explanation: Provisioned IOPS is not an applicable storage configuration for Aurora.

answers.text: Configure the cluster storage type as General Purpose.
answers.explanation: General Purpose is not an applicable storage configuration for Aurora.

answers.text: Configure the cluster to use the Aurora I/O-Optimized storage configuration.
answers.explanation: Aurora I/O-Optimized is designed for I/O-intensive applications. While the per GB-month cost may be higher, it eliminates charges for read and write I/O operations, potentially leading to significant cost savings for high-traffic applications.

overall_explanation: Aurora I/O-Optimized provides improved price performance for I/O-intensive applications by eliminating charges for I/O operations. Given the large amounts of traffic, this option is the most cost-effective because the business wants to optimize storage performance of the cluster as the load on the application increases. Aurora only has Standard and I/O- Optimized storage options. Provisioned IOPS and General Purpose storage types are not valid storage configurations for Aurora.

question: A financial services company operating on AWS needs to demonstrate compliance with industry standards like NIST and PCI DSS to its third-party auditors. The company has hundreds of AWS accounts within a single AWS Organizations setup. They require a solution to consistently monitor the state of their security controls across all accounts and provide evidence of implementation and proper functioning to the auditors. Which AWS service will best satisfy these requirements?

answers.text: Designate one account as the Amazon Inspector delegated administrator account from the Organizations management account. Integrate Inspector with Organizations to discover and scan resources across all AWS accounts. Enable Inspector industry standards for NIST and PCI DSS.
answers.explanation: Inspector primarily focuses on vulnerability assessments, not continuous compliance monitoring against industry standards across an entire organization.

answers.text: Designate one account as the Amazon GuardDuty delegated administrator account from the Organizations management account. In the designated GuardDuty administrator account, enable GuardDuty to protect all member accounts. Enable GuardDuty industry standards for NIST and PCI DSS.
answers.explanation: GuardDuty is a threat detection service and does not provide compliance monitoring or reporting capabilities for NIST and PCI DSS.

answers.text: Configure an AWS CloudTrail organization trail in the Organizations management account. Designate one account as the compliance account. Enable CloudTrail security standards for NIST and PCI DSS in the compliance account.
answers.explanation: CloudTrail primarily logs API calls; it doesn't provide a compliance dashboard or assess configurations against NIST and PCI DSS standards.

answers.text: Designate one account as the AWS Security Hub delegated administrator account from the Organizations management account. In the designated Security Hub administrator account, enable Security Hub for all member accounts. Enable Security Hub standards for NIST and PCI DSS.
answers.explanation: Security Hub integrates with AWS Organizations, supports multiple compliance standards like NIST and PCI DSS, and allows for centralized monitoring of security posture across all accounts.

overall_explanation: AWS Security Hub is the most appropriate service. By designating a delegated administrator account, Security Hub can be enabled for all member accounts within AWS Organizations. It supports enabling security standards like NIST and PCI DSS, providing a centralized view of compliance status and enabling the company to demonstrate the implementation and functioning of security controls to auditors.

question: A company uses an Amazon S3 bucket as its data lake storage platform. The S3 bucket contains a massive amount of data that is accessed randomly by multiple teams and hundreds of applications. The company wants to reduce the S3 storage costs and provide immediate availability for frequently accessed objects. What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

answers.text: Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition objects to the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class.
answers.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically stores objects in access tiers optimized for frequent, infrequent, and rarely accessed data, reducing costs and providing immediate availability.

answers.text: Store objects in Amazon S3 Glacier. Use S3 Select to provide applications with access to the data.
answers.explanation: S3 Glacier is for archival data and S3 Select, while useful, does not provide immediate availability as required.

answers.text: Use data from S3 storage class analysis to create S3 Lifecycle rules to automatically transition objects to the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class.
answers.explanation: While this approach is valid, it requires manual configuration and analysis, which is less operationally efficient than S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

answers.text: Transition objects to the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class. Create an AWS Lambda function to transition objects to the S3 Standard storage class when they are accessed by an application.
answers.explanation: This approach introduces operational overhead with managing a Lambda function and is less efficient than the automated tiering provided by S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

overall_explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering is the most operationally efficient solution because it automatically manages storage tiers based on access patterns, ensuring immediate availability for frequently accessed objects while reducing storage costs for infrequently accessed objects without manual intervention.

question: A company's dynamic website is hosted using on-premises servers in the United States. The company is launching its product in Europe, and it wants to optimize site loading times for new European users. The site's backend must remain in the United States. The product is being launched in a few days, and an immediate solution is needed. What should the solutions architect recommend?

answers.text: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in us-east-1 and migrate the site to it.
answers.explanation: Launching a single EC2 instance, even in a US region, will not effectively reduce latency for European users and migrating the site takes time.

answers.text: Move the website to Amazon S3. Use Cross-Region Replication between Regions.
answers.explanation: Amazon S3 is designed for static content and doesn't provide the server-side processing capabilities needed for a dynamic website. Also, this migration would take too long.

answers.text: Use Amazon CloudFront with a custom origin pointing to the on-premises servers.
answers.explanation: Amazon CloudFront, a CDN, caches content at edge locations closer to users, reducing latency. Using a custom origin allows it to point to the existing on-premises servers without requiring a full migration. This is also the quickest solution.

answers.text: Use an Amazon Route 53 geoproximity routing policy pointing to on-premises servers.
answers.explanation: While Route 53 geoproximity routing directs users to the closest server, it doesn't cache content like a CDN, so European users would still experience latency accessing the US-based on-premises servers.

overall_explanation: Amazon CloudFront is the best solution because it's a CDN that can cache static and dynamic content at edge locations closer to European users, thereby reducing latency. The custom origin feature allows it to seamlessly integrate with the existing on-premises infrastructure without requiring a complete migration, making it the fastest option to implement. The other options involve full migration and would take longer to implement.

question: A social media company has a dataset of 5 TB containing 1 million user profiles and 10 million connections represented as many-to-many relationships. They need to efficiently identify mutual connections between users up to five degrees of separation. Which AWS service is best suited for this task, ensuring high performance and scalability?

answers.text: Amazon S3 with Amazon Athena using SQL JOIN queries.
answers.explanation: While S3 is suitable for storing large datasets and Athena allows querying data in S3, using SQL JOIN queries for finding connections up to five levels will be inefficient and slow due to the complex relationships.

answers.text: Amazon Neptune, storing the data as a graph database with nodes and edges.
answers.explanation: Amazon Neptune is a graph database service designed for handling highly connected data. It can efficiently traverse relationships and find connections up to multiple levels, making it ideal for this use case.

answers.text: Amazon S3 with Amazon QuickSight for visualizing connections.
answers.explanation: QuickSight is a business intelligence service for visualization, not for efficiently querying highly connected data for multiple degrees of separation.

answers.text: Amazon RDS using multiple tables with SQL JOIN queries.
answers.explanation: Similar to Athena, using a relational database like RDS and SQL JOIN queries for finding connections up to five levels will be inefficient and slow due to the complex relationships.

overall_explanation: Amazon Neptune is the best choice because it's a graph database specifically designed for efficiently managing and querying highly connected data like social networks. It allows for fast traversal of relationships to find mutual connections up to five levels. Relational databases and S3-based solutions with SQL JOIN queries or visualization tools will be less efficient for this type of complex relationship analysis. Neptune automatically scales storage and compute resources based on workload demands, ensuring optimal performance even as the dataset grows over time. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/notebooks-visualization.html

question: A company needs to establish a secure and cost-effective connection between their on- premises data center and their AWS environment. The connection requires low bandwidth and will only handle a small amount of traffic. The setup also needs to be implemented as quickly as possible. Which of the following options is the MOST suitable for this scenario?

answers.text: Implement a client VPN.
answers.explanation: A client VPN is more suited for individual users connecting to the network, not for a site-to-site connection.

answers.text: Implement AWS Direct Connect.
answers.explanation: AWS Direct Connect is designed for high-bandwidth, low-latency connections and is a more expensive option, making it unsuitable for low-bandwidth requirements.

answers.text: Implement a bastion host on Amazon EC2.
answers.explanation: A bastion host provides secure access to EC2 instances within a VPC but doesn't establish a site-to- site connection between the on-premises network and AWS.

answers.text: Implement an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection.
answers.explanation: An AWS Site-to-Site VPN provides a secure, cost-effective, and quick way to connect an on- premises network to AWS. It is ideal for low-bandwidth and low-traffic scenarios.

overall_explanation: AWS Site-to-Site VPN is the most cost-effective and appropriate solution for establishing a secure connection between an on-premises environment and AWS when low bandwidth and quick setup are required. Direct Connect is overkill for low bandwidth. A client VPN is for individual users, and a bastion host does not provide the desired site-to-site connection. Therefore, Site-to-Site VPN is the best choice.

question: A company is migrating its on-premises SFTP file transfer solution to AWS to improve scalability and reduce costs using Amazon S3. Employees need to use their existing on-premises Microsoft Active Directory (AD) credentials to access the new solution. The company wants to maintain its current authentication and file access mechanisms with minimal operational overhead. Which solution is the MOST suitable?

answers.text: Configure an S3 File Gateway. Create SMB file shares on the file gateway that use the existing Active Directory to authenticate.
answers.explanation: S3 File Gateway is primarily for presenting S3 data as a file share to on-premises applications, not for direct SFTP access with AD authentication. It also involves more infrastructure to manage.

answers.text: Configure an Auto Scaling group with Amazon EC2 instances to run an SFTP solution. Configure the group to scale up at 60% CPU utilization.
answers.explanation: This solution requires managing EC2 instances, patching, and the SFTP software itself, leading to high operational overhead. It also doesn't natively integrate with AD for authentication.

answers.text: Create an AWS Transfer Family server with SFTP endpoints. Choose the AWS Directory Service option as the identity provider. Use AD Connector to connect the on-premises Active Directory.
answers.explanation: AWS Transfer Family simplifies SFTP server management and natively integrates with AWS Directory Service. Using AD Connector allows leveraging existing on-premises AD credentials for authentication with minimal operational overhead.

answers.text: Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP endpoint. Configure the endpoint to use the AWS Directory Service option as the identity provider to connect to the existing Active Directory.
answers.explanation: This option misses a critical step. Transfer Family requires a *server* to be created before an endpoint can be configured. Without creating the server, no SFTP service is enabled.

overall_explanation: AWS Transfer Family provides a managed SFTP service that integrates with Amazon S3 and supports authentication via AWS Directory Service. By using AD Connector, the solution allows employees to use their existing on-premises Active Directory credentials for SFTP access. This option eliminates the need for managing servers and minimizes operational overhead compared to alternatives. Option C correctly explains the need to create Transfer Family *server* and use AD Connector.

question: A company is designing an event-driven order processing system. Upon order creation, multiple independent validation steps are required, each performed by an idempotent AWS Lambda function. Each validation step only requires a specific subset of the order event data. The company needs to ensure each Lambda function has access only to its required data subset. Furthermore, the system components should be loosely coupled to accommodate future business changes. Which solution best meets these requirements?

answers.text: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue for each validation step. Create a new Lambda function to transform the order data to the format that each validation step requires and publish the messages to the appropriate SQS queues. Subscribe each validation step Lambda function to its corresponding SQS queue.
answers.explanation: This solution requires an additional Lambda function for data transformation and introduces complexity with multiple SQS queues. It's a valid approach but not the most efficient.

answers.text: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the validation step Lambda functions to the SNS topic. Use message body filtering to send only the required data to each subscribed Lambda function.
answers.explanation: SNS message filtering cannot manipulate messages; it can only discard or forward the FULL message based on attribute matching. It doesn't allow for sending only a subset of the data.

answers.text: Create an Amazon EventBridge event bus. Create an event rule for each validation step. Configure the input transformer to send only the required data to each target validation step Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Amazon EventBridge with input transformation allows for routing events based on rules and transforming the event payload to send only the required data subset to each Lambda function. This promotes loose coupling and efficient data handling.

answers.text: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Create a new Lambda function to subscribe to the SQS queue and to transform the order data to the format that each validation step requires. Use the new Lambda function to perform synchronous invocations of the validation step Lambda functions in parallel on separate threads.
answers.explanation: This approach introduces tighter coupling through synchronous invocations and requires an additional Lambda function for transformation and orchestration, making it less ideal than EventBridge.

overall_explanation: Amazon EventBridge provides the best solution because it allows for event-driven architecture and input transformation. The input transformer feature enables sending only the necessary data subset to each Lambda function, satisfying the requirement of providing each validation step with only the information it needs. Furthermore, EventBridge facilitates loose coupling between components, accommodating future business changes more effectively. Option A requires an extra Lambda, option B cannot transform the message to only include certain attributes, and option D uses synchronous invocations which creates tight coupling. Therefore, EventBridge is the most suitable and efficient approach.

question: A company is migrating a three-tier application to AWS. The application utilizes a MySQL database. Historically, users have reported performance degradation when creating new entries due to the generation of real-time reports during business hours. Which solution will optimize the application's performance in AWS, specifically addressing the reporting-related performance bottlenecks?

answers.text: Import the data into an Amazon DynamoDB table with provisioned capacity. Refactor the application to use DynamoDB for reports.
answers.explanation: DynamoDB is a NoSQL database suitable for high-throughput reads and writes. While it could handle report generation, refactoring the entire application to use DynamoDB solely for reports is a significant undertaking and might not be the most efficient solution for the described problem.

answers.text: Create the database on a compute optimized Amazon EC2 instance. Ensure compute resources exceed the on-premises database.
answers.explanation: While increasing compute resources might improve overall database performance, it doesn't isolate the reporting workload, meaning that the performance issues related to real-time reports impacting new entry creation are unlikely to be fully resolved.

answers.text: Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ DB cluster with multiple read replicas. Configure the application to use the reader endpoint for reports.
answers.explanation: This is the most suitable solution. Aurora MySQL read replicas allow read-only queries to be offloaded from the primary database instance, preventing report generation from impacting the performance of write operations (new entry creation). The reader endpoint distributes read traffic across multiple replicas, further enhancing performance.

answers.text: Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ DB cluster. Configure the application to use the backup instance of the cluster as an endpoint for the reports.
answers.explanation: While Aurora Multi-AZ clusters have a standby instance for failover, it's not intended to be used as a read replica in the same way dedicated read replicas are. Furthermore, using the backup instance directly for reports is not a supported or recommended practice, as it can interfere with the failover process and potentially lead to data inconsistency.

overall_explanation: The most effective solution is to create an Amazon Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ DB cluster with multiple read replicas. By configuring the application to use the reader endpoint for report generation, the read-heavy report queries are offloaded from the primary database instance. This prevents the performance impact on write operations, such as creating new entries, addressing the reported performance issues. Options A and B are not the best choices as they involve unnecessary overhead. Using a backup instance is also not recommended.

question: A company is expanding a secure on-premises network to the AWS Cloud by using an AWS Direct Connect connection. The on-premises network has no direct internet access. An application that runs on the on-premises network needs to access an Amazon S3 bucket in the MOST cost-effective manner. Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.text: Create a public virtual interface (VIF). Route the AWS traffic over the public VIF.
answers.explanation: This option is incorrect because a public VIF requires internet access, which the on-premises network does not have.

answers.text: Create a VPC and a NAT gateway. Route the AWS traffic from the on-premises network to the NAT gateway.
answers.explanation: This option is incorrect because NAT gateway requires internet access for traffic routing, which is not available for the on-premises network.

answers.text: Create a VPC and an Amazon S3 interface endpoint. Route the AWS traffic from the on- premises network to the S3 interface endpoint.
answers.explanation: This is the correct answer. Using an S3 interface endpoint allows the on-premises network to access S3 privately, without traversing the internet, and is a cost-effective solution.

answers.text: Create a VPC peering connection between the on-premises network and Direct Connect. Route the AWS traffic over the peering connection.
answers.explanation: VPC peering is used for connectivity between VPCs and does not provide access to AWS public services such as Amazon S3.

overall_explanation: The MOST cost-effective solution is to create a VPC and an Amazon S3 interface endpoint. This allows private access to S3 without the need for internet access, which aligns with the constraint that the on-premises network has no direct internet access. Public VIF requires internet access and NAT Gateway also requires internet access. VPC peering doesn't provide access to public AWS Services.

question: A company hosts its website using an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances in a single AWS Region. The website does not rely on a database. The company is expanding and has deployed the website to a second Region. They want to distribute traffic across both Regions to handle increased traffic and ensure disaster recovery. The solution should prevent serving traffic from a Region where the website is unhealthy. Which policy or resource should the company use to meet these requirements?

answers.text: An Amazon Route 53 simple routing policy
answers.explanation: A simple routing policy does not support health checks, so it cannot ensure traffic is only served from healthy Regions.

answers.text: An Amazon Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy
answers.explanation: A multivalue answer routing policy allows configuring Amazon Route 53 to return multiple values (e.g., IP addresses) in response to DNS queries. It also supports health checks, returning only values for healthy resources. This improves availability and load balancing.

answers.text: An Application Load Balancer in one Region with a target group that specifies the EC2 instance IDs from both Regions
answers.explanation: Application Load Balancers (ALBs) operate within a single Region. Specifying EC2 instances from different Regions in a single ALB's target group is not a valid configuration.

answers.text: An Application Load Balancer in one Region with a target group that specifies the IP addresses of the EC2 instances from both Regions
answers.explanation: While ALBs can use IP addresses as targets, they still operate within a single Region. Distributing traffic across Regions using a single ALB is not possible. Also, this approach wouldn't provide native health checking across regions.

overall_explanation: Amazon Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy is the best solution. It allows returning multiple IP addresses (from different Regions) in response to DNS queries, and it supports health checks to ensure that only healthy instances/Regions receive traffic. Simple routing policies lack health checks, and Application Load Balancers operate within a single Region, making them unsuitable for cross-region traffic distribution and failover.

question: A company's applications run on Amazon EC2 instances backed by Amazon EBS. These instances use the latest Amazon Linux release. Employees are experiencing availability issues when storing and retrieving files that are 25 GB or larger. The company requires a solution that avoids file transfers between EC2 instances and ensures file availability across many EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones. Which solution best meets these requirements?

answers.text: Migrate all files to an Amazon S3 bucket and instruct employees to access the files from the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: While S3 provides durable object storage, it might not be the most efficient for frequent file access directly from the EC2 instances. It also doesn't inherently address the 'available across many EC2 instances' requirement without additional configuration.

answers.text: Take a snapshot of the existing EBS volume. Mount the snapshot as an EBS volume across the EC2 instances. Instruct the employees to access the files from the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: EBS volumes are region-locked. Mounting a snapshot as a volume on multiple EC2 instances across Availability Zones would require creating multiple volumes from the snapshot, increasing management overhead and not providing a shared file system.

answers.text: Mount an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system across all the EC2 instances. Instruct the employees to access the files from the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Amazon EFS is designed to be mounted concurrently by multiple EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. This fulfills the requirement of shared access and availability across different AZs without manual data transfer.

answers.text: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the EC2 instances. Configure new EC2 instances from the AMI that use an instance store volume. Instruct the employees to access the files from the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Instance store volumes are ephemeral and the data is lost when the instance is stopped or terminated. Also, sharing data across Availability Zones wouldn't be inherently addressed.

overall_explanation: Amazon EFS provides a shared file system that can be mounted concurrently by multiple EC2 instances, addressing the requirement for file availability across many EC2 instances and multiple Availability Zones. It eliminates the need for file transfers between instances and maintains availability when dealing with large files.

question: A company is running a highly sensitive application on Amazon EC2 backed by an Amazon RDS database. Compliance regulations mandate that all personally identifiable information (PII) be encrypted at rest. Which solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of changes to the infrastructure?

answers.text: Deploy AWS Certificate Manager to generate certificates. Use the certificates to encrypt the database volume.
answers.explanation: AWS Certificate Manager is used for managing SSL/TLS certificates for securing network communications, not for encrypting data at rest on database volumes.

answers.text: Deploy AWS CloudHSM, generate encryption keys, and use the keys to encrypt database volumes.
answers.explanation: CloudHSM provides hardware security modules in the AWS cloud. While this can be used for encryption, it involves more infrastructure changes and complexity than necessary for this requirement.

answers.text: Configure SSL encryption using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt database volumes.
answers.explanation: SSL encryption secures data in transit, not data at rest. While using KMS is appropriate, SSL is not the correct mechanism for encrypting the database volumes themselves.

answers.text: Configure Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) encryption and Amazon RDS encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt instance and database volumes.
answers.explanation: This option provides encryption at rest for both the EC2 instance's EBS volumes and the RDS database volumes, using KMS for key management. It is the least disruptive approach as it leverages existing AWS features.

overall_explanation: Option D provides the most straightforward way to meet the encryption-at-rest compliance requirement with minimal changes to the existing infrastructure. RDS relies on EBS volumes for storage, therefore encrypting both EBS and RDS ensures comprehensive protection. Using KMS allows centralized key management.

question: A company runs an AWS Lambda function in private subnets within a VPC. These subnets route outbound traffic through an EC2 NAT instance to access the internet. The Lambda function processes data and uploads the resulting objects to Amazon S3. Intermittently, the Lambda function experiences timeouts during the object upload process, attributed to network saturation on the NAT instance. The company aims to enable the Lambda function to access Amazon S3 without routing traffic through the internet. Which solution satisfies these requirements?

answers.text: Replace the EC2 NAT instance with an AWS managed NAT gateway.
answers.explanation: Replacing the EC2 NAT instance with a NAT gateway will not prevent the Lambda function from traversing the internet to access S3.

answers.text: Increase the size of the EC2 NAT instance in the VPC to a network optimized instance type.
answers.explanation: Increasing the size of the EC2 NAT instance might alleviate the saturation temporarily, but it does not prevent the Lambda function from traversing the internet to access S3. The problem statement explicitly states that the company wants to avoid internet traversal.

answers.text: Provision a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC. Update the route tables of the subnets accordingly.
answers.explanation: A gateway endpoint allows direct access to S3 from within the VPC, without needing to route traffic through the internet. By updating the subnet route tables to use the gateway endpoint, the Lambda function can access S3 directly.

answers.text: Provision a transit gateway. Place transit gateway attachments in the private subnets where the Lambda function is running.
answers.explanation: A transit gateway is primarily used to connect multiple VPCs and on-premises networks. While it could be used, it is not the most straightforward or cost-effective solution for accessing S3 from a Lambda function in private subnets without traversing the internet. Gateway endpoints are the preferred way to achieve this.

overall_explanation: Provisioning a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 allows the Lambda function in the private subnets to directly access S3 without routing traffic through the internet or a NAT instance. Updating the route tables ensures that traffic destined for S3 uses the endpoint. This eliminates the saturation issue on the NAT instance and fulfills the requirement of avoiding internet traversal. NAT Gateways will still require internet access and Transit Gateways are used to connect VPCs, so they will not solve the problem as directly and cost-effectively as a Gateway Endpoint.

question: A company aims to minimize costs for its existing three-tier web architecture hosted on Amazon EC2 instances across development, test, and production environments. The instances show average CPU utilization of 30% during peak hours and 10% during off-peak hours. Production instances must run 24/7. Development and test instances are required for at least 8 hours daily, with plans to automate their shutdown when not in use. Which EC2 instance purchasing option provides the MOST cost-effective solution for the company's needs?

answers.text: Use Spot Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Spot Instances are not suitable for production environments requiring continuous availability. Reserved Instances may not be optimal for Dev/Test as these are not used 24/7.

answers.text: Use Reserved Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use On-Demand Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Reserved Instances are cost-effective for production instances that run continuously. On-Demand Instances offer flexibility for development and test instances with variable usage patterns.

answers.text: Use Spot Blocks for the production EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Spot Blocks are no longer available as an option. Reserved Instances may not be optimal for Dev/Test as these are not used 24/7.

answers.text: Use On-Demand Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use Spot Blocks for the development and test EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: On-Demand Instances for production will be the most expensive option. Spot Blocks are no longer available.

overall_explanation: The most cost-effective solution is to utilize Reserved Instances for the production environment, which operates continuously. This provides significant savings compared to On-Demand pricing. For the development and test environments, On-Demand Instances are ideal due to their variable usage patterns and the ability to stop them when not needed. This avoids paying for idle resources, ensuring cost optimization.

question: A global news company uses AWS to host its broadcast system. Reporters worldwide send live broadcasts using RTMP (Real-Time Messaging Protocol) from their phones to the system. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that allows reporters to send the highest quality streams with accelerated TCP connections back to the broadcast system. Which AWS service should the solutions architect use?

answers.text: Amazon CloudFront
answers.explanation: CloudFront is a CDN primarily used for caching and delivering static and dynamic web content. While it can accelerate HTTP(S) traffic, it's not the best solution for general TCP acceleration required for RTMP streaming.

answers.text: AWS Global Accelerator
answers.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator provides static IP addresses that serve as entry points for applications. It optimizes the network path to improve TCP and UDP performance, making it suitable for accelerating RTMP streams from reporters worldwide.

answers.text: AWS Client VPN
answers.explanation: AWS Client VPN provides secure remote access to AWS resources. While it offers secure connections, it doesn't inherently accelerate TCP connections for live streaming.

answers.text: Amazon EC2 instances and AWS Elastic IP addresses
answers.explanation: Using EC2 instances with Elastic IP addresses provides static IPs, but it doesn't offer the global network optimization and TCP acceleration provided by Global Accelerator.

overall_explanation: AWS Global Accelerator is the most suitable choice because it is designed to optimize TCP and UDP traffic globally, providing accelerated and reliable connections back to the broadcast system. It uses the AWS global network to route traffic efficiently, improving the quality and reliability of live streams from reporters around the world.

question: A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) to run its self-managed database. The company has 350 TB of data spread across all EBS volumes. The company takes daily EBS snapshots and keeps the snapshots for 1 month. The daily change rate is 5% of the EBS volumes. Because of new regulations, the company needs to keep the monthly snapshots for 7 years. The company needs to change its backup strategy to comply with the new regulations and to ensure that data is available with minimal administrative effort. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.text: Keep the daily snapshot in the EBS snapshot standard tier for 1 month. Copy the monthly snapshot to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive with a 7-year retention period.
answers.explanation: This option involves copying to S3 Glacier Deep Archive. While Glacier is cost-effective for long-term storage, the initial transfer and potential restores can add complexity and administrative overhead.

answers.text: Continue with the current EBS snapshot policy. Add a new policy to move the monthly snapshot to Amazon EBS Snapshots Archive with a 7-year retention period.
answers.explanation: EBS Snapshots Archive is designed for long-term EBS snapshot retention and provides a balance between cost and accessibility. Using it in conjunction with the existing snapshot policy offers a straightforward solution.

answers.text: Keep the daily snapshot in the EBS snapshot standard tier for 1 month. Keep the monthly snapshot in the standard tier for 7 years. Use incremental snapshots.
answers.explanation: Keeping snapshots in the standard tier for 7 years would be prohibitively expensive, making this option not cost-effective.

answers.text: Keep the daily snapshot in the EBS snapshot standard tier. Use EBS direct APIs to take snapshots of all the EBS volumes every month. Store the snapshots in an Amazon S3 bucket in the Infrequent Access tier for 7 years.
answers.explanation: Using EBS direct APIs and storing in S3 Infrequent Access involves more management overhead than using EBS Snapshot Archive and might not be as cost-effective.

overall_explanation: The most cost-effective solution that meets the requirements is to continue the current EBS snapshot policy and add a new policy to move the monthly snapshot to Amazon EBS Snapshots Archive with a 7-year retention period. This solution leverages a feature designed for long-term snapshot storage and minimizes administrative effort. While S3 Glacier Deep Archive is cheaper, the effort to copy data there and potentially restore it adds complexity.

question: A company runs an application on several Amazon EC2 instances that store persistent data on an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. The company needs to replicate the data to another AWS Region by using an AWS-managed service solution in the MOST cost- effective manner. Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.text: Use the EFS-to-EFS replication to replicate the data to an EFS file system in another Region.
answers.explanation: While EFS-to-EFS replication is a valid solution, AWS Backup is generally considered a more managed service and can offer better cost-effectiveness for long-term retention, backup policies and regional availability.

answers.text: Run a nightly script to copy data from the EFS file system to an Amazon S3 bucket. Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication on the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: This solution requires managing your own scripts and is not a fully AWS-managed service. It also potentially involves higher operational overhead and costs compared to AWS Backup or EFS Replication.

answers.text: Create a VPC in another Region. Establish a cross-Region VPC peer. Run a nightly rsync to copy data from the original Region to the new Region.
answers.explanation: Similar to option B, this solution involves managing your own infrastructure and scripts. This is not an AWS-managed service and can incur significant operational overhead, complexity and cost.

answers.text: Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan with a rule that takes a daily backup and replicates it to another Region. Assign the EFS file system resource to the backup plan.
answers.explanation: AWS Backup is a managed service specifically designed for backing up and replicating data across regions. It provides a cost-effective, policy-based approach with centralized management, making it the most suitable option.

overall_explanation: AWS Backup provides a fully managed, policy-based service for backing up and replicating data, satisfying the requirement for an AWS-managed service and cost-effective solution for replicating the EFS file system to another Region. While EFS-to-EFS replication can be considered, AWS Backup offers simplicity in policy management and a more comprehensive approach to data protection across services.

question: An e-commerce company is migrating its on-premises workload to the AWS Cloud. The workload currently consists of a web application and a backend Microsoft SQL database for storage. The company anticipates a surge in customer traffic during an upcoming promotional event. The new infrastructure in the AWS Cloud must be highly available and scalable, while minimizing administrative overhead. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.text: Migrate the web application to two Amazon EC2 instances across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server with read replicas in both Availability Zones.
answers.explanation: This option provides high availability for the application but using read replicas for the database is not the optimal way to achieve HA. Read replicas are typically used for read scaling and not for automatic failover in case of a primary database failure. It also increases administrative overhead compared to a managed solution.

answers.text: Migrate the web application to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to two EC2 instances across separate AWS Regions with database replication.
answers.explanation: While this option offers scalability for the web application, replicating the database across AWS Regions introduces significant complexity and higher latency. Managing database replication on EC2 instances requires more administrative overhead than using a managed database service.

answers.text: Migrate the web application to Amazon EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS with Multi-AZ deployment.
answers.explanation: This option is the MOST suitable solution. Using an Auto Scaling group with EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones ensures high availability and scalability for the web application. Amazon RDS with Multi-AZ deployment provides automatic failover and high availability for the database with minimal administrative overhead.

answers.text: Migrate the web application to three Amazon EC2 instances across three Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to three EC2 instances across three Availability Zones.
answers.explanation: This option doesn't utilise managed service for the database and requires manual administration of EC2 instances for the database, which creates a high operational overhead. While it can be highly available, it doesn't provide the least administrative overhead compared to the RDS Multi-AZ solution.

overall_explanation: The optimal solution involves using managed services to minimize administrative overhead while maximizing availability and scalability.
