Auto Scaling groups for the web application and RDS with Multi-AZ deployment for the database are key components. Auto Scaling group with EC2 instances behind an ALB provides high availability and scalability. RDS Multi-AZ deployment provides automatic failover, minimizing administrative overhead and ensuring database availability.

question: A company's on-premises business application generates hundreds of files daily, stored on an SMB file share, requiring low-latency connection to application servers. A new policy mandates copying all application-generated files to AWS. A VPN connection to AWS already exists. The application development team lacks time for code modifications to move the application to AWS. Which service should a solutions architect recommend to copy files to AWS?

answers.text: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
answers.explanation: Amazon EFS is a network file system for use with AWS Cloud compute instances and on-premises servers. It does not natively integrate with on-premises SMB shares without modification to the application.

answers.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
answers.explanation: While Amazon FSx for Windows File Server supports SMB, it's primarily designed for cloud-native Windows applications and doesn't directly facilitate copying data from an existing on-premises SMB share without code modifications or additional tools.

answers.text: AWS Snowball
answers.explanation: AWS Snowball is a data transport solution that uses physical devices to move large amounts of data into and out of AWS. It's suitable for initial bulk data migration but isn't designed for continuous, automated file copying.

answers.text: AWS Storage Gateway
answers.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway provides hybrid cloud storage services, offering on-premises access to virtually unlimited cloud storage. The File Gateway configuration supports SMB (and NFS), enabling on-premises applications to seamlessly store and retrieve files in Amazon S3 using existing file system protocols, without application modifications.

overall_explanation: AWS Storage Gateway, specifically the File Gateway configuration, is the recommended solution. It allows seamless integration with the existing on-premises SMB file share and automatically copies files to AWS (e.g., Amazon S3) in the background. This meets the requirement of copying all application-generated files to AWS without requiring application code modifications and leverages the existing VPN connection.

question: A company with 15 employees stores employee start dates in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company wants to send an email message to each employee on the day of their work anniversary. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

answers.text: Create a script that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Use a cron job to run this script every day on an Amazon EC2 instance.
answers.explanation: This solution requires managing an EC2 instance and a cron job, increasing operational overhead.

answers.text: Create a script that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Use a cron job to run this script every day on an Amazon EC2 instance.
answers.explanation: This solution requires managing an EC2 instance and a cron job, increasing operational overhead. SQS is also not suitable for sending emails.

answers.text: Create an AWS Lambda function that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Schedule this Lambda function to run every day.
answers.explanation: This solution uses a serverless approach with Lambda and SNS, reducing operational overhead. Lambda can be scheduled to run daily.

answers.text: Create an AWS Lambda function that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Schedule this Lambda function to run every day.
answers.explanation: This solution uses Lambda, but SQS is not designed for sending email messages directly.

overall_explanation: The most operationally efficient solution is to use a Lambda function triggered daily to scan the DynamoDB table and send email messages using SNS. This approach avoids the overhead of managing an EC2 instance and cron job. SNS is the correct service to send email. SQS is used for message queuing, not direct email sending.

question: A company's application is running on Amazon EC2 instances within an Auto Scaling group behind an Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) load balancer. Based on the application's history, the company anticipates a spike in traffic during a holiday each year. A solutions architect must design a strategy to ensure that the Auto Scaling group proactively increases capacity to minimize any performance impact on application users. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.text: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to scale up the EC2 instances when CPU utilization exceeds 90%.
answers.explanation: This is a reactive approach and does not proactively increase capacity before the expected traffic spike.

answers.text: Create a recurring scheduled action to scale up the Auto Scaling group before the expected period of peak demand.
answers.explanation: This is a proactive approach. A scheduled action allows the Auto Scaling group to increase capacity in advance of the anticipated traffic spike.

answers.text: Increase the minimum and maximum number of EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group during the peak demand period.
answers.explanation: While increasing the minimum and maximum sizes has some benefit, it doesn't proactively scale up before the event. It simply allows the Auto Scaling group to scale higher if needed, but won't trigger scaling.

answers.text: Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to send alerts when there are autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH events.
answers.explanation: This option only provides notification of scaling events and does not proactively increase capacity.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to create a recurring scheduled action. Since the company anticipates a spike in traffic during a holiday each year, a scheduled action is an ideal way to proactively scale up the Auto Scaling group before the expected period of peak demand, minimizing any performance impact. CloudWatch alarms are reactive and trigger scaling based on metrics, which might be too late. Increasing the min/max capacity only allows for scaling but doesn't trigger it. SNS notifications are for awareness and not proactive scaling.

question: A company uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL databases for its data tier. The company is required to implement automated password rotation for these databases with minimal operational overhead. Which solution should the company implement?

answers.text: Store the password in AWS Secrets Manager. Enable automatic rotation on the secret.
answers.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager allows for automatic rotation of secrets, including database passwords, with minimal operational overhead. It is specifically designed for this purpose.

answers.text: Store the password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Enable automatic rotation on the parameter.
answers.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store does not natively support automatic password rotation. It requires custom solutions like Lambda functions, increasing operational overhead.

answers.text: Store the password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Write an AWS Lambda function that rotates the password.
answers.explanation: While possible, using Parameter Store with a Lambda function for password rotation increases operational overhead due to the need to develop, deploy, and manage the Lambda function.

answers.text: Store the password in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Enable automatic rotation on the AWS KMS key.
answers.explanation: AWS KMS is designed for managing encryption keys, not database passwords. It doesn't offer automatic rotation of database credentials and is not an appropriate choice for this scenario.

overall_explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is the best option because it provides built-in functionality for automatic secret rotation, reducing operational overhead. Parameter Store requires a custom implementation with Lambda, and KMS is not designed for managing database passwords. Secrets Manager allows setting up automatic rotation for secrets (passwords). https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html

question: A company currently runs its application on Oracle Database Enterprise Edition on-premises. The company plans to migrate the application and its database to AWS, leveraging the Bring Your Own License (BYOL) model. A critical requirement is maintaining support for third-party database features that necessitate privileged access. A solutions architect needs to design the most cost-effective solution for this database migration to AWS. Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.text: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for Oracle by using native tools. Replace the third-party features with AWS Lambda.
answers.explanation: This option doesn't directly address the need for privileged access to third-party database features and requires significant application changes. Replacing database features with Lambda functions might not be feasible or cost-effective.

answers.text: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle by using native tools. Customize the new database settings to support the third-party features.
answers.explanation: Amazon RDS Custom allows for customization of the database environment, enabling support for third-party features that require privileged access. It also supports the BYOL model for Oracle licenses, making it a suitable and cost-effective solution.

answers.text: Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Customize the new database settings to support the third-party features.
answers.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL database and is not compatible with Oracle and third-party features, thus this option does not fit the customer's requirements.

answers.text: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Rewrite the application code to remove the dependency on third-party features.
answers.explanation: This option requires significant application code rewrites, which can be complex and expensive. It also involves migrating to a different database engine (PostgreSQL), which introduces compatibility challenges and is not the most cost-effective solution given the requirements.

overall_explanation: Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle allows the necessary level of customization to support third-party features that require privileged access, while also supporting the BYOL model. This approach avoids the need for costly application code rewrites or the need to migrate to a completely different database platform. Therefore, migrating to Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle is the most cost-effective solution.

question: A large organization with a significant presence in the AWS Cloud utilizes Amazon EC2, Amazon RDS, and Amazon DynamoDB. They currently rely on disparate, custom scripts for backing up their infrastructure. To improve efficiency and reduce management overhead, the organization aims to centralize backup management and automate data backups using AWS-native solutions. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.text: Use third-party backup software with an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway virtual tape library.
answers.explanation: This solution introduces third-party dependencies and doesn't leverage native AWS backup capabilities for EC2, RDS, and DynamoDB directly. While tape gateway can be useful, it doesn't address the need for centralized management and automation with AWS native tools.

answers.text: Use AWS Backup to configure and monitor all backups for the services in use.
answers.explanation: AWS Backup is a centralized backup service that supports EC2, RDS, and DynamoDB, providing a single pane of glass for managing and automating backups. It allows for policy-based backup scheduling and retention, meeting the requirements of centralized management and automation.

answers.text: Use AWS Config to set lifecycle management to take snapshots of all data sources on a schedule.
answers.explanation: AWS Config is primarily a configuration management service and not a backup service. While it can trigger actions based on configuration changes, it does not provide centralized backup management or automated scheduling of backups across all specified services.

answers.text: Use AWS Systems Manager State Manager to manage the configuration and monitoring of backup tasks.
answers.explanation: AWS Systems Manager State Manager is a configuration management service, not a dedicated backup service. While it can be used to automate tasks like running backup scripts, it doesn't provide the centralized management and automation capabilities offered by AWS Backup for various data sources.

overall_explanation: AWS Backup is the ideal solution because it's an AWS-native service designed for centralized management and automation of backups for various AWS services, including EC2, RDS, and DynamoDB. It provides a single console to configure, manage, and monitor backups, fulfilling the organization's requirements to move away from custom scripts and streamline their backup processes. The other options either introduce third-party dependencies or are not specifically designed for centralized backup management.

question: A company has a production web application where users upload documents through a web interface or a mobile app. Due to a new regulatory requirement, new documents must not be modified or deleted after they are stored. Which solution should a solutions architect implement to meet this requirement?

answers.text: Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning and S3 Object Lock enabled.
answers.explanation: S3 Versioning preserves every version of a document, preventing accidental or intentional modifications/deletions. S3 Object Lock allows setting a retention period or legal hold on objects, making them immutable, satisfying the regulatory requirement.

answers.text: Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to archive the documents periodically.
answers.explanation: Configuring an S3 Lifecycle policy to archive documents periodically does not guarantee the prevention of document modification or deletion after they are stored. Archiving is for cost optimization, not immutability.

answers.text: Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning enabled. Configure an ACL to restrict all access to read-only.
answers.explanation: Enabling S3 Versioning alone does not prevent modifications or deletions of objects. Configuring an ACL does not guarantee the prevention of modifications or deletions by authorized users with sufficient permissions.

answers.text: Store the uploaded documents on an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Access the data by mounting the volume in read-only mode.
answers.explanation: Using EFS does not prevent modifications or deletions of the documents by users or processes with write permissions. Mounting in read-only mode relies on the application to enforce restrictions, which is not as robust as using S3 Object Lock.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to use Amazon S3 with S3 Versioning and S3 Object Lock. S3 Versioning ensures that all versions of an object are retained, while S3 Object Lock prevents objects from being overwritten or deleted for a specified period or indefinitely using a WORM (Write Once Read Many) model. This combination satisfies the regulatory requirement of preventing modifications and deletions.

question: A company aims to establish a comprehensive map of its IT infrastructure to effectively identify and enforce policies on resources that present security vulnerabilities. The security team requires the ability to query this IT infrastructure map and promptly detect security risks with minimal administrative effort. Which solution best fulfills these requirements while minimizing operational overhead?

answers.text: Use Amazon RDS to store the data. Use SQL to query the data to identify security risks.
answers.explanation: Amazon RDS is a relational database service, which is not optimized for graph data representing relationships between resources in an IT infrastructure. SQL queries would be complex and inefficient for traversing these relationships.

answers.text: Use Amazon Neptune to store the data. Use SPARQL to query the data to identify security risks.
answers.explanation: Amazon Neptune is a graph database service ideal for storing and querying interconnected data, such as an IT infrastructure map. SPARQL is a query language designed for graph databases, enabling efficient identification of security risks by traversing relationships.

answers.text: Use Amazon Redshift to store the data. Use SQL to query the data to identify security risks.
answers.explanation: Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse service optimized for analytical workloads. It is not designed for real-time querying of graph data representing an IT infrastructure map. SQL queries would be complex and inefficient.

answers.text: Use Amazon DynamoDB to store the data. Use PartiQL to query the data to identify security risks.
answers.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL database service. While PartiQL allows SQL-compatible queries, it is not optimized for traversing complex relationships in graph data. Managing relationships would be more complex compared to a graph database.

overall_explanation: Amazon Neptune is the best solution because it's a graph database specifically designed for storing and querying relationship-heavy data like IT infrastructure maps. SPARQL is the standard query language for graph databases, making it efficient for identifying security risks based on resource relationships. This combination results in the least operational overhead for the given requirements.

question: A large company requires a cost-effective solution to provide its globally located developers with separate, limited-size, managed PostgreSQL databases for development purposes. These databases will have low volume and developers need them only when actively working. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.text: Give the developers the ability to launch separate Amazon Aurora instances. Set up a process to shut down Aurora instances at the end of the workday and to start Aurora instances at the beginning of the next workday.
answers.explanation: This option is more expensive than a serverless solution because Amazon Aurora instances use On- Demand or Reserved instances.

answers.text: Develop an AWS Service Catalog product that enforces size restrictions for launching Amazon Aurora instances. Give the developers access to launch the product when they need a development database.
answers.explanation: This option is more expensive than a serverless solution because Amazon Aurora instances use On- Demand or Reserved instances.

answers.text: Create an Amazon Aurora Serverless cluster. Develop an AWS Service Catalog product to launch databases in the cluster with the default capacity settings. Grant the developers access to the product.
answers.explanation: Amazon Aurora Serverless automatically starts up, shuts down, and scales capacity based on application needs. You only pay for consumed capacity, making it cost-effective. AWS Service Catalog provides a catalog of services that users can utilize within permitted configurations.

answers.text: Monitor AWS Trusted Advisor checks for idle Amazon RDS databases. Create a process to terminate identified idle RDS databases.
answers.explanation: This option involves manual monitoring and termination, introducing operational overhead and potentially causing delays in database availability for developers. Furthermore, RDS instances are more expensive than Aurora Serverless.

overall_explanation: Amazon Aurora Serverless combined with AWS Service Catalog is the most cost-effective solution. Aurora Serverless automatically scales and shuts down, reducing costs. AWS Service Catalog allows developers to easily access the required resources within predefined configurations. Using Aurora or RDS instances involve on-demand or reserved instances. Hence, option A, B and D are less cost-effective. Option C provides an automated and cost optimized solution.

question: A company hosts a content management system (CMS) on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). These instances reside within an Auto Scaling group spanning multiple Availability Zones. Users frequently update website content, requiring all EC2 instances to maintain synchronized assets with minimal delay. What solution ensures efficient and real- time content sharing across all EC2 instances with the least possible lag time?

answers.text: Update the EC2 user data in the Auto Scaling group lifecycle policy to copy website assets from the newest EC2 instance. Configure the ALB to direct changes only to this instance.
answers.explanation: This solution has significant lag time and potential inconsistencies as the content is only synchronized during new instance launches. It does not address ongoing updates.

answers.text: Copy the website assets to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Configure each EC2 instance to mount the EFS file system locally and reference the assets within.
answers.explanation: Amazon EFS provides a shared file system accessible by all EC2 instances. This allows for real-time content updates to be immediately available across all instances, fulfilling the requirement.

answers.text: Copy website assets to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure each EC2 instance to download assets from S3 to an attached Amazon EBS volume. Use a scheduled S3 sync command to maintain updates.
answers.explanation: Using S3 and a sync command introduces significant delay and complexity, as content is only updated hourly, failing to meet the near real-time requirement. EBS volumes are also not inherently shared between instances.

answers.text: Restore an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshot with website assets. Attach the EBS snapshot as a secondary EBS volume to new EC2 instances. Configure the website application to reference the assets on this volume.
answers.explanation: This approach only provides the initial website data and doesn't account for updates. EBS snapshots aren't designed for real-time content sharing, and each instance would have a static copy of the data.

overall_explanation: Amazon EFS (Elastic File System) is the ideal solution for sharing website assets across multiple EC2 instances in real-time. By mounting the EFS file system on each instance, content updates are immediately reflected across all instances, ensuring minimal lag time and data consistency. Using user data to copy content or using S3 sync methods introduces significant delays and is not suitable for a dynamic content management system requiring real-time updates. Therefore, EFS ensures the content is up-to-date and readily available for all EC2 instances without significant latency.

question: A company's web application consists of multiple Amazon EC2 instances that run behind an Application Load Balancer in a VPC. An Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance contains the data. The company needs the ability to automatically detect and respond to suspicious or unexpected behavior in its AWS environment. The company already has added AWS WAF to its architecture. What should a solutions architect do next to protect against threats?

answers.text: Use Amazon GuardDuty to perform threat detection. Configure Amazon EventBridge to filter for GuardDuty findings and to invoke an AWS Lambda function to adjust the AWS WAF rules.
answers.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service that continuously monitors for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior across your AWS environment. EventBridge can be used to trigger Lambda functions based on GuardDuty findings to update WAF rules automatically.

answers.text: Use AWS Firewall Manager to perform threat detection. Configure Amazon EventBridge to filter for Firewall Manager findings and to invoke an AWS Lambda function to adjust the AWS WAF web ACL.
answers.explanation: AWS Firewall Manager is primarily used for managing AWS WAF rules across multiple accounts and resources. While it provides centralized management, GuardDuty is a more appropriate service for threat detection.

answers.text: Use Amazon Inspector to perform threat detection and to update the AWS WAF rules. Create a VPC network ACL to limit access to the web application.
answers.explanation: Amazon Inspector is a vulnerability management service that assesses EC2 instances and container images for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure. It does not directly detect threats like GuardDuty does, nor does it directly integrate with WAF for dynamic rule updates. While network ACLs enhance security, they are not the primary solution for threat detection.

answers.text: Use Amazon Macie to perform threat detection and to update the AWS WAF rules. Create a VPC network ACL to limit access to the web application.
answers.explanation: Amazon Macie is a data security and privacy service that uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and protect sensitive data in AWS. It is not primarily designed for general threat detection or integration with WAF.

overall_explanation: Amazon GuardDuty is designed for threat detection, continuously monitoring for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior. Configuring Amazon EventBridge to react to GuardDuty findings and trigger a Lambda function to adjust AWS WAF rules provides an automated response to identified threats.

question: A company is planning to run a group of Amazon EC2 instances that connect to an Amazon Aurora database. The company has built an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy the EC2 instances and the Aurora DB cluster. The company wants to allow the instances to authenticate to the database in a secure way, and does not want to maintain static database credentials. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

answers.text: Create a database user with a user name and password. Add parameters for the database user name and password to the CloudFormation template. Pass the parameters to the EC2 instances when the instances are launched.
answers.explanation: This solution requires managing credentials and is not the least operational effort.

answers.text: Create a database user with a user name and password. Store the user name and password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Configure the EC2 instances to retrieve the database credentials from Parameter Store.
answers.explanation: This solution still requires managing credentials, although stored securely, and is not the least operational effort.

answers.text: Configure the DB cluster to use IAM database authentication. Create a database user to use with IAM authentication. Associate a role with the EC2 instances to allow applications on the instances to access the database.
answers.explanation: This is the correct answer. Using IAM database authentication and associating a role with the EC2 instances is the least operational effort. It avoids managing database passwords.

answers.text: Configure the DB cluster to use IAM database authentication with an IAM user. Create a database user that has a name that matches the IAM user. Associate the IAM user with the EC2 instances to allow applications on the instances to access the database.
answers.explanation: You cannot directly associate an IAM user with EC2 instances. You associate an IAM role, making this option incorrect.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to configure IAM database authentication for the Aurora cluster and associate an IAM role with the EC2 instances. This allows the instances to authenticate to the database without needing to store or manage database credentials. This is the least operational effort because it leverages IAM roles for authentication, eliminating the need for static credentials. IAM roles can be easily managed and rotated by AWS and don't require manual rotation or management.

question: A company wants to configure its Amazon CloudFront distribution to use SSL/TLS certificates with a custom domain name. The company wants to deploy the certificate without incurring additional costs. Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.text: Request an Amazon issued private certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region.
answers.explanation: Private certificates are generally used for internal resources and are not suitable for CloudFront distributions with custom domain names. Also, Private CA is not free.

answers.text: Request an Amazon issued private certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-west-1 Region.
answers.explanation: Private certificates are generally used for internal resources and are not suitable for CloudFront distributions with custom domain names. ACM certificates for CloudFront must be requested in the us-east-1 Region. Also, Private CA is not free.

answers.text: Request an Amazon issued public certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region.
answers.explanation: ACM provides free public SSL/TLS certificates. To use an ACM certificate with CloudFront, it must be requested in the US East (N. Virginia) Region (us-east-1).

answers.text: Request an Amazon issued public certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-west-1 Region.
answers.explanation: While public certificates from ACM are free, ACM certificates for CloudFront must be requested in the us-east-1 Region.

overall_explanation: Public SSL/TLS certificates provisioned through AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) are free. To use an ACM certificate with CloudFront, you must request it in the US East (N. Virginia) Region (us-east-1). Therefore, requesting an Amazon issued public certificate from ACM in us-east-1 is the correct solution.

question: A company stores operations data in an Amazon S3 bucket. For an annual audit, an external consultant requires access to an annual report stored in the bucket for 7 days. The company needs a solution that grants the consultant access only to the specific report with the highest operational efficiency. Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.text: Create a new S3 bucket configured to host a public static website. Migrate the report to the new bucket and share the website URL with the consultant.
answers.explanation: Creating a new bucket and migrating the report is operationally inefficient and unnecessarily exposes the report via a public website.

answers.text: Enable public access to the entire S3 bucket for 7 days. Remove public access when the consultant completes the audit.
answers.explanation: Enabling public access to the entire bucket is a security risk and grants the consultant more access than necessary.

answers.text: Create a new IAM user with access to the report in the S3 bucket. Provide the access keys to the consultant. Revoke the access keys after 7 days.
answers.explanation: Creating and managing an IAM user adds unnecessary operational overhead compared to using a presigned URL.

answers.text: Generate a presigned URL that provides the required access to the specific report in the S3 bucket. Share the presigned URL with the consultant.
answers.explanation: Presigned URLs provide secure, temporary access to specific S3 objects without requiring IAM user creation or broad public access.

overall_explanation: A presigned URL provides temporary, secure access to a specific object in S3. It is the most operationally efficient solution because it avoids creating new IAM users or modifying bucket-level permissions. The consultant gains access only to the required report for the specified duration (7 days) without any ongoing management overhead. Presigned URLs are ideal for providing short-term access to private objects in S3 by appending an AWS Access Key, expiration time, and Sigv4 signature as query parameters to the S3 object.

question: A company is planning to run a High Performance Computing (HPC) workload on Amazon EC2 instances. The HPC workload demands low-latency network performance and high network throughput for tightly coupled node-to-node communication. Which of the following solutions will best satisfy these requirements?

answers.text: Configure the EC2 instances to be part of a cluster placement group.
answers.explanation: Cluster placement groups provide low latency and high network throughput which are essential for tightly coupled node-to-node communication in HPC workloads.

answers.text: Launch the EC2 instances with Dedicated Instance tenancy.
answers.explanation: Dedicated Instance tenancy ensures that the instances run on dedicated hardware, but it does not directly address the need for low-latency or high-throughput networking.

answers.text: Launch the EC2 instances as Spot Instances.
answers.explanation: Spot Instances offer cost savings, but they are subject to interruption and do not guarantee low latency or high network throughput.

answers.text: Configure an On-Demand Capacity Reservation when the EC2 instances are launched.
answers.explanation: On-Demand Capacity Reservations guarantee the availability of EC2 capacity but do not inherently provide low-latency or high-throughput networking.

overall_explanation: Cluster placement groups are designed to provide low-latency and high-bandwidth connectivity between instances within the group, which is essential for HPC workloads that require tightly coupled node-to-node communication. Dedicated Instances offer dedicated hardware, but do not focus on low latency and high throughput. Spot Instances are about pricing. On-Demand Capacity Reservations are for ensuring capacity is available, but do not ensure high networking performance.

question: A company has primary and secondary data centers that are 500 miles (804.7 km) apart and interconnected with high-speed fiber-optic cable. The company requires a highly available and secure network connection between its data centers and a VPC on AWS for a mission-critical workload. To ensure maximum resiliency, which connectivity solution should a solutions architect recommend?

answers.text: Two AWS Direct Connect connections from the primary data center terminating at two Direct Connect locations on two separate devices.
answers.explanation: This option only provides redundancy for the primary data center, not both. It doesn't protect against failure in the secondary data center.

answers.text: A single AWS Direct Connect connection from each of the primary and secondary data centers terminating at one Direct Connect location on the same device.
answers.explanation: This option introduces a single point of failure at the Direct Connect location and device.

answers.text: Two AWS Direct Connect connections from each of the primary and secondary data centers terminating at two Direct Connect locations on two separate devices.
answers.explanation: This option provides maximum redundancy by having multiple connections from both data centers terminating at different Direct Connect locations on separate devices. This protects against data center failure, connection failure, and Direct Connect location/device failure.

answers.text: A single AWS Direct Connect connection from each of the primary and secondary data centers terminating at one Direct Connect location on two separate devices.
answers.explanation: While this provides some redundancy with two separate devices, it introduces a single point of failure at the Direct Connect location. If the Direct Connect location experiences issues, connectivity from both data centers will be impacted.

overall_explanation: The most resilient solution is to have two independent Direct Connect connections from each data center, terminating at two different Direct Connect locations on separate devices. This setup provides redundancy against data center failures, connection failures, and Direct Connect location/device failures. Option C ensures maximum availability for the mission-critical workload.

question: A company runs several Amazon RDS for Oracle On-Demand DB instances that have high utilization. The RDS DB instances run in member accounts that are in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company's finance team has access to the organization's management account and member accounts. The finance team wants to find ways to optimize costs by using AWS Trusted Advisor. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.text: Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations in the management account.
answers.explanation: Trusted Advisor in the management account doesn't provide insights for member accounts unless the organizational view is enabled.

answers.text: Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations in the member accounts where the RDS DB instances are running.
answers.explanation: The finance team needs access to each member account to review Trusted Advisor recommendations directly, which might be operationally complex.

answers.text: Review the Trusted Advisor checks for Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization.
answers.explanation: Given the high utilization of On-Demand instances, reviewing the Reserved Instance Optimization checks is crucial to identify potential cost savings by switching to Reserved Instances.

answers.text: Review the Trusted Advisor checks for Amazon RDS Idle DB Instances.
answers.explanation: Because the RDS instances have high utilization, this check is less relevant.

answers.text: Review the Trusted Advisor checks for compute optimization. Crosscheck the results by using AWS Compute Optimizer.
answers.explanation: The question explicitly mentions RDS DB instances and optimizing their costs. Compute Optimizer primarily focuses on EC2 instances and not RDS.

overall_explanation: The best approach is to review the Trusted Advisor recommendations in the member accounts directly to get specific insights for each RDS instance. Additionally, because the instances have high utilization and are On-Demand, checking the Reserved Instance Optimization is a must to save money. Options A, D and E are less relevant or incorrect. A is not applicable as Trusted Advisor is account specific unless organizational view is enabled, D is wrong as the instances are highly utilized, E is irrelevant as it is specific to compute optimization and not RDS.

question: A company has several web servers that need to frequently access a common Amazon RDS MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance. The company wants a secure method for the web servers to connect to the database while meeting a security requirement to rotate user credentials frequently. Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.text: Store the database user credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Grant the necessary IAM permissions to allow the web servers to access AWS Secrets Manager.
answers.explanation: Secrets Manager allows secure storage and automatic rotation of credentials, and IAM permissions grant access to the web servers.

answers.text: Store the database user credentials in AWS Systems Manager OpsCenter. Grant the necessary IAM permissions to allow the web servers to access OpsCenter.
answers.explanation: SSM OpsCenter is not designed for storing and rotating database credentials; it's primarily for operational issue management.

answers.text: Store the database user credentials in a secure Amazon S3 bucket. Grant the necessary IAM permissions to allow the web servers to retrieve credentials and access the database.
answers.explanation: Storing credentials in S3 lacks the features and security controls of AWS Secrets Manager for secure storage and rotation.

answers.text: Store the database user credentials in files encrypted with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) on the web server file system. The web server should be able to decrypt the files and access the database.
answers.explanation: Managing credentials directly on web servers, even with KMS, introduces complexities and security risks for rotation and scaling.

overall_explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is designed for storing and managing secrets such as database credentials. It provides automated secret rotation and IAM integration for secure access, meeting the requirements for secure access and frequent credential rotation. Storing credentials on the web servers or in S3 is less secure and harder to manage. OpsCenter is for operational issue management, not credential storage.

question: A solutions architect is designing an application that will run on Amazon EC2 instances within private subnets across multiple Availability Zones in a VPC. These EC2 instances need to frequently access large files containing confidential data stored in Amazon S3 buckets for processing. To minimize data transfer costs and ensure secure access to S3, what network architecture should the solutions architect implement?

answers.text: Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC. In the route tables for the private subnets, add an entry for the gateway endpoint.
answers.explanation: A gateway endpoint for S3 provides cost-effective and secure access to S3 from private subnets without traversing the internet. It keeps traffic within the AWS network, thus minimizing data transfer costs and improving security.

answers.text: Create a single NAT gateway in a public subnet. In the route tables for the private subnets, add a default route that points to the NAT gateway.
answers.explanation: Using a NAT gateway allows the EC2 instances to access the internet, including S3, but it incurs data transfer costs and requires the traffic to traverse the internet, which is less secure.

answers.text: Create an AWS PrivateLink interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC. In the route tables for the private subnets, add an entry for the interface endpoint.
answers.explanation: While AWS PrivateLink provides secure, private connectivity to AWS services, it is generally more expensive than using a gateway endpoint for S3 access and is more suitable when you need to access the S3 API rather than direct object access.

answers.text: Create one NAT gateway for each Availability Zone in public subnets. In each of the route tables for the private subnets, add a default route that points to the NAT gateway in the same Availability Zone.
answers.explanation: Using multiple NAT gateways improves availability but does not address the requirement of minimizing data transfer costs and is also more expensive than using gateway endpoints. Also, the traffic will traverse internet to reach S3.

overall_explanation: The most cost-effective and secure solution is to create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC. This allows the EC2 instances in private subnets to access S3 directly without incurring data transfer costs associated with NAT gateways or exposing the traffic to the internet. Adding an entry for the gateway endpoint in the route tables ensures that traffic destined for S3 is routed through the endpoint.

question: A company is migrating its on-premises MySQL database to AWS. The database frequently receives data imports from a client application, resulting in a high volume of write operations. The company is concerned about potential performance impacts on the application due to this traffic. How should a solutions architect design the architecture on AWS to address these concerns?

answers.text: Provision an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with Provisioned IOPS SSD storage. Monitor write operation metrics by using Amazon CloudWatch. Adjust the provisioned IOPS if necessary.
answers.explanation: Provisioned IOPS storage is designed for I/O-intensive workloads like this. CloudWatch monitoring allows for proactive adjustments to maintain performance.

answers.text: Provision an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with General Purpose SSD storage. Place an Amazon ElastiCache cluster in front of the DB instance. Configure the application to query ElastiCache instead.
answers.explanation: ElastiCache is primarily for read caching. While it can reduce read load, it doesn't directly address high write volume and introduces complexity.

answers.text: Provision an Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) instance with a memory optimized instance type. Monitor Amazon CloudWatch for performance- related issues. Change the instance class if necessary.
answers.explanation: Changing the database engine to DocumentDB is not recommended if the current database is MySQL and is working fine. This option is also not optimized to support High IOPS.

answers.text: Provision an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system in General Purpose performance mode. Monitor Amazon CloudWatch for IOPS bottlenecks. Change to Provisioned Throughput performance mode if necessary.
answers.explanation: EFS is a file storage service and not suitable as a database.

overall_explanation: Given the high volume of write operations, the most effective solution is to use Amazon RDS for MySQL with Provisioned IOPS SSD storage. This option is optimized for I/O- intensive workloads. Monitoring with CloudWatch ensures that the provisioned IOPS can be adjusted as needed to maintain optimal performance. Using ElastiCache for write-heavy operations is not the most efficient approach. Switching to Amazon DocumentDB without a clear requirement is not recommended, and EFS is not an appropriate storage solution for a relational database.

question: A company runs an application in the AWS Cloud that generates sensitive archival data files. The company wants to rearchitect the application's data storage. The company wants to encrypt the data files and to ensure that third parties do not have access to the data *before* the data is encrypted and sent to AWS. The company has already created an Amazon S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.text: Configure the S3 bucket to use client-side encryption with an Amazon S3 managed encryption key. Configure the application to use the S3 bucket to store the archival files.
answers.explanation: This option uses client-side encryption, but with an S3-managed key, which means the encryption happens on the server side, not before the data reaches AWS. Thus, it does not satisfy the requirement that third parties should not be able to access the unencrypted data before it reaches AWS.

answers.text: Configure the S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Configure the application to use the S3 bucket to store the archival files.
answers.explanation: Server-side encryption encrypts the data *after* it is uploaded to S3. The requirement is to encrypt the data *before* sending it to AWS.

answers.text: Configure the S3 bucket to use dual-layer server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Configure the application to use the S3 bucket to store the archival files.
answers.explanation: Dual-layer server-side encryption, like regular server-side encryption, encrypts the data *after* it is uploaded to S3. The requirement is to encrypt the data *before* sending it to AWS.

answers.text: Configure the application to use client-side encryption with a key stored in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Configure the application to store the archival files in the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: This option uses client-side encryption. The application encrypts the data before it is sent to S3. The encryption key is stored and managed by AWS KMS. This ensures that third parties do not have access to the data before it reaches AWS.

overall_explanation: The requirement is to ensure that the data is encrypted *before* it is sent to AWS to prevent third-party access. Only client-side encryption satisfies this requirement. Server- side encryption encrypts the data after it reaches AWS. Using client-side encryption with a key stored in AWS KMS fulfills the requirement.

question: A company uses Amazon RDS with default backup settings for its database tier. The company needs to make a daily backup of the database to meet regulatory requirements. The company must retain the backups for 30 days. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.text: Write an AWS Lambda function to create an RDS snapshot every day.
answers.explanation: This option requires writing and maintaining a Lambda function, increasing operational overhead.

answers.text: Modify the RDS database to have a retention period of 30 days for automated backups.
answers.explanation: Amazon RDS performs a full daily backup of your data during a backup window that you define when you create the DB instance. You can configure a retention period of up to 35 days for the automated backup, so simply modifying the retention period is the easiest and least overhead approach.

answers.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Maintenance Windows to modify the RDS backup retention period.
answers.explanation: While Systems Manager Maintenance Windows can automate tasks, it's an unnecessarily complex solution for simply changing the RDS backup retention period.

answers.text: Create a manual snapshot every day by using the AWS CLI. Modify the RDS backup retention period.
answers.explanation: Creating daily manual snapshots using the AWS CLI adds significant operational overhead. Additionally, it's not necessary to *also* modify the RDS backup retention period, which is confusing, and already handled automatically by the RDS service.

overall_explanation: Amazon RDS automatically performs a full daily snapshot of your data during a backup window that you define when you create the DB instance. You can configure a retention period of up to 35 days for the automated backup. Therefore, modifying the RDS database to have a retention period of 30 days for automated backups provides the required functionality with the least operational overhead.

question: A company runs its application on AWS using an Amazon Aurora DB cluster. During peak hours, numerous users access and read data, leading to degraded write query performance. The company aims to improve application scalability to handle these peak demands cost-effectively. Which solution BEST addresses these requirements?

answers.text: Create a second Aurora DB cluster. Configure a copy job to replicate the user data to the new database. Update the application to use the second database for read operations.
answers.explanation: Creating a second full Aurora cluster and replicating data is a costly solution. Read replicas are more cost-effective for read scaling.

answers.text: Create an Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster in front of the existing Aurora DB cluster. Update the application to use the DAX cluster for read-only queries, writing data directly to the Aurora DB cluster.
answers.explanation: DAX is designed for DynamoDB, not Aurora. It cannot be used to cache reads for Aurora.

answers.text: Create an Aurora read replica within the existing Aurora DB cluster. Update the application to use the replica endpoint for read-only queries and the cluster endpoint for write queries.
answers.explanation: This is the most cost-effective solution. Read replicas offload read operations from the primary instance, improving write performance. They are also purpose-built for Aurora, ensuring compatibility and optimal performance.

answers.text: Create an Amazon Redshift cluster. Copy the user data to the Redshift cluster. Update the application to connect to the Redshift cluster and perform read-only queries.
answers.explanation: Redshift is a data warehouse solution and is not ideal for transactional read operations of an application. It's better suited for analytics and reporting.

overall_explanation: Creating an Aurora read replica (Option C) is the MOST cost-effective solution. It allows you to offload read queries from the primary database instance, thus improving write performance during peak usage. Using read replicas is the recommended approach for scaling read capacity in Aurora clusters without incurring the high costs of creating separate full clusters (Option A) or misusing services like DAX (designed for DynamoDB (Option B) ) or Redshift (designed for data warehousing (Option D)).

question: A company's near-real-time streaming application is running on AWS. As the data is ingested, a job runs on the data and takes 30 minutes to complete. The workload frequently experiences high latency due to large amounts of incoming data. A solutions architect needs to design a scalable and serverless solution to enhance performance. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take? (Choose two.)

answers.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to ingest the data.
answers.explanation: Kinesis Data Firehose is designed for ingesting streaming data into AWS data stores and analytics services.

answers.text: Use AWS Lambda with AWS Step Functions to process the data.
answers.explanation: Lambda functions have a maximum execution time of 15 minutes, which is insufficient for the 30- minute job. Step Functions manages workflows but doesn't solve the Lambda execution time limitation.

answers.text: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to ingest the data.
answers.explanation: AWS DMS is for database migrations, not general streaming data ingestion.

answers.text: Use Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to process the data.
answers.explanation: While EC2 with Auto Scaling can provide scalability, it is not a serverless solution.

answers.text: Use AWS Fargate with Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to process the data.
answers.explanation: AWS Fargate with ECS allows you to run containers without managing servers, offering a scalable and serverless solution capable of running longer-duration jobs.

overall_explanation: To build a scalable and serverless solution, Kinesis Data Firehose is used for ingesting the streaming data (Option A). Since the job takes 30 minutes, Lambda is not suitable as it has a 15-minute execution time limit. ECS with Fargate provides a serverless compute environment to run the 30-minute job (Option E).

question: A company runs a web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC. The application needs to write sensitive data to an Amazon S3 bucket. The data cannot be sent over the public internet. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.text: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Create a route in the VPC route table to the endpoint.
answers.explanation: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 allows traffic to stay within the AWS network and does not traverse the public internet. The route table entry directs traffic destined for S3 to the endpoint.

answers.text: Create an internal Network Load Balancer that has the S3 bucket as the target.
answers.explanation: An internal Network Load Balancer cannot target an S3 bucket directly. S3 is not a compute instance or IP address that can be targeted by an NLB.

answers.text: Deploy the S3 bucket inside the VPC. Create a route in the VPC route table to the bucket.
answers.explanation: It's not possible to deploy an S3 bucket directly inside a VPC. S3 is a service that resides outside of your VPC, but can be accessed securely from within it.

answers.text: Create an AWS Direct Connect connection between the VPC and an S3 regional endpoint.
answers.explanation: While Direct Connect provides a dedicated network connection to AWS, it doesn't inherently prevent data from traversing the public internet unless combined with private VIF and appropriate routing. A VPC endpoint is a more direct and cost-effective solution for keeping S3 traffic within the AWS network.

overall_explanation: A gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 is the correct solution because it allows the EC2 instances in the VPC to access S3 without traversing the public internet. The endpoint creates a route within the VPC's network to S3. The other options are incorrect because they either don't prevent internet traffic, can't be implemented, or are more complex than necessary. Direct connect is a solution for hybrid environment.

question: A company runs its production workload on Amazon EC2 instances with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. A solutions architect needs to analyze the current EBS volume cost and to recommend optimizations. The recommendations need to include estimated monthly saving opportunities. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.text: Use Amazon Inspector reporting to generate EBS volume recommendations for optimization.
answers.explanation: Amazon Inspector is a vulnerability management service and does not provide EBS volume cost analysis or optimization recommendations.

answers.text: Use AWS Systems Manager reporting to determine EBS volume recommendations for optimization.
answers.explanation: AWS Systems Manager provides operational insights and automation capabilities, but it's not the primary service for EBS cost optimization recommendations.

answers.text: Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics reporting to determine EBS volume recommendations for optimization.
answers.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch provides metrics and monitoring, but requires manual analysis and doesn't directly generate optimization recommendations with cost savings estimates.

answers.text: Use AWS Compute Optimizer to generate EBS volume recommendations for optimization.
answers.explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer analyzes the utilization metrics of your AWS resources, including EBS volumes, and provides recommendations to optimize performance and reduce costs, including estimated monthly savings.

overall_explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer provides recommendations to optimize your use of AWS resources, including EC2 instances and EBS volumes. It helps avoid over-provisioning and under-provisioning based on your utilization data and can estimate monthly saving opportunities. Therefore, it is the most appropriate solution for analyzing EBS volume costs and recommending optimizations.

question: A company needs to enhance its e-commerce order-processing application, currently deployed on AWS. The application must guarantee that each order is processed exactly once and maintain a positive customer experience, even during unpredictable traffic surges. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.text: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Place all orders into the SQS queue. Configure an AWS Lambda function as the target to process the orders.
answers.explanation: Using an SQS FIFO queue guarantees that messages (orders) are processed exactly once, and in the order they were received. Lambda can scale to handle unpredictable traffic surges.

answers.text: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) standard topic. Publish all orders to the SNS standard topic. Configure the application as a notification target.
answers.explanation: SNS standard topics do not guarantee message order or exactly-once processing. Messages could be lost or delivered more than once, which violates the requirements.

answers.text: Create a flow by using Amazon AppFlow. Send the orders to the flow. Configure an AWS Lambda function as the target to process the orders.
answers.explanation: Amazon AppFlow is designed to transfer data between AWS services and SaaS applications. It's not primarily designed for guaranteeing exactly-once processing of e-commerce orders in a queueing scenario.

answers.text: Configure AWS X-Ray in the application to track the order requests. Configure the application to process the orders by pulling the orders from Amazon CloudWatch.
answers.explanation: AWS X-Ray is for tracing and debugging distributed applications. CloudWatch is primarily for monitoring and logging. Neither service provides the queueing and exactly-once processing required.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to use an Amazon SQS FIFO queue. FIFO queues guarantee that each message (order) is processed exactly once, and in the same order it was sent. Utilizing an AWS Lambda function as a consumer for the SQS queue provides scalability to handle unpredictable traffic surges without affecting the customer experience.

question: A company hosts an application on AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by an Amazon API Gateway API. The Lambda functions save customer data to an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. Whenever the company upgrades the database, the Lambda functions fail to establish database connections until the upgrade is complete, resulting in customer data not being recorded for some events. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that stores customer data created during database upgrades. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.text: Provision an Amazon RDS Proxy to sit between the Lambda functions and the database. Configure the Lambda functions to connect to the RDS Proxy.
answers.explanation: RDS Proxy primarily helps manage database connections but does not inherently store data during outages or upgrades. While it can reduce failover times, it doesn't guarantee data persistence during prolonged database unavailability.

answers.text: Increase the run time of the Lambda functions to the maximum. Create a retry mechanism in the code that stores the customer data in the database.
answers.explanation: Increasing Lambda runtime and adding retry logic might help with transient errors, but it's insufficient if the database upgrade duration exceeds Lambda's maximum execution time. Data could still be lost.

answers.text: Persist the customer data to Lambda local storage. Configure new Lambda functions to scan the local storage to save the customer data to the database.
answers.explanation: Lambda local storage is ephemeral and is not guaranteed to persist across invocations. Relying on it for durable storage is unreliable and not suitable for this scenario.

answers.text: Store the customer data in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Create a new Lambda function that polls the queue and stores the customer data in the database.
answers.explanation: Using an SQS FIFO queue provides a reliable and durable buffer for customer data during database upgrades. A separate Lambda function can then poll the queue and process the data once the database is available, ensuring no data loss.

overall_explanation: The most effective solution is to use an Amazon SQS FIFO queue to store the data during database upgrades. This decouples the data ingestion from the database's availability. A separate Lambda function can then process the queue and reliably store the data into the database once it is back online. RDS Proxy (Option A) doesn't store data. Increasing Lambda runtime (Option B) is not reliable for longer outages. Lambda local storage (Option C) is ephemeral.

question: A company has two AWS accounts: Production and Development. The company needs to push code changes in the Development account to the Production account. During the alpha phase, only two senior developers on the development team require access to the Production account. In the beta phase, more developers will need access to perform testing. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.text: Create two policy documents by using the AWS Management Console in each account. Assign the policy to developers who need access.
answers.explanation: This option doesn't establish secure cross-account access. Policies created within each account only manage permissions within that account, not across accounts.

answers.text: Create an IAM role in the Development account. Grant the IAM role access to the Production account. Allow developers to assume the role.
answers.explanation: It's best practice to create IAM roles in the account being accessed (Production). This approach centralizes permission management in the Production account.

answers.text: Create an IAM role in the Production account. Define a trust policy that specifies the Development account. Allow developers to assume the role.
answers.explanation: This is the recommended approach. An IAM role in the Production account with a trust relationship to the Development account allows developers in the Development account to assume the role and gain temporary access to Production resources.

answers.text: Create an IAM group in the Production account. Add the group as a principal in a trust policy that specifies the Production account. Add developers to the group.
answers.explanation: IAM groups cannot be directly used as principals in trust policies for cross-account access. Trust policies define which accounts or entities are allowed to assume the role.

overall_explanation: Creating an IAM role in the Production account with a trust policy that specifies the Development account is the correct approach. This allows developers in the Development account to assume the role in Production and gain temporary access. In the alpha phase, the trust policy will allow only the two senior developers to assume the role. Later in the beta phase, more developers can be granted access through the role's trust policy. This approach facilitates secure, cross-account access while maintaining control over who has access to the Production environment. Groups can't be used in a trust policy. Option B violates AWS best practices by creating the IAM role in the development account.

question: A company wants to restrict access to the content of its web application. The company needs to protect the content by using authorization techniques that are available on AWS. The company also wants to implement a serverless architecture for authorization and authentication that has low login latency. The solution must integrate with the web application and serve web content globally. The application currently has a small user base, but the company expects the application's user base to increase. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.text: Configure Amazon Cognito for authentication. Implement Lambda@Edge for authorization. Configure Amazon CloudFront to serve the web application globally.
answers.explanation: This solution uses Cognito for authentication, providing a scalable and managed user directory. Lambda@Edge allows for authorization logic to be executed at the edge, reducing latency and improving performance globally via CloudFront.

answers.text: Configure AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Implement AWS Lambda for authorization. Use an Application Load Balancer to serve the web application globally.
answers.explanation: Using Active Directory adds unnecessary complexity and management overhead, and doesn't directly address the requirement for global content delivery. While Lambda can perform authorization, it won't be as performant as Lambda@Edge for global authorization and an ALB doesn't inherently provide global content delivery.

answers.text: Configure Amazon Cognito for authentication. Implement AWS Lambda for authorization. Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration to serve the web application globally.
answers.explanation: S3 Transfer Acceleration improves upload speeds to S3, not global content delivery for a web application. While Cognito is suitable for authentication and Lambda can do authorization, S3 Transfer Acceleration is not correct here.

answers.text: Configure AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Implement Lambda@Edge for authorization. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to serve the web application globally.
answers.explanation: Active Directory adds unnecessary complexity and management overhead. Elastic Beanstalk provides a platform for deploying web applications but doesn't inherently provide global content delivery or the optimal architecture for it.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to use Amazon Cognito for authentication and Lambda@Edge for authorization with Amazon CloudFront serving the web application globally. Cognito provides a managed authentication service. Lambda@Edge allows you to execute authorization logic at the edge, closer to the user, providing low latency and enhanced security. CloudFront ensures the content is served globally and efficiently.

question: A development team uses multiple AWS accounts for their development, staging, and production environments. Team members have been launching large Amazon EC2 instances that are often underutilized. A solutions architect needs to prevent the launching of large EC2 instances across all AWS accounts with the least operational overhead. What approach should the solutions architect take?

answers.text: Update the IAM policies to deny the launch of large EC2 instances. Apply the policies to all users in each account.
answers.explanation: Updating IAM policies in each account requires separate management and maintenance, leading to increased operational overhead.

answers.text: Define a resource in AWS Resource Access Manager that prevents the launch of large EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) is primarily for resource sharing and doesn't directly restrict resource launches, making it unsuitable for this scenario.

answers.text: Create an IAM role in each account that denies the launch of large EC2 instances. Grant the developers IAM group access to the role.
answers.explanation: Creating IAM roles in each account adds to the operational overhead because these roles need to be managed and maintained across all accounts.

answers.text: Create an organization in AWS Organizations in the management account with the default policy. Create a service control policy (SCP) that denies the launch of large EC2 instances, and apply it to the AWS accounts.
answers.explanation: SCPs are centrally managed within AWS Organizations and apply to all member accounts. They effectively prevent launching large instances with minimal operational overhead. SCPs override IAM permissions.

overall_explanation: Service Control Policies (SCPs) within AWS Organizations provide a centralized mechanism to manage permissions across multiple AWS accounts. By creating an SCP that denies the launch of large EC2 instances and applying it to the AWS accounts, the solutions architect can effectively prevent these instances from being launched with the least operational overhead. This approach avoids the need to manage individual IAM policies or roles in each account. AWS Resource Access Manager is for resource sharing and not preventing EC2 launches. IAM policies would require individual updates for each account.

question: A company has migrated a fleet of hundreds of on-premises virtual machines (VMs) to Amazon EC2 instances. The instances run a diverse fleet of Windows Server versions along with several Linux distributions. The company needs a solution that will automate the inventory and updating of the operating systems. The company also requires a summary of common vulnerabilities of each instance for regular monthly reviews. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

answers.text: Set up AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to manage all the EC2 instances. Configure AWS Security Hub to produce monthly reports.
answers.explanation: AWS Security Hub aggregates security alerts and performs security best practice checks but is not the primary tool for vulnerability scanning or patching.

answers.text: Set up AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to manage all the EC2 instances. Deploy Amazon Inspector, and configure monthly reports.
answers.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager automates OS and application patching, and Amazon Inspector scans for vulnerabilities. This solution meets both requirements.

answers.text: Set up AWS Shield Advanced, and configure monthly reports. Deploy AWS Config to automate patch installations on the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: AWS Shield Advanced protects against DDoS attacks and AWS Config is primarily for configuration management and tracking changes, not patching. This does not meet the OS inventory and vulnerability scanning requirements.

answers.text: Set up Amazon GuardDuty in the account to monitor all EC2 instances. Deploy AWS Config to automate patch installations on the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty provides threat detection, while AWS Config focuses on configuration management. Neither fulfills the requirements for OS inventory, patch management, or vulnerability summaries.

overall_explanation: The correct solution is to use AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager for automated OS and application patching across the diverse fleet of EC2 instances. Additionally, Amazon Inspector should be deployed to scan the instances for vulnerabilities and generate monthly reports summarizing common vulnerabilities. Therefore, option B provides the best solution for meeting the stated requirements.

question: A company hosts its application in the AWS Cloud. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) load balancer. The application connects to an Amazon DynamoDB table. For disaster recovery (DR) purposes, the company wants to ensure that the application is available from another AWS Region with minimal downtime. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST downtime?

answers.text: Create an Auto Scaling group and an ELB in the DR Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Configure DNS failover to point to the new DR Region's ELB.
answers.explanation: This approach allows for quick failover since the infrastructure is already in place in the DR region and DynamoDB is already replicating data. DNS failover provides a fast and automated way to redirect traffic.

answers.text: Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances, ELBs, and DynamoDB tables to be launched when necessary. Configure DNS failover to point to the new DR Region's ELB.
answers.explanation: Creating infrastructure using CloudFormation during a DR event will introduce significant downtime as it takes time to provision resources.

answers.text: Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances and an ELB to be launched when necessary. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Configure DNS failover to point to the new DR Region's ELB.
answers.explanation: Creating infrastructure using CloudFormation during a DR event will introduce significant downtime as it takes time to provision resources.

answers.text: Create an Auto Scaling group and an ELB in the DR Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm with an evaluation period of 10 minutes to invoke an AWS Lambda function that updates Amazon Route 53 to point to the DR Region's ELB.
answers.explanation: While this approach pre-provisions infrastructure, using a CloudWatch alarm and Lambda function to update Route 53 adds unnecessary complexity and potential delay compared to direct DNS failover.

overall_explanation: The solution that provides the least downtime involves pre-provisioning the application infrastructure (Auto Scaling group and ELB) in the DR Region and configuring the DynamoDB table as a global table. Using DNS failover provides the quickest and most efficient way to redirect traffic to the DR Region in the event of a failure in the primary Region. CloudFormation based approaches will induce delay, and using Cloudwatch alarms with Lambda is more complex than required for direct DNS failover.

question: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances within a private subnet. The application requires storing and retrieving data in Amazon S3 buckets. To comply with regulatory requirements, the data must not traverse the public internet. Which solution should a solutions architect implement to satisfy these requirements most cost-effectively?

answers.text: Deploy a NAT gateway to access the S3 buckets.
answers.explanation: A NAT gateway allows instances in a private subnet to connect to the internet or other AWS services, but it does not prevent traffic from traversing the public internet. This option is not cost-effective and does not meet the regulatory requirements.

answers.text: Deploy AWS Storage Gateway to access the S3 buckets.
answers.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway is used to integrate on-premises environments with AWS storage services. While it can access S3, it's not the most direct or cost-effective solution for accessing S3 from EC2 instances within the same AWS region when avoiding the public internet.

answers.text: Deploy an S3 interface endpoint to access the S3 buckets.
answers.explanation: An S3 interface endpoint creates a private network interface (ENI) in your VPC that connects to Amazon S3. Although it provides private access, it's generally more expensive due to the cost associated with the network interface and data processing charges compared to a gateway endpoint.

answers.text: Deploy an S3 gateway endpoint to access the S3 buckets.
answers.explanation: An S3 gateway endpoint creates a route entry in the VPC route table for accessing S3 without crossing the public internet. Gateway endpoints are free and provide a cost-effective solution for accessing S3 from within a VPC.

overall_explanation: An S3 gateway endpoint is the most cost-effective solution because it's free and allows private access to S3 without traversing the public internet. While an S3 interface endpoint also provides private access, it is more expensive. NAT gateway is used for Internet access from Private Subnet and not the correct answer in this scenario. Storage gateway is irrelevant in this scenario.

question: A company hosts an application on Amazon EC2 instances that run in a single Availability Zone. The application is accessible by using the transport layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model. The company needs the application architecture to have high availability. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

answers.text: Configure new EC2 instances in a different Availability Zone. Use Amazon Route 53 to route traffic to all instances.
answers.explanation: While distributing instances across Availability Zones is good, this option doesn't address automatic scaling or health checks.

answers.text: Configure a Network Load Balancer in front of the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: A Network Load Balancer (NLB) operates at the transport layer (OSI layer 4), distributing traffic based on IP protocol data. It's suitable for TCP applications and provides high throughput and low latency.

answers.text: Configure a Network Load Balancer for TCP traffic to the instances. Configure an Application Load Balancer for HTTP and HTTPS traffic to the instances.
