answers.explanation: Since the application is accessible via the transport layer and there is no explicit need for HTTP/HTTPS, an Application Load Balancer is not necessary and adds unnecessary cost and complexity.

answers.text: Create an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use multiple Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to run application health checks on the instances.
answers.explanation: Auto Scaling across multiple Availability Zones provides redundancy and automatically replaces unhealthy instances, improving availability.

answers.text: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm. Configure the alarm to restart EC2 instances that transition to a stopped state.
answers.explanation: While helpful, this only addresses instances that are stopped. It doesn't address instances that are unhealthy but still running, or instances that are impacted by an Availability Zone outage.

overall_explanation: The MOST cost-effective solution to achieve high availability is to combine a Network Load Balancer (NLB) with an Auto Scaling group configured across multiple Availability Zones. The NLB distributes traffic at the transport layer, while the Auto Scaling group ensures that healthy instances are available to handle the load, even if an Availability Zone fails. Option B provides the correct load balancing strategy and option D provides the necessary autoscaling and multi-AZ functionality.

question: A company hosts its static website on Amazon S3. They want to implement a contact form that allows users to submit their name, email, phone number, and a message. Given the website has fewer than 100 visits per month and the company needs to be notified via email for each submission, which solution offers the MOST cost-effective implementation?

answers.text: Host the dynamic contact form in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Set up Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to connect to a third-party email provider.
answers.explanation: ECS may be overkill and more expensive for a low-traffic contact form. Additionally, using a third- party email provider adds complexity and potential cost.

answers.text: Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint that invokes an AWS Lambda function to return the contact form. Configure another Lambda function on the API Gateway to publish a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.
answers.explanation: This solution leverages serverless technologies (API Gateway, Lambda, SNS), which are cost-effective for low-traffic applications. Lambda charges per invocation, making it ideal for infrequent submissions. SNS provides an easy way to notify the company via email.

answers.text: Host the website by using AWS Amplify Hosting for static content and dynamic content. Use server-side scripting to build the contact form. Configure Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to deliver the message to the company.
answers.explanation: While Amplify can host dynamic content, using SQS to deliver notifications might not be as straightforward or efficient as using SNS for email notifications.

answers.text: Migrate the website from Amazon S3 to Amazon EC2 instances that run Windows Server. Use Internet Information Services (IIS) for Windows Server to host the webpage. Use client-side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.
answers.explanation: Migrating to EC2 is significantly more expensive than using S3 for static hosting and is unnecessary for a simple contact form. Client-side scripting with WorkMail integration may have limitations and be less reliable for server-side processing and notifications.

overall_explanation: The most cost-effective solution is to utilize serverless technologies like API Gateway, Lambda, and SNS. Option B allows for a dynamic contact form using Lambda, triggered by API Gateway. The SNS topic then provides a simple and reliable method for notifying the company via email about each submission. ECS and EC2 based solutions are less cost effective for small contact form needs.

question: A company uses AWS Organizations with dedicated AWS accounts for each business unit. Recently, a critical notification was mistakenly sent to the root user email address of a business unit account instead of the designated account owner. The company wants to ensure all future notifications are routed to the appropriate teams (billing, operations, or security) based on notification category. What is the MOST secure solution?

answers.text: Configure each AWS account to use a single, company-managed email address accessible to all account owners. Configure alternate contacts for each account with corresponding distribution lists for the billing, security, and operations teams for each business unit.
answers.explanation: This option requires all account owners to access a single email account, which is not ideal for security and separation of duties.

answers.text: Configure each AWS account to use a different email distribution list for each business unit. Ensure each distribution list has administrator email addresses to respond to alerts. Configure alternate contacts for each AWS account with corresponding distribution lists for the billing team, the security team, and the operations team for each business unit.
answers.explanation: While using distribution lists is a good approach, having admin email addresses to respond might not be the most secure way of directing alerts. There are better approaches to routing notifications by category.

answers.text: Configure each AWS account root user email address to be the individual company- managed email address of one person from each business unit. Configure alternate contacts for each AWS account with corresponding distribution lists for the billing team, the security team, and the operations team for each business unit.
answers.explanation: This option ties root user access to a single individual, potentially creating a single point of failure and security risk.

answers.text: Configure each AWS account root user to use email aliases that forward to a centralized mailbox. Configure alternate contacts for each account using a single, business- managed email distribution list for the billing, security, and operations teams respectively.
answers.explanation: This approach uses email aliases for the root user, directing those notifications to a centralized location. This is combined with separate business-managed distribution lists for alternate contacts based on notification category (billing, operations, security), providing proper routing and improving security by not sending sensitive information directly to individuals.

overall_explanation: The most secure solution (Option D) involves using email aliases for root user notifications and utilizing dedicated, business-managed distribution lists for alternate contacts based on notification category. This centralizes control, reduces the risk of unauthorized access, and ensures appropriate routing of notifications to the relevant teams. Configuring email aliases for root users to a centralized mailbox avoids sending critical notifications to individual emails. Using distribution lists for alternate contacts allows routing the emails to the correct teams.

question: A company runs an ecommerce application on AWS. Amazon EC2 instances process purchases and store the purchase details in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster. Customers are experiencing application timeouts during times of peak usage. A solutions architect needs to rearchitect the application so that the application can scale to meet peak usage demands. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

answers.text: Configure an Auto Scaling group of new EC2 instances to retry the purchases until the processing is complete. Update the applications to connect to the DB cluster by using Amazon RDS Proxy.
answers.explanation: RDS Proxy is primarily for connection pooling and availability, addressing connection limits rather than performance bottlenecks related to processing purchases. Retrying purchases adds complexity and doesn't resolve the underlying scaling issue.

answers.text: Configure the application to use an Amazon ElastiCache cluster in front of the Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
answers.explanation: ElastiCache is suitable for read-heavy workloads. However, purchase transactions primarily involve writes, making caching less effective in addressing the timeout issues during peak usage.

answers.text: Update the application to send the purchase requests to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure an Auto Scaling group of new EC2 instances that read from the SQS queue.
answers.explanation: Using SQS decouples the application and provides a buffer for purchase requests. An Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances consuming messages from the SQS queue allows the application to scale independently and handle bursts in traffic effectively.

answers.text: Configure an AWS Lambda function to retry the ticket purchases until the processing is complete.
answers.explanation: Lambda functions are not ideal for long-running database transactions and can become cost- prohibitive at scale due to invocation rates.

answers.text: Configure an Amazon API Gateway REST API with a usage plan.
answers.explanation: API Gateway provides API management capabilities, but does not directly address the scaling and timeout issues related to purchase processing and database interactions.

overall_explanation: Using SQS to queue purchase requests allows for decoupling and buffering. The Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances will then process these requests at their own pace, scaling according to demand. This is more cost effective than options using Lambda for retries, or solely relying on caching or RDS proxy. C is correct.

question: A survey company stores 3 TB of data in an Amazon S3 bucket, which is growing daily. They need to share this data with a marketing firm that also uses S3 buckets. To minimize the survey company's data transfer costs, which solution should they implement?

answers.text: Configure the Requester Pays feature on the company's S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: With Requester Pays, the marketing firm bears the data transfer costs when accessing the data in the company's S3 bucket, minimizing costs for the survey company.

answers.text: Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication from the company's S3 bucket to one of the marketing firm's S3 buckets.
answers.explanation: Cross-Region Replication would incur additional storage and data transfer costs for the survey company, increasing their expenses instead of reducing them.

answers.text: Configure cross-account access for the marketing firm so that the marketing firm has access to the company's S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: While this allows access, it doesn't inherently address who pays for the data transfer. The survey company would still likely be responsible for data transfer costs.

answers.text: Configure the company's S3 bucket to use S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Sync the S3 bucket to one of the marketing firm's S3 buckets.
answers.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering optimizes storage costs but doesn't reduce data transfer costs when the marketing firm accesses the data. Syncing the buckets would also incur costs for the survey company.

overall_explanation: The most cost-effective solution is to configure Requester Pays on the survey company's S3 bucket. This ensures the marketing firm pays for data transfer costs, minimizing the survey company's expenses. Replication incurs costs, and simple cross-account access doesn't shift data transfer payment responsibility.

question: A company uses AWS Organizations with 150 applications spread across 30 AWS accounts. They've configured an AWS Cost and Usage Report in the management account, delivering it to an Amazon S3 bucket which is replicated to another bucket in a data collection account. Senior leadership requires a custom dashboard displaying daily NAT gateway costs, starting from the current month's beginning. What solution fulfills these requirements?

answers.text: Share an Amazon QuickSight dashboard with a table visual, configuring QuickSight to use AWS DataSync to query the report.
answers.explanation: DataSync is used for data transfer, not querying data in S3 for visualization.

answers.text: Share an Amazon QuickSight dashboard with a table visual, configuring QuickSight to use Amazon Athena to query the report.
answers.explanation: This is the correct answer. QuickSight offers dashboarding capabilities for senior leadership, and Athena allows querying of the Cost and Usage Report data in S3.

answers.text: Share an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard with a table visual, configuring CloudWatch to use AWS DataSync to query the report.
answers.explanation: CloudWatch is designed for monitoring metrics and logs and isn't the ideal solution for custom dashboards for senior leadership. DataSync is also not appropriate for querying the data.

answers.text: Share an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard with a table visual, configuring CloudWatch to use Amazon Athena to query the report.
answers.explanation: While CloudWatch can display some metrics, it's not suited for displaying custom reports in a user- friendly format for leadership consumption, and the table visualization requirement would be hard to achieve. QuickSight is much better for dashboarding.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to use Amazon QuickSight for the dashboarding, given its strong visualization capabilities. To query the data in the S3 bucket containing the AWS Cost and Usage Report, Amazon Athena is the most appropriate choice. Athena allows you to use SQL to directly query data in S3. Therefore, the correct answer is B.

question: A company is hosting a high-traffic static website on Amazon S3 with an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has a default TTL of 0 seconds. The company wants to implement caching to improve performance for the website. However, the company also wants to ensure that stale content is not served for more than a few minutes after a deployment. Which combination of caching methods should a solutions architect implement to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.text: Set the CloudFront default TTL to 2 minutes.
answers.explanation: Setting the default TTL to 2 minutes allows CloudFront to cache content for a short period, ensuring content is cached and served quickly.

answers.text: Set a default TTL of 2 minutes on the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: TTL is not a concept applied directly to S3 buckets. TTL and caching behaviors are managed through Cache-Control headers and CloudFront settings.

answers.text: Add a Cache-Control private directive to the objects in Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: The `private` directive lets caching occur locally only, not in shared caches like CloudFront, preventing shared caching.

answers.text: Create an AWS Lambda@Edge function to add an Expires header to HTTP responses. Configure the function to run on viewer response.
answers.explanation: While Lambda@Edge offers fine-grained control, setting the default TTL in CloudFront is simpler and sufficient for the requirements. Plus, Lambda@Edge is not necessary to ensure content is served fresh after a deployment when using CloudFront invalidation.

answers.text: Add a Cache-Control max-age directive of 24 hours to the objects in Amazon S3. On deployment, create a CloudFront invalidation to clear any changed files from edge caches.
answers.explanation: Using a long Cache-Control `max-age` directive improves performance, while targeted CloudFront invalidations ensure that updated content is served immediately after deployment.

overall_explanation: The optimal solution is to set the CloudFront default TTL to 2 minutes and add a Cache- Control `max-age` directive to objects in S3, coupled with CloudFront invalidations on deployment. Setting a short TTL ensures that the browser asks CloudFront after 2 minutes. Adding `Cache-Control max-age` to S3 and invalidating on deployment ensures stale content is cleared and that updates are propagated efficiently. This combination balances performance and freshness of content.

question: A company's application uses Amazon EC2 instances and AWS Lambda functions. The EC2 instances reside in private subnets within a VPC. The Lambda functions require direct network access to the EC2 instances for proper operation. The application is intended to run for 1 year, and the number of Lambda functions utilized will increase throughout the year. The company aims to minimize costs across all application resources. Which solution best meets these requirements?

answers.text: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan. Connect the Lambda functions to the private subnets that contain the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: An EC2 Instance Savings Plan only applies to EC2 usage, and does not provide cost savings for Lambda functions. Therefore this is incorrect.

answers.text: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan. Connect the Lambda functions to new public subnets in the same VPC where the EC2 instances run.
answers.explanation: An EC2 Instance Savings Plan only applies to EC2 usage. Lambda functions in public subnets cannot directly communicate with EC2 instances in private subnets, further complicating the solution.

answers.text: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan. Connect the Lambda functions to the private subnets that contain the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: A Compute Savings Plan provides discounts on both EC2 and Lambda usage, making it suitable for the evolving needs of the application. Connecting Lambda functions to private subnets allows direct and secure access to EC2 instances.

answers.text: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan. Keep the Lambda functions in the Lambda service VPC.
answers.explanation: Keeping the Lambda functions in the Lambda service VPC would not allow for direct network access to the EC2 instances in the private subnets.

overall_explanation: The most cost-effective and functional solution is to purchase a Compute Savings Plan, which covers both EC2 and Lambda usage, and to connect the Lambda functions to the private subnets containing the EC2 instances. This ensures direct network access while minimizing costs and maximizing resource utilization. A Compute Savings Plan accounts for increased Lambda usage throughout the year. EC2 Instance Savings Plans do not apply to Lambda function costs.

question: A company has deployed a multi-account strategy on AWS by using AWS Control Tower. The company has provided individual AWS accounts to each of its developers. The company wants to implement controls to limit AWS resource costs that the developers incur. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.text: Instruct each developer to tag all their resources with a tag that has a key of CostCenter and a value of the developer's name. Use the required-tags AWS Config managed rule to check for the tag. Create an AWS Lambda function to terminate resources that do not have the tag. Configure AWS Cost Explorer to send a daily report to each developer to monitor their spending.
answers.explanation: This approach requires manual tagging by developers, creating and maintaining Lambda functions, and relies on daily reports, leading to high operational overhead and reactive cost control.

answers.text: Use AWS Budgets to establish budgets for each developer account. Set up budget alerts for actual and forecast values to notify developers when they exceed or expect to exceed their assigned budget. Use AWS Budgets actions to apply a DenyAll policy to the developer's IAM role to prevent additional resources from being launched when the assigned budget is reached.
answers.explanation: AWS Budgets allows setting budgets for each developer account and triggering actions based on budget breaches. This includes applying IAM policies to restrict resource creation, providing proactive cost control with minimal operational overhead. Note that the 'DenyAll' policy may not exist as is, but custom deny policies can be used.

answers.text: Use AWS Cost Explorer to monitor and report on costs for each developer account. Configure Cost Explorer to send a daily report to each developer to monitor their spending. Use AWS Cost Anomaly Detection to detect anomalous spending and provide alerts.
answers.explanation: Cost Explorer provides monitoring and reporting capabilities, and anomaly detection can identify unusual spending. However, this approach is reactive and does not prevent developers from incurring costs exceeding their limits.

answers.text: Use AWS Service Catalog to allow developers to launch resources within a limited cost range. Create AWS Lambda functions in each AWS account to stop running resources at the end of each work day. Configure the Lambda functions to resume the resources at the start of each work day.
answers.explanation: Service Catalog can help control resource types, and Lambda functions can stop/start resources. However, managing Service Catalog and Lambda functions across multiple accounts increases operational overhead. It also doesn't effectively limit costs as developers can still launch resources within the allowed catalog during the day.

overall_explanation: The most effective solution with the least operational overhead is to utilize AWS Budgets. It offers proactive cost control by establishing budgets, sending alerts, and triggering actions to restrict resource creation when budget limits are reached. While tagging and reporting are useful, they don't actively prevent excessive spending. Service Catalog and Lambda functions introduce significant management overhead. Therefore, AWS Budgets provides the best balance of cost control and ease of management.

question: A solutions architect is designing a three-tier web application with security as a high priority. The architecture consists of an internet-facing Application Load Balancer (ALB), a web tier on EC2 instances in private subnets, an application tier with business logic on EC2 instances in private subnets, and a database tier with Microsoft SQL Server on EC2 instances in private subnets. Which combination of security group configurations should the solutions architect implement to achieve this? (Choose three.)

answers.text: Configure the security group for the web tier to allow inbound HTTPS traffic from the security group for the ALB.
answers.explanation: This allows the ALB to send traffic to the web tier over HTTPS. Security groups are stateful, so return traffic is automatically allowed.

answers.text: Configure the security group for the web tier to allow outbound HTTPS traffic to 0.0.0.0/0.
answers.explanation: This is not necessary. Security groups are stateful, so outbound rules are not required for established connections.

answers.text: Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound Microsoft SQL Server traffic from the security group for the application tier.
answers.explanation: This allows the application tier to communicate with the database tier using the Microsoft SQL Server protocol. Security groups are stateful, so return traffic is automatically allowed.

answers.text: Configure the security group for the database tier to allow outbound HTTPS traffic and Microsoft SQL Server traffic to the security group for the web tier.
answers.explanation: This is incorrect. Security groups should only allow traffic from tiers that need to communicate directly with that tier. The database tier does not need to talk to the web tier directly.

answers.text: Configure the security group for the application tier to allow inbound HTTPS traffic from the security group for the web tier.
answers.explanation: This allows the web tier to send traffic to the application tier over HTTPS. Security groups are stateful, so return traffic is automatically allowed.

answers.text: Configure the security group for the application tier to allow outbound HTTPS traffic and Microsoft SQL Server traffic to the security group for the web tier.
answers.explanation: This is not necessary. The Application tier initiates connection to the DB, not to the web tier. The return traffic for existing connections is already allowed because of stateful nature of security groups.

overall_explanation: To secure the three-tier web application, the following security group configurations are necessary: 1. Allow inbound HTTPS traffic to the web tier from the ALB security group. 2. Allow inbound HTTPS traffic to the application tier from the web tier security group. 3. Allow inbound Microsoft SQL Server traffic to the database tier from the application tier security group. Security groups are stateful, meaning that return traffic for established connections is automatically allowed. This simplifies the configuration and enhances security by limiting the allowed traffic to only what is necessary for the application to function.

question: A company has released a new version of its production application. The company's workload uses Amazon EC2, AWS Lambda, AWS Fargate, and Amazon SageMaker. The company wants to cost optimize the workload now that usage is at a steady state. The company wants to cover the most services with the fewest savings plans. Which combination of savings plans will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.text: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for Amazon EC2 and SageMaker.
answers.explanation: An EC2 Instance Savings Plan only applies to EC2 usage in a specific Region.

answers.text: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan for Amazon EC2, Lambda, and SageMaker.
answers.explanation: A Compute Savings Plan covers EC2, Lambda, and Fargate, but not SageMaker.

answers.text: Purchase a SageMaker Savings Plan.
answers.explanation: A SageMaker Savings Plan specifically covers SageMaker usage.

answers.text: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan for Lambda, Fargate, and Amazon EC2.
answers.explanation: A Compute Savings Plan covers EC2, Lambda, and Fargate.

answers.text: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for Amazon EC2 and Fargate.
answers.explanation: An EC2 Instance Savings Plan only applies to EC2 usage in a specific Region.

overall_explanation: The best solution to cover all services with the fewest savings plans is to purchase a SageMaker Savings Plan and a Compute Savings Plan. A SageMaker Savings Plan covers the Amazon SageMaker costs. A Compute Savings Plan covers the AWS Lambda, AWS Fargate, and Amazon EC2 costs. Using this combination of savings plans maximizes the cost savings and minimizes the number of plans.

question: A company's applications are connected to a Microsoft SQL Server database. The company plans to migrate to an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database while minimizing application code changes. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.text: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to rewrite the SQL queries in the applications.
answers.explanation: AWS SCT helps in converting the database schema, but doesn't directly rewrite SQL queries within the application code itself.

answers.text: Enable Babelfish on Aurora PostgreSQL to run the SQL queries from the applications.
answers.explanation: Babelfish for Aurora PostgreSQL allows Aurora to understand commands from applications written for Microsoft SQL Server, minimizing the need to rewrite queries.

answers.text: Migrate the database schema and data by using the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) and AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).
answers.explanation: AWS SCT handles schema conversion, and AWS DMS handles data migration. This is a standard approach for migrating databases.

answers.text: Use Amazon RDS Proxy to connect the applications to Aurora PostgreSQL.
answers.explanation: Amazon RDS Proxy helps improve database scalability and availability, but it doesn't address the compatibility issues between SQL Server and Aurora PostgreSQL.

answers.text: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to rewrite the SQL queries in the applications.
answers.explanation: AWS DMS is used for data migration, not for rewriting SQL queries within the applications.

overall_explanation: Using AWS SCT and AWS DMS for migrating the database schema and data (Option C), coupled with enabling Babelfish on Aurora PostgreSQL to understand SQL Server commands (Option B), minimizes the need for application code changes during the migration. AWS SCT converts the schema, DMS migrates the data, and Babelfish allows the application to continue using familiar SQL Server syntax.

question: A company plans to rehost an application to Amazon EC2 instances that use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) as the attached storage. A solutions architect must design a solution to ensure that all newly created Amazon EBS volumes are encrypted by default. The solution must also prevent the creation of unencrypted EBS volumes. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.text: Configure the EC2 account attributes to always encrypt new EBS volumes.
answers.explanation: Configuring the EC2 account attributes will encrypt all newly created volumes. However, it doesn't prevent the creation of unencrypted volumes during instance launch if the request specifies no encryption. While this enables default encryption, it does not explicitly *prevent* unencrypted volume creation.

answers.text: Use AWS Config. Configure the encrypted-volumes identifier. Apply the default AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key.
answers.explanation: AWS Config can be used to identify non-compliant EBS volumes and trigger remediation actions. By using AWS Config, you can enforce the rule that all EBS volumes must be encrypted and prevent the creation of unencrypted EBS volumes. This aligns with the requirement to prevent the creation of unencrypted volumes.

answers.text: Configure AWS Systems Manager to create encrypted copies of the EBS volumes. Reconfigure the EC2 instances to use the encrypted volumes.
answers.explanation: This solution involves creating encrypted copies of EBS volumes *after* they are created. This does not prevent the initial creation of unencrypted volumes and adds unnecessary complexity.

answers.text: Create a customer managed key in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Configure AWS Migration Hub to use the key when the company migrates workloads.
answers.explanation: AWS Migration Hub is used for migration tracking. Configuring it with a KMS key doesn't ensure default encryption of EBS volumes or prevent the creation of unencrypted EBS volumes. Migration Hub is not directly involved in EBS volume creation or encryption enforcement.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to use AWS Config to ensure all EBS volumes are encrypted. AWS Config can identify non-compliant resources, like unencrypted volumes, and automatically trigger remediation actions. Option A configures default encryption, but does not prevent unencrypted volume creation. Options C and D do not meet the requirements. Therefore, using AWS Config is the most comprehensive solution that prevents the creation of unencrypted EBS volumes.

question: An e-commerce company requires a solution to collect user clickstream data from its website for real-time analytics. The website experiences fluctuating traffic patterns throughout the day. The company needs a scalable solution that can dynamically adjust to these varying levels of traffic. Which of the following solutions best meets these requirements?

answers.text: Use a data stream in Amazon Kinesis Data Streams in on-demand mode to capture the clickstream data. Use AWS Lambda to process the data in real time.
answers.explanation: This is the best solution because Kinesis Data Streams in on-demand mode automatically scales based on traffic, making it ideal for fluctuating traffic patterns. AWS Lambda enables real-time processing of the data without managing infrastructure.

answers.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to capture the clickstream data. Use AWS Glue to process the data in real time.
answers.explanation: While Kinesis Data Firehose is scalable, it's geared more towards near real-time delivery, not strictly real-time. AWS Glue is better suited for ETL and batch processing, not real-time analysis.

answers.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to capture the clickstream data. Use AWS Glue to process the data in real time.
answers.explanation: Kinesis Video Streams is designed specifically for video and audio streaming data, not clickstream data. AWS Glue is better suited for ETL and batch processing, not real-time analysis.

answers.text: Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink (previously known as Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics) to capture the clickstream data. Use AWS Lambda to process the data in real time.
answers.explanation: While Flink can be used for stream processing, it's not typically used to initially capture and ingest the raw clickstream data directly. Kinesis Data Streams is more suitable for initial data capture.

overall_explanation: The optimal solution is to use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams in on-demand mode to capture clickstream data and AWS Lambda to process it in real time. Kinesis Data Streams in on-demand mode provides the necessary scalability to handle fluctuating traffic, and AWS Lambda allows for real-time data processing without infrastructure management. Kinesis Data Firehose is more for near real-time delivery, Kinesis Video Streams is for video, and Kinesis Data Analytics isn't the best service for capturing the initial stream.

question: A global company runs its workloads on AWS. The company's application uses Amazon S3 buckets across AWS Regions for sensitive data storage and analysis. The company stores millions of objects in multiple S3 buckets daily. The company wants to identify all S3 buckets that are *not* versioning-enabled across all regions. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.text: Set up an AWS CloudTrail event that has a rule to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across Regions.
answers.explanation: CloudTrail primarily logs API calls made to AWS services. While CloudTrail can track changes to S3 buckets, it doesn't provide a built-in mechanism to efficiently identify buckets without versioning enabled across all regions.

answers.text: Use Amazon S3 Storage Lens to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across Regions.
answers.explanation: S3 Storage Lens provides organization-wide visibility into object storage, including metrics on data protection best practices like versioning. It can directly identify buckets where versioning is not enabled.

answers.text: Enable IAM Access Analyzer for S3 to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning- enabled across Regions.
answers.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer for S3 helps identify buckets with access that is shared with external entities. It does not directly provide metrics related to S3 versioning status.

answers.text: Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across Regions.
answers.explanation: S3 Multi-Region Access Points are used to simplify access to data in multiple regions but do not offer any insights or functionality related to versioning status across buckets.

overall_explanation: Amazon S3 Storage Lens is the best solution because it is specifically designed to provide visibility into object storage usage and data protection best practices, including identifying S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across different regions. It offers metrics like 'Versioning-enabled bucket count' to easily find buckets without versioning. CloudTrail can't directly identify buckets without versioning enabled. IAM Access Analyzer focuses on access control, not versioning. S3 Multi-Region Access Points simplifies data access but doesn't provide versioning information.

question: A company stores confidential audit documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. The S3 bucket policy restricts access to audit team IAM user credentials following the principle of least privilege. Company managers are concerned about accidental deletion of documents in the S3 bucket and desire a more secure solution. What should a solutions architect implement to secure the audit documents?

answers.text: Enable the versioning and MFA Delete features on the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Enabling versioning allows recovery of accidentally deleted objects, while MFA Delete requires multi-factor authentication for deletion, preventing accidental or unauthorized permanent deletions.

answers.text: Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) on the IAM user credentials for each audit team IAM user account.
answers.explanation: While MFA enhances user authentication security, it doesn't directly prevent accidental object deletion in the S3 bucket.

answers.text: Add an S3 Lifecycle policy to the audit team's IAM user accounts to deny the s3:DeleteObject action during audit dates.
answers.explanation: Lifecycle policies can manage object lifecycles but using them to deny deletion only during audit dates doesn't protect against accidental deletions at other times.

answers.text: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt the S3 bucket and restrict audit team IAM user accounts from accessing the KMS key.
answers.explanation: KMS encryption secures data at rest, but doesn't prevent accidental object deletion. Restricting KMS key access would prevent access to the encrypted objects but wouldn't prevent deletion if the IAM user had the s3:DeleteObject permission.

overall_explanation: Enabling versioning allows for the recovery of accidentally deleted objects. Enabling MFA Delete provides an additional layer of security by requiring multi-factor authentication to permanently delete an object, mitigating the risk of accidental deletion.

question: A company needs to optimize its Amazon S3 storage costs for an application that generates many files that cannot be recreated. Each file is approximately 5 MB and is stored in Amazon S3 Standard storage. The company must store the files for 4 years before the files can be deleted. The files must be immediately accessible. The files are frequently accessed in the first 30 days of object creation, but they are rarely accessed after the first 30 days. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.text: Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move the files to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval 30 days after object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
answers.explanation: While Glacier Instant Retrieval offers immediate access, it has a minimum storage duration of 90 days and storage costs may be higher than S3 Standard-IA when access is infrequent after 30 days.

answers.text: Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move the files to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) 30 days after object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
answers.explanation: S3 One Zone-IA is cheaper but stores data in a single Availability Zone. Because the files cannot be recreated, this option violates the durability requirement.

answers.text: Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move the files to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 30 days after object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
answers.explanation: S3 Standard-IA is optimized for objects accessed less frequently but still requires rapid retrieval and high durability. This option provides immediate access and cost savings after the initial 30 days while maintaining data durability.

answers.text: Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move the files to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 30 days after object creation. Move the files to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval 4 years after object creation.
answers.explanation: Moving the files to Glacier after 4 years is unnecessary, as the company needs to delete the files after 4 years to meet the storage requirement. Deleting the files directly from S3 Standard-IA after 4 years provides the most cost-effective solution.

overall_explanation: S3 Standard-IA offers the best balance of cost and accessibility for infrequently accessed data that still requires rapid retrieval and high durability. Moving the files to S3 Standard- IA after the first 30 days allows the company to leverage the lower storage costs while maintaining immediate access and deleting them after 4 years. Therefore, the files are stored in S3 Standard-IA storage class for the remaining duration which reduces the costs. S3 One Zone-IA is not suitable as data can not be recreated and Glacier is not required as data is deleted after 4 years.

question: A company operates a critical storage application in the AWS Cloud, utilizing Amazon S3 in two AWS Regions. The application needs to direct remote user data to the S3 bucket nearest to them, avoiding public network congestion. The company also requires the application to automatically failover between regions with minimal S3 management overhead. Which solution best meets these requirements?

answers.text: Implement an active-active design between the two Regions. Configure the application to use the regional S3 endpoints closest to the user.
answers.explanation: While this uses both regions, it doesn't leverage a global endpoint and requires the application to manage routing, potentially increasing complexity and not providing seamless failover.

answers.text: Use an active-passive configuration with S3 Multi-Region Access Points. Create a global endpoint for each of the Regions.
answers.explanation: Active-passive doesn't fully utilize both regions for performance and cost optimization. Also, creating multiple global endpoints defeats the purpose of a centralized access point.

answers.text: Send user data to the regional S3 endpoints closest to the user. Configure an S3 cross- account replication rule to keep the S3 buckets synchronized.
answers.explanation: This approach necessitates managing the regional endpoint selection within the application and does not inherently provide failover capabilities without additional logic. It also doesn't guarantee data is sent via the AWS network, thus not fulfilling the 'no public network congestion' requirement.

answers.text: Set up Amazon S3 to use Multi-Region Access Points in an active-active configuration with a single global endpoint. Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication.
answers.explanation: This is the best solution. Multi-Region Access Points in active-active configuration with S3 Cross- Region Replication directs requests to the nearest region and provides automatic failover. The global endpoint simplifies application integration. S3 Cross-Region Replication ensures data consistency across regions.

overall_explanation: Option D is the most suitable because it leverages Amazon S3 Multi-Region Access Points in an active-active configuration, directing requests to the closest AWS Region with low latency via the AWS global network. The single global endpoint simplifies application connectivity and the application does not need to implement failover logic. S3 Cross- Region Replication ensures data consistency across regions, enabling seamless failover capabilities in case of an outage in one region.

question: A company is migrating a data center from its on-premises location to AWS. The company has several legacy applications that are hosted on individual virtual servers, and changes to the application designs cannot be made. Each virtual server currently runs as its own EC2 instance. A solutions architect needs to ensure that the applications are reliable and fault tolerant after migration to AWS. The applications will run on Amazon EC2 instances. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.text: Create an Auto Scaling group that has a minimum of one and a maximum of one. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of each application instance. Use the AMI to create EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group. Configure an Application Load Balancer in front of the Auto Scaling group.
answers.explanation: An Auto Scaling group with min/max of 1 ensures one instance is always running, replacing it if it fails. Using an AMI ensures consistent configuration. An ALB manages traffic and prepares for potential scaling.

answers.text: Use AWS Backup to create an hourly backup of the EC2 instance that hosts each application. Store the backup in Amazon S3 in a separate Availability Zone. Configure a disaster recovery process to restore the EC2 instance for each application from its most recent backup.
answers.explanation: Hourly backups provide disaster recovery, but not real-time fault tolerance. The recovery process introduces downtime, failing to meet reliability requirements.

answers.text: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of each application instance. Launch two new EC2 instances from the AMI. Place each EC2 instance in a separate Availability Zone. Configure a Network Load Balancer that has the EC2 instances as targets.
answers.explanation: This option provides high availability but relies on manual intervention if an instance fails. Without Auto Scaling, new instances must be launched manually.

answers.text: Use AWS Migration Hub Refactor Spaces to migrate each application off the EC2 instance. Break down functionality from each application into individual components. Host each application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with an AWS Fargate launch type.
answers.explanation: This option requires changing the application design, which is explicitly prohibited in the scenario.

overall_explanation: Option A provides fault tolerance within the given constraints. Auto Scaling ensures a replacement instance is launched automatically in case of failure, leveraging an AMI for consistent configuration. Although the min/max is one, Auto Scaling will still replace the failed instance. The ALB provides a stable endpoint and is forward-looking in case scaling becomes an option. Options B, C, and D all have drawbacks relating to downtime or a violation of the problem requirements.

question: A company wants to isolate its workloads by creating an AWS account for each workload. The company needs a solution that centrally manages networking components for the workloads. The solution also must create accounts with automatic security controls (guardrails). Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.text: Use AWS Control Tower to deploy accounts. Create a networking account that has a VPC with private subnets and public subnets. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the subnets with the workload accounts.
answers.explanation: This is the correct answer because AWS Control Tower simplifies account creation with built-in guardrails. Centralizing networking in a dedicated account and sharing subnets with AWS RAM minimizes operational overhead. AWS Control Tower also helps in automating account deployment and management. Control Tower is also designed to simplify the process of creating and managing a multi-account AWS environment while maintaining security and compliance.

answers.text: Use AWS Organizations to deploy accounts. Create a networking account that has a VPC with private subnets and public subnets. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the subnets with the workload accounts.
answers.explanation: While AWS Organizations helps in managing accounts, it does not provide the automatic security controls (guardrails) that AWS Control Tower offers. Therefore, it requires more operational overhead to implement and manage security controls.

answers.text: Use AWS Control Tower to deploy accounts. Deploy a VPC in each workload account. Configure each VPC to route through an inspection VPC by using a transit gateway attachment.
answers.explanation: This approach, while using Control Tower, introduces higher operational overhead due to the complexity of managing multiple VPCs and transit gateway attachments. Also, it is less efficient than centralizing networking components.

answers.text: Use AWS Organizations to deploy accounts. Deploy a VPC in each workload account. Configure each VPC to route through an inspection VPC by using a transit gateway attachment.
answers.explanation: This option has the highest operational overhead. It requires managing multiple VPCs, transit gateway attachments and lacks the automatic security control offered by AWS Control Tower.

overall_explanation: AWS Control Tower automates account deployment with built-in guardrails, addressing the need for automatic security controls. Centralizing networking in a dedicated account and using AWS RAM to share subnets efficiently manages networking components with minimal operational overhead. Therefore, using Control Tower and AWS RAM offers the least operational overhead while meeting the requirements.

question: A company hosts a website on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website serves static content. Website traffic is increasing. The company wants to minimize the website hosting costs. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.text: Move the website to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Moving static content to S3 and using CloudFront offers cost-effective scalability and content delivery, reducing the load on EC2 instances and minimizing hosting costs. CloudFront caches content, reducing latency and improving user experience.

answers.text: Move the website to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon ElastiCache cluster for the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: ElastiCache is primarily used for caching dynamic content or database queries. While S3 is suitable for static content, ElastiCache is not the appropriate service to handle increased traffic for static website content. ElastiCache isn't typically used in conjunction with S3 in this way, so this solution wouldn't be optimal or cost-effective.

answers.text: Move the website to AWS Amplify. Configure an ALB to resolve to the Amplify website.
answers.explanation: AWS Amplify is suitable for hosting static websites, but using an ALB in front of it is unnecessary and adds complexity and cost. Amplify is designed to directly serve static content.

answers.text: Move the website to AWS Amplify. Configure EC2 instances to cache the website.
answers.explanation: Using EC2 instances to cache a website hosted on Amplify defeats the purpose of using Amplify for static content hosting. It introduces unnecessary complexity and cost. Amplify is designed to directly serve static content efficiently.

overall_explanation: The most cost-effective solution for serving static content is to utilize Amazon S3 for storage and Amazon CloudFront for content delivery. This combination allows for scalable and efficient distribution of static assets, minimizing the load on EC2 instances and reducing overall hosting costs. Options B, C, and D introduce unnecessary services or configurations that increase costs and complexity.

question: A company is migrating its on-premises file server to AWS. The company requires a solution that allows users to access files from their existing SMB clients. The solution should also minimize administrative overhead. Which AWS service should the company use?

answers.text: AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway with a created file share using the required client protocol and connected application server.
answers.explanation: Volume Gateway does not directly support SMB. SMB is more commonly supported in File Gateway or FSx for Windows.

answers.text: AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway configured to use Amazon S3 with connected application server.
answers.explanation: Tape Gateway is designed for backup and archival purposes, not for real-time file sharing using SMB.

answers.text: An Amazon EC2 Windows instance with a Windows file share role installed and configured, and connected application server.
answers.explanation: While possible, this option involves manual setup, patching, maintenance, backups, and scaling, leading to significant administrative overhead.

answers.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system with connected application server.
answers.explanation: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed service that provides native Windows file system capabilities, including SMB support, with minimal administrative overhead.

overall_explanation: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is the best choice because it offers native SMB support with minimal administrative overhead. It is a fully managed service, simplifying setup, maintenance, and scaling compared to creating your own file server on EC2 or using Storage Gateway Volume Gateway. Tape Gateway is not suitable for this use case.

question: A company is designing its production application's disaster recovery (DR) strategy. The application is backed by a MySQL database on an Amazon Aurora cluster in the us-east-1 Region. The company has chosen the us-west-1 Region as its DR Region. The company's target recovery point objective (RPO) is 5 minutes and the target recovery time objective (RTO) is 20 minutes. The company wants to minimize configuration changes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

answers.text: Create an Aurora read replica in us-west-1 similar in size to the production application's Aurora MySQL cluster writer instance.
answers.explanation: Read replicas do not automatically provide failover in the event of a disaster, and manual intervention could exceed the RTO.

answers.text: Convert the Aurora cluster to an Aurora global database. Configure managed failover.
answers.explanation: Aurora Global Databases are designed for cross-region replication with minimal impact on database performance and enable fast failover, making it suitable for meeting the specified RPO and RTO with minimal operational overhead.

answers.text: Create a new Aurora cluster in us-west-1 that has Cross-Region Replication.
answers.explanation: While Cross-Region Replication can replicate data, it doesn't automatically fail over. Manual intervention is required which exceeds RTO.

answers.text: Create a new Aurora cluster in us-west-1. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to sync both clusters.
answers.explanation: Using AWS DMS to sync clusters introduces complexity and may not meet the required RPO due to replication latency. Also it requires much more management overhead.

overall_explanation: Aurora Global Database provides a recovery point objective (RPO) of 1 second and a recovery time objective (RTO) of less than 1 minute, providing a strong foundation for a global business continuity plan. It allows for managed failover which eliminates the need for manual interventions.

question: A company needs to run a critical, stateful data analysis job every week before the start of the work week. The job must run uninterrupted for at least 1 hour. What is the MOST suitable AWS solution for this scenario?

answers.text: Create a container for the job. Schedule the job to run as an AWS Fargate task on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster by using Amazon EventBridge Scheduler.
answers.explanation: This is the most suitable solution. Fargate allows for long-running, uninterrupted tasks, and EventBridge Scheduler provides reliable scheduling.

answers.text: Configure the job to run in an AWS Lambda function. Create a scheduled rule in Amazon EventBridge to invoke the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: This is not a suitable solution. AWS Lambda functions have a maximum execution time of 15 minutes, which is insufficient for the 1-hour job duration.

answers.text: Configure an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 Spot Instances that run Amazon Linux. Configure a crontab entry on the instances to run the analysis.
answers.explanation: This is not a suitable solution. Spot Instances can be interrupted, violating the requirement for uninterrupted job execution.

answers.text: Configure an AWS DataSync task to run the job. Configure a cron expression to run the task on a schedule.
answers.explanation: This is not a suitable solution. AWS DataSync is designed for data transfer, not for running long running analysis jobs.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to containerize the data analysis job and run it as a Fargate task scheduled by EventBridge Scheduler. Fargate offers a serverless compute environment suitable for long-running tasks, and EventBridge provides a reliable scheduling mechanism. Lambda functions are not suitable due to their time constraints, Spot Instances are prone to interruption, and DataSync is not designed for running applications.

question: A company runs workloads in the AWS Cloud. The company wants to centrally collect security data to assess security across the entire company and to improve workload protection. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

answers.text: Configure a data lake in AWS Lake Formation. Use AWS Glue crawlers to ingest the security data into the data lake.
answers.explanation: This option requires significant development effort to configure and manage AWS Lake Formation and Glue crawlers.

answers.text: Configure an AWS Lambda function to collect the security data in .csv format. Upload the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: This option requires development effort to create and maintain a Lambda function and manage the data in S3.

answers.text: Configure a data lake in Amazon Security Lake to collect the security data. Upload the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Amazon Security Lake is purpose-built for collecting and centralizing security data with minimal configuration and integrates easily with AWS security services. This option provides the least development effort.

answers.text: Configure an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication instance to load the security data into an Amazon RDS cluster.
answers.explanation: AWS DMS is not the correct service to load security data, as it is meant to migrate databases.

overall_explanation: Amazon Security Lake automatically centralizes security data from AWS environments, SaaS providers, on premises, and cloud sources into a purpose-built data lake, requiring the least development effort. It integrates easily with AWS security services, providing a streamlined solution with less manual configuration compared to using AWS Glue or Lambda. It is also designed to scale automatically, making it the most efficient and effective solution.

question: A company is migrating five on-premises applications to VPCs in the AWS Cloud. Each application is currently deployed in isolated virtual networks on premises and should be deployed similarly in the AWS Cloud. The applications need to reach a shared services VPC. All the applications must be able to communicate with each other. If the migration is successful, the company will repeat the migration process for more than 100 applications. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

answers.text: Deploy software VPN tunnels between the application VPCs and the shared services VPC. Add routes between the application VPCs in their subnets to the shared services VPC.
answers.explanation: Deploying software VPN tunnels is complex, has high administrative overhead, and doesn't scale well to a large number of VPCs. It requires setting up and maintaining individual tunnels for each VPC.

answers.text: Deploy VPC peering connections between the application VPCs and the shared services VPC. Add routes between the application VPCs in their subnets to the shared services VPC through the peering connection.
answers.explanation: VPC peering is better than VPN tunnels but becomes complex and unmanageable as the number of VPCs increases. It requires manual peering for each pair of VPCs and routing configurations.

answers.text: Deploy an AWS Direct Connect connection between the application VPCs and the shared services VPC. Add routes from the application VPCs in their subnets to the shared services VPC and the applications VPCs. Add routes from the shared services VPC subnets to the applications VPCs.
answers.explanation: Direct Connect is costly and is designed for hybrid cloud setups or data center connectivity, not for inter-VPC communication within AWS.

answers.text: Deploy a transit gateway with associations between the transit gateway and the application VPCs and the shared services VPC. Add routes between the application VPCs in their subnets and the application VPCs to the shared services VPC through the transit gateway.
answers.explanation: A transit gateway provides a centralized hub for managing inter-VPC communication. It simplifies the process of routing between VPCs, is highly scalable, and reduces the complexity of adding new VPCs, making it optimal for managing large-scale environments.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to deploy a transit gateway. It allows for inter-VPC communication for all applications/VPCs, can reach a shared services VPC, and easily scales for future migrations. VPN tunnels and VPC peering are not as scalable. Direct Connect is not appropriate for connecting numerous VPCs in the AWS Cloud.

question: A company hosts an SMB file server in its data center. This server houses large files that are actively accessed for the first week after creation, after which access becomes infrequent. The data volume is nearing the storage capacity. To address this, a solutions architect needs to expand storage without compromising low-latency access to recent files and implement lifecycle management. Which solution satisfies these requirements?

answers.text: Use AWS DataSync to migrate data older than 7 days from the SMB file server to AWS.
answers.explanation: AWS DataSync focuses on data synchronization, not on providing extended storage and tiered access based on file age. It doesn't address the low-latency requirement for recent files.

answers.text: Implement an Amazon S3 File Gateway to extend the company's storage. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days.
answers.explanation: S3 File Gateway provides a local cache for frequently accessed files, ensuring low latency. The lifecycle policy automatically transitions older, less frequently accessed files to Glacier Deep Archive for cost-effective storage.

answers.text: Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system to extend the company's storage space.
answers.explanation: While FSx provides a managed Windows file server, it doesn't inherently provide file lifecycle management or tiering to a lower-cost storage solution like Glacier.

answers.text: Install a utility on each user's computer to access Amazon S3. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 7 days.
answers.explanation: Installing a utility on each user's computer is not a scalable solution and adds complexity. The direct user access to S3 also bypasses the local caching mechanism offered by S3 File Gateway, which is important for low-latency access to recently accessed files. Flexible retrieval isn't needed because the access is infrequent after 7 days.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to use Amazon S3 File Gateway to extend the company's storage with S3. The gateway caches recently accessed files for low-latency access. An S3 lifecycle policy then automatically transitions files to Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days to optimize costs for infrequently accessed data.

question: A company has a publicly accessible SQL database containing movie data. The database runs on an Amazon RDS Single-AZ DB instance. A script executes queries at random intervals daily to record the number of new movies added to the database and reports a final total during business hours. The development team is experiencing inadequate database performance for development tasks while the script runs. A solutions architect needs to recommend a solution to resolve this with the LEAST operational overhead. Which solution will meet this requirement?

answers.text: Modify the DB instance to be a Multi-AZ deployment.
answers.explanation: A Multi-AZ deployment improves high availability and fault tolerance, but it does not directly address the performance issue caused by the script's read queries.

answers.text: Create a read replica of the database. Configure the script to query only the read replica.
answers.explanation: Creating a read replica and directing the script's queries to it offloads the read traffic from the primary database, resolving the performance issue with minimal operational overhead.

answers.text: Instruct the development team to manually export the entries in the database at the end of each day.
answers.explanation: Manually exporting data introduces significant operational overhead and is not a scalable or efficient solution.

answers.text: Use Amazon ElastiCache to cache the common queries that the script runs against the database.
answers.explanation: ElastiCache is useful for caching frequently accessed data. Since the script is looking for newly added movies, the data is constantly changing, making ElastiCache less effective and requiring more operational overhead to implement and manage.

overall_explanation: The correct solution is to create a read replica (Option 2). This allows the reporting script to run its queries against the read replica, isolating the workload and preventing it from impacting the performance of the primary database used for development. It requires minimal changes and offers the least operational overhead compared to the other options. Multi-AZ improves availability, manual exports are inefficient, and ElastiCache is not suitable for frequently changing data.

question: A company is migrating its on-premises containerized application to a hybrid environment using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The application must run both on- premises and in the AWS Cloud, utilizing containers for consistency and scalability. The company requires a solution that allows seamless scaling across both environments, with new application containers running in the AWS Cloud and utilizing a load balancer to manage HTTP traffic. Which combination of actions will satisfy these requirements?

answers.text: Set up an ECS cluster that uses the AWS Fargate launch type for the cloud application containers. Use an Amazon ECS Anywhere external launch type for the on-premises application containers.
answers.explanation: This option allows you to run containers in the cloud using Fargate (serverless) and extend ECS to your on-premises environment with ECS Anywhere. ECS Anywhere enables you to register your on- premises servers or VMs as part of your ECS cluster.

answers.text: Set up an Application Load Balancer for cloud ECS services.
answers.explanation: Using an Application Load Balancer is essential for distributing HTTP traffic across the ECS containers running in the cloud. It provides the necessary load balancing and traffic management capabilities for web-based applications.

answers.text: Set up a Network Load Balancer for cloud ECS services.
answers.explanation: A Network Load Balancer is more suited for TCP or UDP traffic, not HTTP traffic as specified in the requirements. Therefore, this option is not optimal.

answers.text: Set up an ECS cluster that uses the AWS Fargate launch type. Use Fargate for the cloud application containers and the on-premises application containers.
answers.explanation: Fargate cannot be directly used for on-premises environments without ECS Anywhere. Therefore, this option is not valid for the hybrid setup.

answers.text: Set up an ECS cluster that uses the Amazon EC2 launch type for the cloud application containers. Use Amazon ECS Anywhere with an AWS Fargate launch type for the on- premises application containers.
answers.explanation: Using EC2 launch type for the cloud environment is a valid option but it requires more operational overhead compared to Fargate. Also, the Fargate launch type cannot be directly used with ECS Anywhere on-premises. ECS Anywhere uses external instances registered to the ECS control plane.

overall_explanation: The correct combination includes setting up an ECS cluster with Fargate for the cloud and ECS Anywhere for on-premises to provide a scalable, hybrid, and cloud-native solution. An Application Load Balancer is needed to balance HTTP traffic across the containers running in the cloud. The combination of using Fargate and ECS Anywhere allows the customer to run the same containerized application in both environments, reducing operational overhead and ensuring consistent behavior.

question: A company is migrating its on-premises workloads, including sensitive SQL Server databases, to AWS. The company wants to enhance database security and minimize operational overhead. Which solution best meets these requirements?

answers.text: Migrate the databases to Amazon EC2 instances. Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key for encryption.
answers.explanation: While EC2 provides flexibility, it increases operational overhead as you're responsible for managing the OS, database software, patching, and backups.

answers.text: Migrate the databases to a Multi-AZ Amazon RDS for SQL Server DB instance. Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key for encryption.
answers.explanation: This option provides a managed database service (RDS) that reduces operational overhead and offers enhanced security features like encryption at rest using KMS and high availability with Multi- AZ deployment.

answers.text: Migrate the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Macie to ensure data security.
answers.explanation: S3 is object storage, not a relational database. Migrating data to S3 would require significant application changes and wouldn't meet the requirement of using a SQL Server database.

answers.text: Migrate the databases to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs to ensure data security.
answers.explanation: DynamoDB is a NoSQL database, not a relational database like SQL Server. This would require significant application changes. CloudWatch Logs is for logging and monitoring, not data security itself.

overall_explanation: Using a Multi-AZ Amazon RDS for SQL Server DB instance with KMS encryption offers the best balance between increased security (through encryption and high availability) and reduced operational overhead (through managed database services) while maintaining the existing relational database structure. EC2 requires more management overhead. S3 and DynamoDB are not suitable replacements for SQL Server without significant application changes.

question: A company wants to migrate an application to AWS and improve its availability. They also want to implement AWS WAF to protect the application. Which solution best meets these requirements?

answers.text: Create an Auto Scaling group containing multiple Amazon EC2 instances hosting the application across two Availability Zones. Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and set the Auto Scaling group as the target. Connect AWS WAF to the ALB.
answers.explanation: This solution provides high availability through the Auto Scaling group and multiple Availability Zones. AWS WAF protects the application by filtering malicious traffic at the ALB level.

answers.text: Create a cluster placement group containing multiple Amazon EC2 instances that host the application. Configure an Application Load Balancer and set the EC2 instances as the targets. Connect a WAF to the placement group.
answers.explanation: Cluster placement groups offer low latency but do not inherently provide high availability across Availability Zones. WAF cannot be directly connected to placement group.

answers.text: Create two Amazon EC2 instances hosting the application across two Availability Zones. Configure the EC2 instances as the targets of an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Connect a WAF to the ALB.
answers.explanation: While this solution uses multiple Availability Zones, it does not scale automatically and therefore doesn't maximize availability as much as an Auto Scaling group.

answers.text: Create an Auto Scaling group containing multiple Amazon EC2 instances hosting the application across two Availability Zones. Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and set the Auto Scaling group as the target. Connect a WAF to the Auto Scaling group.
answers.explanation: AWS WAF cannot be directly associated with an Auto Scaling Group. It must be associated with a supported resource such as an Application Load Balancer.

overall_explanation: The best solution is to use an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones for high availability and an Application Load Balancer (ALB) with AWS WAF attached for application protection. The WAF filters traffic before it reaches the EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling Group. The flow is: WAF -> ALB -> Auto Scaling Group (EC2 instances).

question: A company manages a data lake in an Amazon S3 bucket that numerous applications access. The S3 bucket contains a unique prefix for each application. The company wants to restrict each application to its specific prefix and to have granular control of the objects under each prefix. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.text: Create dedicated S3 access points and access point policies for each application.
answers.explanation: By creating separate access points for each application, you can enforce access controls specific to their respective prefixes while minimizing administrative complexity. This approach provides a clean separation of permissions and reduces the risk of misconfigurations. S3 Access Points provide a way to manage access to shared data sets in Amazon S3. Each access point has a unique hostname and a policy that is specific to the use case, allowing for granular control over access to data. Access Point Policies can be tailored to restrict access to specific prefixes within an S3 bucket, ensuring that each application only has access to its designated prefix.

answers.text: Create an S3 Batch Operations job to set the ACL permissions for each object in the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: S3 Batch Operations involves setting ACL permissions for each object individually, which can be cumbersome and time-consuming. Also, ACL is not recommended by AWS.

answers.text: Replicate the objects in the S3 bucket to new S3 buckets for each application. Create replication rules by prefix.
answers.explanation: Replicating objects to new S3 buckets introduces additional buckets and replication rules, increasing management overhead.

answers.text: Replicate the objects in the S3 bucket to new S3 buckets for each application. Create dedicated S3 access points for each application.
answers.explanation: This option adds unnecessary complexity by combining replication and access point creation.

overall_explanation: The most efficient solution is to create dedicated S3 access points and access point policies for each application. This approach provides granular control and restricts each application to its specific prefix with minimal operational overhead. Options B, C, and D are less efficient due to increased complexity and management overhead.

question: A company's application allows customers to upload images to an Amazon S3 bucket. Currently, a nightly Amazon EC2 Spot Fleet processes all images received that day. Each image takes 2 minutes to process and requires 512 MB of memory. A solutions architect needs to modify the application to process images immediately upon upload. Which change will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.text: Use S3 Event Notifications to write a message with image details to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure an AWS Lambda function to read the messages from the queue and to process the images.
answers.explanation: This is the most cost-effective solution. Lambda is well-suited for processing tasks under 15 minutes with sufficient memory (up to 10 GB). Using SQS ensures that all images are processed reliably.

answers.text: Use S3 Event Notifications to write a message with image details to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure an EC2 Reserved Instance to read the messages from the queue and to process the images.
answers.explanation: Reserved Instances are typically more expensive than using a Spot Fleet or Lambda for this use case, making it less cost-effective.

answers.text: Use S3 Event Notifications to publish a message with image details to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure a container instance in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to subscribe to the topic and to process the images.
answers.explanation: Container instances in ECS are generally more expensive than Lambda for this task. Also, SNS is not ideal for guaranteed message delivery compared to SQS.

answers.text: Use S3 Event Notifications to publish a message with image details to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure an AWS Elastic Beanstalk application to subscribe to the topic and to process the images.
answers.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk is generally more expensive than Lambda. Also, SNS is not ideal for guaranteed message delivery compared to SQS.

overall_explanation: The most cost-effective solution is to use S3 Event Notifications to trigger an AWS Lambda function via an SQS queue. Lambda provides a serverless, cost-efficient way to process images when they are uploaded. SQS ensures that all messages are delivered and processed, handling any potential load spikes gracefully. The image processing time of 2 minutes and memory requirement of 512MB are well within Lambda's capabilities. EC2 Reserved Instances, ECS, and Elastic Beanstalk are generally more expensive options for this on-demand, short-duration processing task. SNS also isn't the best queueing mechanism, SQS offers guaranteed delivery of messages.

question: A company wants to improve the availability and performance of its hybrid application. The application consists of a stateful TCP-based workload hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in different AWS Regions and a stateless UDP-based workload hosted on premises. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to improve availability and performance?

answers.text: Create an accelerator using AWS Global Accelerator. Add the load balancers as endpoints.
answers.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator improves application availability and performance by directing traffic to optimal endpoints over the AWS global network. It is well-suited for non-HTTP traffic like UDP.

answers.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin that uses Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to route requests to the load balancers.
answers.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is designed for HTTP/HTTPS traffic and caching content closer to users. It is not the appropriate service for TCP and UDP traffic.

answers.text: Configure two Application Load Balancers in each Region. The first will route to the EC2 endpoints, and the second will route to the on-premises endpoints.
